Mueller and is an ordained Lutheran pastor.

Mary Keller was born on May 28, 1934, and married Richard Wojick. Now she is
married to John Little. She has two sons, Paul and John Wojick.

Gideon & Pauline (Blotter) Ketterling

Gideon Ketterling was born March 22, 1909, at Zeeland, N.D. to George and
Katherine (Wolf) Ketterling where he grew up on his parent's farm. He attended
rural school.

He moved to a farm near Mercer, N.D., in 1930. Two years later he moved to farm
near Benedict, N.D.

They purchased the Rudolph Reinish farm 12 miles northeast of Mercer in 1935
where they made their home. They raised their family of four girls, Gloris,
Janice, Marliss and Joyce and one son, Roger. They farmed and milked cows,
raised pigs, chickens, ducks and geese.

Gideon had a threshing machine and threshed for all the neighbors, and Pauline
helped the ladies prepare the meals until the threshing was done.

        Photo: The Gideon Ketterling family: (front, from left) Gideon, Joyce,
        Pauline; (back) Janice, Roger, Gloris and Marliss.

In 1970, they sold their farm to their son Roger and his wife Dayle. Gideon and
Pauline purchased the Chapman house on Main Street in Turtle Lake. Gideon did
carpentry work and remodeled homes for people. Gideon also worked as a
taxidermist. He mounted many animals and birds. The room was completely
surrounded by shelves with sliding glass doors for display to the many people
who came to see his collection. Gideon's collection of taxidermy is on display
at the McLean County Historical Museum in Washburn.

He also loved to work with wood and made many beautiful baskets for family and
friends. He also carved many sets of cranes for family and friends.

Pauline had a large garden and preserved her fruits and vegetables for her
family's enjoyment during the cold winters. Pauline was accomplished at
crocheting. She crocheted many doilies for her children and grandchildren. She
was also an avid quilter and made many hand stitched quilts for her children and
grandchildren.

They had five children:

Gloris married Mervyn Singer (deceased) and they had two children, Terry
(deceased) and Brian (deceased). Gloris is now living near Turtle Lake.

Janice married Arthur Geigel (deceased) and they had five children: Cheryl,
Cheryn, Curtis, Charles and Cheryi. Janice lives in Turtle Lake, N.D.

Marliss married Orville Olson (deceased). They had four children: Shelly,
Heather, Eric and Michael.

Roger married Dayle Meadows and they had three children: Tamara, Tracy and Todd.

Joyce (deceased) married Edward Huesers. They had two children, Nicole and
Patrick. She then married Harlan Goerger and they had one child, Elyzabeth.

Pauline and Gideon had 17 grandchildren. In September of 1983 they celebrated
their 50th wedding anniversary with family and friends.

They were active members of St. John's Lutheran Church, rural Turtle Lake until
it closed in 1980. They transferred to Trinity Lutheran Church in Turtle Lake.

Gideon entered into eternal rest on May 30, 1988, and Pauline entered into her
heavenly home on Nov. 15, 1994.

Johannes Valentin (John) & Olga Fehlau (Jacob) Ketterling

John was born on June 8, 1871, in Kassel, Cherson, in South Russia and was
baptized in the Kassel Lutheran Church. He was confirmed in the Lutheran Church
in Freeman, S.D. He died on Jan. 5, 1941, in the St. Alexius Hospital in
Bismarck, N.D. The funeral was on Jan. 8, 1941, in the Hope Lutheran Church in
Mercer. He was one of the charter members. He is buried in the Mercer Cemetery.

        Photo: Olga and John Ketterling

He came to the United States with his family at the age of 13 on April 28, 1885,
and lived in Hutchinson County, Dakota Territory until 1890 when the family
moved to Edmunds County, S.D. where the family homesteaded one and one-half
miles west of Bowdle. He worked on the family farm and at the Bowdle Four Mill.

        Photo: John Ketterling with his children, Ida and Richard.

He married Amalia Olga Fehlau Jacob on Feb. 11, 1896, in Bowdle, S.D. She was
born on Oct. 26, 1871, in Gombin (Gabin) Poland to German immigrant parents,
Henrich and Emilie Preiss Fehlau. She was married to Joseph Jacob in 1891 in
Poland and he died soon after their marriage. In 1893, she came to the United
States and to Bowdle to live with her widower brother, the Rev. T. Richard
Fehlau, a pioneer missionary pastor in the area. She died on Aug. 30, 1939, in
Trinity Hospital in Minot. The funeral was on Sept. 1, 1939, (the day Hitler
invaded her homeland of Poland) in Hope Lutheran Church in Mercer. She is buried
in the Mercer Cemetery.

        Photo: Granddaughters of John and Olga Ketterling: (front, from left)
        Lyvian and Vicky Winklemann; (back) LaRose Ketterling and Florence
        Winklemann.

After their marriage, John and Olga lived on a farm on the Walworth/Edmunds
County line in South Dakota. In April of 1906, they moved to the new village of
Mercer and lived there the rest of their lives. John operated an outlet of the
Bowdle Flour Mill until the 1930s. He was foreman of the WPA in McLean County
during the Depression days. He had a cream station in Mercer until his
retirement. He was active in the community and township activities and was one
of the first members of Mercer School District, serving as treasurer. He played
the cornet in the first Mercer City Band. He was a charter member of two German
Lutheran Churches in Mercer, the St. Paulus (Braun Church) which was located
four and one-half miles northwest of Mercer and of the Hope Lutheran Church. He
was treasurer of the Hope Lutheran Church until shortly before his death. He
owned and operated a "launch" on Brush Lake for many years. He and his son,
Richard, operated a silent movie machine and showed movies in the area. The
machine is now in the North Dakota Historical Museum in Bismarck. The family
also had a threshing rig, which they operated in the area.

Throughout her lifetime, Olga was an active member of her church and was the
writer of the constitution and bylaws of Hope Lutheran Church. She was not a
charter member because women were not voting members of the church. She was
called upon to do "care of the dead" and the most notable one was for the
members of the murdered Wolff family in rural Turtle Lake in April of 1920.

John and Olga had three children:

Richard Edward born on April 15, 1900.

Ida born on Oct. 1, 1901, married Victor Winklemann.

Infant daughter who died at birth.

They had five granddaughters:

LaRose and Loretta Ketterling, Loretta was born and died in 1935. Lyvian,
Victoria, and Florence Winklemann.

Richard Edward & Bertha (Obenauer) Ketterling

Richard Edward was the son of John and Olga Fehlau Jacob Ketterling. He was born
on April 15, 1900, on the Ketterling homestead in Bowdle Township, South Dakota.
He was baptized on May 20, 1900, in Bowdle and confirmed in the St. Paulus
Lutheran Church, rural Mercer in 1915. He was a member of the first class taught
in the Mercer school and completed the eighth grade in 1915. He was active in
music and for years was a member of a local dance band. He also was a member of
quartets and choirs. He attended two trade schools in Fargo, steam engine
operation at NDAC (now NDSU) and the Molar Barber School.

        Photo: Richard Ketterling

        Photo: Bertha Ketterling

Occupations during his lifetime were laborer, barber, mechanic and a grain
elevator manager in Mercer, Dunseith and Falkirk, all in North Dakota. He was a
big equipment operator during the building of the Garrison Dam. He owned and
operated a barbershop in Denhoff, Ruso and Benedict, N.D. He was the custodian
of the Mercer School and worked for the WPA and was the second man for Andrew's
Grain Elevator in Mercer before transferring to manage the Andrew's Grain
Elevator, later Peavey in Dunseith in 1942. At the time of his death, he was a
bookkeeper for the North Dakota State Highway Department in Valley City, N.D. He
was a fixer-upper and could fix or mend anything.

        Photo: LaRose and Loretta Ketterling

He died on May 10, 1969, in Valley City and funeral services were held in the
Peterson-Olson Funeral Chapel in Valley City and in Our Savior's Lutheran Church
in Mercer. Burial was in the Mercer Cemetery.

Richard married Bertha Obenauer on Jan. 18, 1927, in Jamestown, N.D. She was the
daughter of Friedrich and Karolina Sackmann Obenauer of Java and Eureka, S.D.
Bertha was born on Feb. 21, 1900, in rural Walworth County, S.D. She attended
rural school and completed a dressmaking course in Aberdeen, S.D. She came to
Mercer in the fall of 1926 as a dressmaker and lived with her aunt, Margaretha
Degg. She was a clerk in the Dakovna Store. She suffered a stroke a week before
her 83rd birthday and was a resident of the Good Samaritan Home in Larimore,
N.D. at the time of her death on Feb. 23, 1988. The funeral was in Our Savior's
Lutheran Church in Mercer and burial was in the Mercer Cemetery.

Richard and Bertha had two daughters:

LaRose Margie born on May 12, 1928, in Denhoff.

Loretta Jean born on April 8, 1935, in Mercer and died Aug. 8, 1935. She is
buried in the Mercer Cemetery beside her grandparents.

LaRose graduated from the Dunseith High School, the University of North Dakota
and completed a dietetic internship at the Good Samaritan Medical Center in
Portland, Ore. She earned a MS degree at the Northern Illinois University and
did postmaster's studies at the University of South Dakota. She is a retired
registered dietitian and a licensed registered dietitian in North Dakota. She
was a member of the first Board of Dietetic Practice in North Dakota. She
received numerous professional awards and in 1987, she was named the Outstanding
Dietitian in North Dakota.

Her professional career was as a Nutrition Educator in schools of nursing at
Trinity Hospital in Minot, Rochester Methodist and St. Mary's, both in
Rochester, Minn., the College of St. Teresa in Winona, Minn. and Loyola
University in Chicago.

She was the Director of the Dietetic Education programs at South Dakota State
University in Brookings and the University of North Dakota, Grand Forks. She has
134 "dietetic children."

She was a clinical (medical) dietitian at the Bismarck Hospital (Medcenter One),
Trinity Hospital in Minot, Mayo Clinic-St. Mary's Hospital in Rochester, Minn.
and the Nebraska Methodist Hospital in Omaha, Neb.

She was an administrator for the American Dietetic Association and the National
Dairy Council, both in Chicago.

She is a translator of German to English and is active in the Germans from
Russia Heritage Society. Music is an important part of her life. She played the
organ for church services in the Hope Lutheran Church in Mercer at the age of 11
and continues to participate in music activities.

Rev. Reinhold & Lillian (Little Soldier) Klaudt

Lillian Little Soldier was born June 29, 1906. Her father was Clarence Little
Soldier and her mother was Wilena Little Soldier. Lillian was one of the
Arickara-Mandan tribe from the Elbowoods, North Dakota area. At birth Lillian
was given the name, White Corn Little Soldier. Both her grandfathers, Soldier
and One Feather, were Custer scouts at the Battle of the Little Big Horn. Her
dad being small of stature was named Little Soldier. Lillian's generation was
the first generation that had family names. It is now in its fourth generation.

Lillian was converted to the White Man's God at a very young age as a result of
the Indian Mission work being established on her Reservation in 1876. Her
mother, Wilena Little Soldier, was a charter member of that mission work and
Lillian received all her musical training as result of this mission on Fort
Berthold.

Lillian's father, Little Soldier, was in the horse trading business. He
furnished horses for other Indians and the U.S. Cavalry at that time and also
furnished horses for the cattlemen in the Dakotas and Montana. Lillian, being a
petite Indian girl, was his jockey. She rode her father's horses for shows.

Lillian met Reinhold Klaudt, a young farmer who lived nearby. She invited him
and his family, Gottlieb and Katharine Klaudt, to their mission whereupon
Reinhold Klaudt and several of his immediate family accepted the White Man's
God.

Lillian and Reinhold were married in 1929. Lillian's father was killed in an
automobile accident in September of 1921. Her mother remained a widow for the
rest of her life, performed a heroic job in raising the seven children by
herself.

At one time, Lillian and Reinhold lived in Mercer and they began to answer
ministerial calls around the area. On Saturday nights they would go uptown on
the corner of a street to sing and preach. Lillian had a beautiful voice and
would play the guitar and accordion while Reinhold would play the banjo. The
Klaudt family traveled as a group for over 50 years. Their marriage lasted 72
years and five children: Vernon, Ramona, Melvin, Raymond and Kenneth. As the
Klaudt children grew in age, they were added to the ministry and later on
grandchildren were added. Before retiring in the late 1970s, they were one of
the most popular gospel singing groups in the nation. Lillian received special
recognition from the U.S. President and rubbed shoulders with the elite of this
world. The Klaudt Indian Family made their home in Doraville, Georgia.

Lillian passed away on March 3, 2001, and Reinhold passed away on July 5, 2001.

        Photo: The Klaudt Family musical group.

Jessie & Sarah (Eckert) Klein

Jessie (Shorty) Klein was born in 1886 in Ireland. He settled in McLean County
in 1906 and married Sarah Eckert.

Jessie operated a pool hall and lunchroom in early Mercer. Read more about

Balthaser & Katharina (Hofer) Kleingartner

Balthaser Kleingartner, son of Balthaser and Luise (Walz) Kleingartner was born
on the Oct. 7, 1887, in Kloestitz, South Russia. He immigrated to North Dakota
on May 22, 1903, with his parents. They homesteaded south of the Mercer
community.

He lived with his parents until March 26, 1911, when he married Katharina Hofer.

Katharina Hofer was born July 23, 1891, to John and Christina (Laib) Hofer. Her
father, John Hofer, died Dec. 13, 1904 in South Russia. Her mother, Christina
married Adolph Engelhardt on Dec. 11, 1905. They immigrated to North Dakota in
1906 to the Garrison, N.D. area.

        Photo: Katharina and Balthaser Kleingartner

After their marriage Balthaser and Katharina lived on a farm northwest of
Mercer. In the summer of 1914 they took up a homestead in Montana and moved
there in March of 1915. They returned on Nov. 4, 1918, to a farm three miles
northwest of Turtle Lake where they lived for 10 months. In February of 1919,
they bought land two miles north of Mercer where they built their home.

They lived there until 1947 when they moved to McClusky, N.D. Balthaser died
Sept. 13, 1973. Katharina died Sept. 6, 1977.

Their children were:

Louise, born Dec. 18, 1911, married Carl Rennich, Sept. 25, 1929, and died Aug.
15, 1976. They had four children: Meinhardt (died in Korea in 1951); Mervin,
Douglas (died in 1998) and Joan.

Hilda, born Aug. 8, 1918, married John Pool, died in 1990. They had one child,
Carol.

Berthold, born Aug. 30, 1923, married Ardith Leedy, Oct. 31, 1946, died Oct.31,
2001. They had three children: Tim, Tom and Terry.

Laura, born Sept. 13, 1926, married Harold Hepper, July 9, 1947. They had two
children: Debra and Gail.

Ervin, born Feb. 25, 1930, married Alice Heer, May 5, 1954. They had five
children: Charles, Sandra, Michael, Kimberly and Mitchell.

        Photo: Balthaser and Luise Kleingartner

Balthaser & Luise (Walz) Kleingartner

Balthaser Kleingartner, Sr., the son of Christian and Katharina (Singer)
Kleingartner, was born May 18, 1853, in Hoffnungstal, Bessarabia, South Russia.
He and Luise Walz were joined in marriage in Kloestitz, Bessarabia on Feb. 7,
1880. Luise, the daughter of Peter and Karolina (Boerkirchert) Walz was born on
Nov. 12, 1854, in Neudorf, South Russia. Balthaser died Jan. 30, 1923, in Mercer
and Luise died Dec. 6, 1946, in Mercer.

They and six of their eight children immigrated to North Dakota from
Hoffnungstal, Bessarabia in 1903 via Canada. Balthaser and Luise settled on land
five and one-half miles south and one and one-half miles west of Mercer in
section 4 of Park Township. Here they farmed and raised their family.

Katharina was born July 18, 1880, and married Adolf Schott and died Feb. 26,

Berthold & Ardith (Leedy)  Kleingartner

Berthold (Bert) Kleingartner was born Aug. 30, 1923, on the family farm north of
Mercer, son of Balthaser and Katharina.

He attended rural school (my-oh-my stories he told). An era before the school
bus meant walking into Mercer for the four years of high school. He loved sports
and played on the basketball team.

Bert married Ardith Leedy in 1946 and they made their home on the family farm.
Bert farmed until he was stricken with polio. This affliction ended his farming
and he pursued a new vocation.

He and his family moved to Bismarck and he was employed at Consolidated
Freightways and the City of Bismarck Water Department and retired as manager of
Commercial Printing. In his spare time he started a saw sharpening business
which was active for many years.

Bert enjoyed hunting and fishing, crossword puzzles and reading. He enjoyed
visiting with friends and just about anyone that was around.

Retirement years were spent living seven miles west of McClusky during the
summer months and in Arizona in the winter. Bert died in October of 2001.

They have three sons, Timothy, Thomas (wife Nyla) and Terrance.

Albert Sr. & Joy (Harrum) Kline

Joy Harrum, daughter of Laurence and Abby Harrum, was born on Oct. 28, 1912.
Albert Kline, son of Frederick and Emelia Renke Kline, was born on July 20,
1913. They both graduated from the Mercer High School. They were married in June
of 1939. Albert and Joy had four children.

Susan graduated from Mercer High School and nursing school. She is married to
John Sullivan and has two children, five grandchildren and one great-grandchild.
She lives in Great Falls, Mont.

Albert Jr. graduated from the Mercer High School. He is married to Gay and they
have five sons and three grandchildren. They live in Mandan.

Jill graduated from the Flasher, N.D. High School, Bismarck State College,
Dickinson State University and the Rowan University in Glassboro, New Jersey.
She is married to Paul Farms and they have two daughters and two grandchildren.
They live in Berlin, New Jersey. Celeste is a retired teacher.

The following are Joy's early memories of life in Mercer as written in the 1979
McLean County Heritage book:

"All I remember about the first grade is the fact that I had to stand in the
corner once and that we all had the influenza which left me so delicate that my
mother had me come home for a glass of milk and cookie each recess. My friend
Aileen Rice walked along with me. We passed Ketterlings' Flour Mill and
Singer's Livery Stable on the way back and forth. Their geese chased us.
Everyone had cows, horses, chickens and other fowl, plus gardens and even pigs
to help feed the family good foods. In winter we skied, skated and studied. In
summer we rode horseback, swam in Brush Lake, picked Juneberries and
chokecherries at Howell Lake. We attended Sunday School at the school and in
1929 Our Savior's Lutheran Church was built, so every Thursday night my future
husband and I walked to Ole Hjelles' to choir practice, our lives centered
around school and church, same as our children's did in later years.

I played on the girls' basketball team. We played three-court girls' rules then,
with six players on each team, a jumping center, side center, two guards. I
played forward position. I can still remember the first basket I made in
competition. We were playing Coleharbor in our old school gym. However, after my
sophomore year there was no more basketball for girls in McLean County, but we
had glee club and county music contests.

I graduated from Mercer High School in May of 1930 as salutatorian at age 17 and
went immediately to Minot State College for a quarter (three months) to get my
second grade elementary teaching certificate. I worked for my room and board,
and at that time Minot was so far away I could only get home one time for the
fourth of July. (My daughter Susan came home from Minot State College every
week.)

My parents retired from nursing and barbering in 1930 and went to live on the
Harrum farm at Valley Spring, S.D., and I was very lonely teaching school in the
country. Some years I had to stay at the schoolhouse with no radio, no
electricity, only the kerosene lamp, the lignite coal heater to keep in fuel and
me. The horses that gathered in the lea of the wind, in the cold, at night
stamped and fought and kept me awake so I read until the wee hours. I was always
glad when my pupils came in the morning.

Albert played on the Legion Baseball team and helped build the Brush Lake golf
course (Oh, yes, we had a golf course way back then!). Albert's mother was an
excellent golfer. Later Albert became the great basketball player all four years
in Mercer High School and sang in all the music festivals. He graduated in 1932
and won an athletic scholarship to Luther College, Decorah, Iowa, but was unable
to take advantage of it in those 30s.

Albert went to Aberdeen, S.D. and to Minneapolis to work for his sister, Ruby
Bambury. Later he and his brother Harry ran the Mercer Café. In 1939 we were
married and settled down in Mercer. In May of 1940, Susan Joy was born and
Albert Donald Jr. was born in July of 1941.

        Photo: Albert D. Kline family in 1968: (front, from left) Susan,
        Celeste, Jill (back) Albert, Jr., Joy and Albert Kline, Sr.

1942 saw us on our way to Portland, Ore., where Albert worked in the shipyards
for the Oregon Shipbuilding Corporation. He won a citation as one of the workers
who volunteered and worked six weeks with no days off, which resulted in the
building in of the greatest number of Liberty Ships in the shortest period of
time in the history of shipbuilding.

We sold our home in Portland and came back to Mercer the fall of 1944, Joy to
teach and Albert to help in the elevator weighing grain and selling lumber with
his brother Archie (just to help out for a few days when his dad died in March)
and ended up staying for 12 years. He was a member of the McClusky baseball
team, a Boy Scout leader, a member of the Lutheran Brotherhood of the church and
an eight-year member of the town board. Jill Adaire as born in October, 1945,
and Celeste Yvonne in April, 1947 This completed our family."

Joy belonged to the Lutheran Ladies Aid, the Homemakers Club, was a member of
the Mercer Women's Study Club for 20 years, as well as a Campfire Girls leader,
County Democratic Party and delegate to the state Democratic convention, clerked
the elections regularly and was a correspondent for the Washburn Leader for
several years.

Albert went to work for Sweetheart Bakery in Minot in 1957. Joy went back to
Minot State College and graduated in 1963 and went back to teaching. Albert went
to work for the State Highway Department. Albert died in 1992.

Archie & Pearl (Lockrem) Kline

Archie Kline was born on April 7, 1911, in Max, the son of Ferdinand and Emelia
Kline. He was raised in Max and the family moved to Mercer where he graduated
from Mercer High School in 1931.

He joined the CCC and was in Watford City, N.D. He and his brother Albert
managed the Peavey Elevator in Mercer until 1962 when he moved to Minot and
worked as a salesman for Main Motors. He retired from the Ryan Chevrolet Company
in 1973.

        Photo: Archie Kline

He married Pearl Lockrem on July 28, 1940. She is the daughter of Chris and Gena
Lockrem. They had two children, Murray and Arlette.

Archie was active in the National Rifle Association and the ducks Unlimited. He
was a North Dakota state checkers champion.

Archie died on Dec. 24, 1999, and is buried in the Max City Cemetery.

Harry & Jesse (Claunts) Kline

Harry Kline was born on June 29, 1909, in Max, N.D., the son of Ferdinand and
Emelia Kline. He was raised and educated in Max and Mercer. He joined the CCC in
1933.

He married Jessie Claunts on May 25, 1935, in Benton, Arkansas. They lived in
Mercer until World War II. Harry worked in the shipyards in Seattle. After the
war, they returned to Mercer where they had a boarding and rooming house in the
Mercer Hotel.

Harry operated Harry's Bar in Mercer until 1954 when they moved to Bismarck.

Jessie died in 1956 and is buried in the Mercer cemetery. Harry married Ann
Senger in 1959. Harry died on November 22, 1986, in Bismarck and is buried in
the Mercer cemetery.

Harry and Jessie had two sons, Frederick (Fritzie) and Charles.

Edwin & Elizabeth (Bauer) Laib

Edwin Laib was born Feb. 10, 1917, to Friedrich Laib and Karolina (Kleingartner)
Laib at Mercer, N.D. He was raised and educated on a farm five miles south and
about two miles west of Mercer. On Oct. 26, 1939, he married Elizabeth Bauer who
was born on June 24, 1918 to William and Magdalena (Wanner) Bauer of Mercer. She
was raised on a farm southwest of Mercer, just two miles away from where Edwin
lived and met him when he worked in the field with threshing. The Laib family
went to visit the Bauer family one-day when Elizabeth gave Edwin a picture of
herself and Edwin decided to ask her for a date. That was the beginning for
building a life together!

        Photo: Elizabeth and Edwin Laib, taken July 4, 1939, at Brush Lake.

They made their first home together after marriage on a farm south of
Pickarville, N.D., six miles east of Mercer and six miles south, where their
first child, a boy named Ronald John Laib, was born on Aug. 4, 1941. They lived
there and farmed for four years until October of 1943 when they moved to a farm
12 miles south of Mercer and lived there for twenty-two years. While living
there, four daughters were born.

The firstborn girl, Darlene Diane Laib, was born Nov. 23, 1943. Next came the
second girl, Arlis Elaine Laib, born on March 14, 1945. While there was plenty
of farmwork to do and Edwin could have used more boys to help with the work,
fate had it that more girls were going to be born. Verdeen Ardell Laib was born
on Aug. 31, 1946, when a year and a half later, Marilyn Jean Laib was born Feb.
24, 1948. So there was lots of farm help, but it took the four girls to work
with only one boy and Elizabeth also had to help with outdoor work.

One day while driving the tractor about six weeks after Marilyn was born, the
tractor overturned and Elizabeth was pinned underneath. With prayers being said
and the power of God, Edwin was able to lift the tractor enough to get Elizabeth
out. She had to be hospitalized with a fractured back and pelvis for several
weeks, so Edwin and her were thankful to have good neighbors and relatives to
take care of all the children. In 1957 a sewer was dug and running water
supplied to the house. How good it was not to have to go out in the cold to get
water from the well or have to use the outhouse!

        Photo: The Laib family in 1976: (front, from left) Byron, Elizabeth,
        Edwin, Ronald; (back) Marilyn, Verdeen, Arlis and Darlene.

        Photo: Elizabeth and Edwin Laib, 1991.

By the grace of God, nine years after the last girl was born, another boy, Byron
Dean Laib, was born on July 10, 1957. He was extremely admired by parents and
siblings alike! He had all of the older girls to help take care of him along
with an older happy brother!

Edwin and Elizabeth were members of a small country church, Zion Lutheran
Church, which was about seven miles south of Mercer. They were active in the
parish where Elizabeth would sometimes play the piano and Edwin served on the
parish council and was a Sunday school superintendent. They were adamant in
raising their family in the Christian faith having family devotions every
morning in their home and seeing that all the children were confirmed.

In August of 1965, after having some hard and drought years of farming, and the
children growing up leaving the farm for college, work or marriage, Edwin and
Elizabeth decided to try city life and moved to Bismarck. Edwin worked at
several jobs finding that is just wasn't the same or as good as farm life. With
Byron, young and at home yet, he decided to buy another farm in April of 1969,
which was seven miles south of Bagley, Minn. In December of 1977, Byron died of
cancer at the age of 20. The next fall in October of 1978, Edwin and Elizabeth
sold and moved off the farm to Carrington, N.D. and lived there for over four
years, then moved back to Bismarck to be closer to their family and live out
retirement.

Edwin and Elizabeth had six children:

Ronald John Laib married Sue Carroll, had a family and was killed in a plane
accident in March of 1997.

Darlene Diane Laib married Jim Rivers and lives in Pocatello, Idaho.

Arlis Elaine Laib married Gerald Tweeten and lives on a farm by Turtle Lake.

Verdeen Ardell Laib married Dennis Schlafmann and lives on a farm north of Wing,
N.D.

Marilyn Jean Laib married Jim Geiger and lives in Bismarck.

Byron Dean Laib died in 1977 at the age of 20 years.

Emanuel & Frieda (Kurle) Laib

Emanuel Laib was born Oct. 19, 1909, the sixth child of Frederick Laib and
Karolina (Kleingartner) Laib. He was raised on his parent's farm south of
Mercer, N.D. and attended rural school. He farmed with is father until Nov. 17,
1932, when he married Frieda Kurle, born Sept 10, 1914. They moved to a farm
south of Pickardville, N.D. where they farmed and ranched.

        Photo: Frieda and Emanuel Liab on their 50th wedding anniversary in
        1964.

In October of 1944, they moved on Emanuel Laib's parent's farm south of Mercer
where they farmed and raised their children. In 1973 they retired and moved to
Mercer. They have six children, 16 grandchildren and 28 grandchildren as of
March of 2003.

Mervin Walter Laib was born Jan. 1, 1933, and died April 23, 1933.

Elmer Laib was born Aug. 21, 1935. On Nov. 23, 1955, he married Odiela Mertz,
born Sept. 19, 1935. They farm and own The R & H Motel in McClusky. They have
six children: LaVern, Sheryl, Steven, Elliot, Virgil and Lynette.

Luella Laib was born May 30, 1939, and was married to Marvin Hausauer and after
his death, she married Marty Anderson. Luella has two sons: Carlyle and Craig.

Melvin Laib was born Jan. 3, 1941, and was married to Ivy Bye and is now married
to Michelle Essick. They have thee children: Tonya, Timothy and Cheri.

Allan Laib was born April 8, 1943. On Feb. 4, 1967, he married Marjorie Johs
born Dec. 1, 1944. They now live on the family farm and have five children:
Sheila, Stephanie, Stacy, Sheldon and Scott.

Larry Laib was born Nov. 1, 1946, and died Nov. 17, 1946.

Emanuel Laib passed away Sept. 30, 1995, and Frieda (Kurle) Laib died in 2003.

Fred & Martha (Schlafman) Laib

Fred Laib was born April 14, 1905, to Friedrich Laib and Karolina (Kleingartner)
Laib in Mercer, N.D. He was raised on the farm five miles south and two miles
west and a ½ mile south of Mercer and received his education in a country school
located one mile west of the farm.

On Oct. 8, 1925, he married Martha Schlafman, born Nov. 7, 1906, to Karl
Schlafman and Kathrina (Wagner) Schlafman, on a farm 14 miles south of Mercer.
Her parents died when Martha was very young so she lived with her grandparents,
William and Kathrina (Metzer) Wagner and started her education in Washburn, N.D.
Shortly after she went to live with her aunt and uncle, John and Elizabeth
(Wagner) Reuer. They moved to Bowdle, S.D., on a farm, where she finished her
education. In 1919 they moved to a farm five miles south and three miles west
and two miles south of Mercer.

        Photo: The Fred Laib family: (front, from left) Willie, Martha, Fred,
        LeRoy; (back) Marion, Meinhart and Eileen.

Fred and Martha lived with Fred's parents after their marriage through the
winter months. In the spring they bought their own place from Christ Singer,
which was located five miles south, 2½ miles west and ½ mile north of Mercer.
Two years later they moved to the farm ½ mile west.

In addition to farming, Fred helped his brother-in-law, Clarence Gilbertson,
build an eight-room house in 1925, and in 1928 they built a barn. This education
helped Fred in later years when he worked on his own house.

Fred also had an interest in automobiles and every chance he had he would stop
and watch Christ Heim repair cars. This helped Fred when he overhauled tractors
during the winter.

Fred and Martha farmed until their retirement in 1969. In 1971 they had a house
built in Mercer at 203 West Wing St. In 1991 Martha sold their house to their
son, Leroy.

Fred and Martha were members of Zion Lutheran Church, located seven miles south
and one mile west of Mercer.

Fred died March 19, 1982, and Martha died May 22, 1999. They are both buried in
Zion Lutheran Cemetery seven miles south and one mile west of Mercer.

Fred and Martha had six children: Meinhart Walter, Loretta, LeRoy, Wilbert
Eugene, Eileen Violet and Marion Delores.

Friedich & Karolina (Kleingartner) & Fredericka (Aldinger) Laib

Friedich (Fred) Laib was born Dec. 29, 1878, at Hoffnungstal, Bessarabia,
Russia, to Georg Laib and Christina (Weishaar) Laib. He was raised in
Hoffnungstal and married Karolina Kleingartner on Oct. 15, 1899. Karolina was
the daughter of Balzer Kleingartner and Louise (Walz) Kleingartner and was born
Oct. 1, 1882.

They were married for two and one-half years when they and Friedich Laib's
parents decided to come to America. At the time Friedrich and Karolina had one
child, Emilia Laib. They received their passports on March 28, 1902, at
Hoffnungstal. They then took most of their belongings and traveled by train to
Bremen, Germany, and left the port on April 22, 1902, on board the ship
"Kronprinz Wilhelm." They arrived on April 29, 1902, at Ellis Island, New York,
from there they went by train to Friedrich's Uncle Andreas Laib at Bowdle, S.D.
From there they traveled to Mercer. On June 24, 1902, they filed for citizenship
at Washburn, N.D. and they became citizens on Dec. 10, 1907.

On Sept. 5, 1902, Friedrich (Fred) paid a $10 fee to file his homestead. Claim
number 11613 in Park Township Sec. 4 NW¼ lots 3 & 4 145N 79W. He got his title
(deed) on Dec. 19, 1907. On Oct. 23, 1914, he bought Claim number 11612, SW¼ of
Sec. 4 in Park Township.

Friedrich built a sod house and barn. The winters were bad with lots of snow and
cold weather. The supplies had to be purchased from Underwood, which took many
days to accomplish. In 1925 Friedrich built an eight-room house and in 1928 he
built a big barn. The house is still on the homestead, which is now owned by
Allan Laib, son of Emanuel Laib, which is the third generation owner.

Karolina died on Jan. 17, 1941, in the Bismarck Hospital. This left Friedrich
with some children still at home.

        Photo: Fred with Magdalena and Karolina with Fred Jr., Emilia in back.

Friedrich remarried on June 25, 1942, to Fredricka (Weisshaar) Aldinger. They
retired in 1943 and moved to 405 N 11th St. in Bismarck. Friedrich (Fred) Laib
passed away on April 24, 1955, and Fredricka (Aldinger) Laib got pneumonia and
passed away 24 hours before Friedrich (Fred).

Friedrich (Fred) Laib and Karolina (Kleingartner) Laib had a large family:

Emilia married Carl Schlafman, Magdalena married John Blotter, Fred Jr. married
Martha Schlafman, Adolph married Carolina Kurle, Emanuel married Frieda Kurle,
Otto married Louise Heinle, Louise married Edward Kurle, Olga married Walter
Flemmer, Edwin married Elizabeth Bauer, Elsie married Carl Littke, John married
Lorraine Neumiller, Ella married William Berg, Arthur married Alvina Klein.

At the present time, there are seven descendants still living in the Mercer
area:

Allan Laib and his wife, Marge. He is the son of Emanuel.

Carlyle Hausauer and his wife, Debbie, and their daughter, Courtney. Carlyle is
the grandson of Emanuel.

Calvin Laib is the son of Otto.

Ervin and Eileen (Laib) Schell. She is the daughter of Fred Jr.

Gordon Schell is the son of Eileen (Laib) and the grandson of Fred Jr.

Lloyd and Marion (Laib) Heib. She is the daughter of Fred Jr.

LeRoy Laib, the son of Fred Jr.

        Photo: The Friedich and Karolina Laib family: (front, from left) Otto,
        Edwin, Friedrch, Karolina, Art, Adolph, Emanuel; (back) Fred Jr.,
        Magdalena, Louise, Ella, Olga, Elsie, Emelia and John.

Georg & Christina (Weishaar) Laib

Georg Laib was born Oct. 19, 1857, at Hoffnungstal, Bessarabia, Russia, to
Ludwig and Magdalena (Naasz) Laib. He was raised in Hoffnungstal and on Nov. 4,
1877, at Kloestitz, Bessarabia, Russia, he married Christina Weishaar born Aug.
25, 1864. They had nine children in Russia. Georg Laib Jr. died (infant),
Friedrich Laib, Johann Laib, Christina Laib died (infant), Adam Laib died
(infant), Paulina Laib, Magdalena Laib, Reinhold Laib died (infant), Jakob Laib.

        Photo: Georg Laib

        Photo: Christina Laib

They came to America April 29, 1902, with all their children. Friedrich Laib
married Karolina Kleingartner; Johann Laib married Bertha Rossmann, Paulina Laib
at the age of 15, Magdalena Laib at the age of 12 and Jacob at the age of six.
After arriving at Ellis Island, New York, they took the train to Bowdle, S.D.,
to Georg's brother Andreas Laib. From there they traveled by covered wagon to
south of Mercer where they homesteaded.

On June 16, 1918, Georg died quite unexpectedly as a result of blood poisoning.
The doctor had lanced a very bad boil that had developed on his back. Shortly
after the treatment blood poisoning set in and death was sudden. Christina then
lived with her daughter, Magdalena (Laib) Schell, and in 1921 she married
Heinrich Pfaff and moved to Arena, N.D. Christina died May 25, 1926. In 1936,
she was moved from the Arena area cemetery to the cemetery south of Mercer at
the Lutheran Church beside her first husband Georg Laib.

Jacob & Emelia (Herman) Laib

Jacob Laib was born in April, 1896, at Hoffnungstal, Bessarabia, Russia, to
Georg and Christina (Weishaar) Laib. In 1902 he came to America with his
parents and farmed southwest of Mercer.

In November of 1914, Jacob married Emelia Herman, born Sept. 1, 1894, to Mr. and
Mrs. Jacob Herman in Russia. She came to America as a young girl, settling in
the Mercer area. They farmed south and west of Mercer and they had three
children:

Lillian Laib married John B. Mills.

Lydia Laib married Alexander Harvey. Lydia had one son, Alexander Harvey Jr.

George Laib married Frances Thersa Hentz. George had five children:

Doyle Laib married Ellen Suzie DeWall; Dale Laib; Mary Ann Laib married to
Richard DeWall; Duane Laib; Ronald Laib.

Emelia passed away May 23 1972, and Jacob passed away June 24, 1981.

        Photo: Emelia and Jacob Laib, June 13, 1948.

Johann (John) & Bertha (Rossmann) Laib

Johann Laib was born Oct. 20, 1881, at Hoffnungstal, Bessarabia, Russia to
George Laib and Christina (Weishaar) Laib. He grew up in Hoffnungstal and
married Bertha Rossmann, born on Sept. 2, 1879, at Hoffnungstal, Bessarabia,
Russia.

They were married March 6, 1902, at Hoffnungstal. On April 22, 1902, they left
port for America with Johann's parents and his brother and sisters. They came
through Ellis Island and took the train to Bowdle, S.D. to Johann's Uncle Andrew
Laib's homestead and from there they got a wagons and horses and traveled to
North Dakota.

Johann and Bertha made their home south of Mercer between his brother Fredrick's
homestead and Baltsar Kleingartner's homestead. They farmed until 1914 when they
moved about two miles east of Arena, N.D. They farmed there until about 1926
when they moved to Twin Falls, Idaho. There they bought a lot and lived in a
tent until they saved enough money, from working as a hired hands for local
farmers, to build a house. Their son John built the house and it still stands on
Tyler Street in Twin Falls. Sometime in the 1940s they bought a 40-acre farm in
King Hill, Idaho.

        Photo: The Johann Laib family: (front, from left) Anna, Johann, Mother
        Bertha, Leontine; (back) Edward, Alfred, Bertha, Leo, John, Edwin.

Bertha died on Jan. 11, 1949. Johann then went to Lodi, Calif. and visited
Walter and Willie Thurn. During that time he remarried and moved back to the
farm. After a short time, she didn't like the area and moved back to California.
Johann then sold the farm and moved in with his children's families, gracefully
aging sitting in the most comfortable recliner in whichever home he was at,
reading the Bible and talking German until his death.

Johann and Bertha Laib had nine children:

John, 1904; Louise, Nov. 26, 1905; Bertha, Oct. 1, 1907; Alfred, May 8, 1912;
Edward, March 17, 1915; Annie, July 3, 1916; Edwin, Feb. 2, 1918; Leontina, June
18, 1919; Leo, Nov. 26, 1923.

All his children were very musical and played various instruments at family
gatherings.

        Photo: The Laibs: (front, from left) Timothy, LeAnn; (back) LeRoy,
        SuEllyn, Melinda, Ellen.

LeRoy & Ellen (Cutsforth) Laib

LeRoy Laib was born Dec. 27, 1928. He is the son of Fred Laib, Jr., and Martha
(Schlafman) Laib.

He was raised on the farm and went to Mercer school, graduating from high school
in 1946.

In 1948 he went into the Army and served in the Korean War. He was wounded at
Taigu, Korea, in 1950 and was again injured in 1951. This earned him the Oak
Leaf Cluster in addition to the Purple Heart and was air-lifted to Hawaii, then
to California for Treatment. With his severe leg injury, he was sent to Camp
Atterbury, Indianapolis, Ind., for a year and then to Fort Campbell, Kentucky,
for skin graft surgery. He returned for duty to California and was sent to
Baumholder, Germany, where he served as a finance clerk in an armored unit and
then was sent to Fontainebleau, France. Returning to the United States to Fort
Sheridan, Ill., he was discharged in 1954. He then went to Wahpeton school and
Capitol Commercial College in Bismarck.

On June 30, 1955, LeRoy married Ellen Gertrude Cutsforth. She was born Jan. 21,
1936, to W. Gale Cutsforth and Frances (Sponagle) Cutsforth. She was raised and
educated in Chetek, Wisconsin. After their marriage they moved to Rice Lake,
Wisconsin, where LeRoy worked as a bookkeeper for a woodwork manufacturing plant
for 13 years. He then became head bookkeeper for a worldwide plastics
manufacturing firm in Winona, Minn. After 24½ years, he retired March 1, 1991.
In appreciation his employer gave him a trip to Venezula. His fishing trip
consisted of Payara fish caught with Piranha fish.

LeRoy and Ellen have four children:

Timothy Lee Laib, born July 28, 1956, and married June 2, 1979, to Laurel Ann
Berg, born Sept. 14, 1956. They have two children, Angela Joy Laib, born June
13, 1983, and Jenna Lynn Laib, born March 13, 1989.

Melinda Francene Laib, born March 6, 1958, and married May 5, 1979, to Vernon
Adkins, born June 8, 1954. They have two children, Vernon Lee Adkins, born May
5, 1981, and Christopher Bruce Adkins, born April 3, 1984.

SuEllyn Maree Laib, born July 23, 1962.

LeAnn Martha Laib, born Dec. 22, 1967, and married Sept. 2, 1989, to Ervin
Schreiber, born Jan. 6, 1964. They have three children, Jordan Ray Schreiber,
born Nov. 18, 1993, Malissa Ann Schreiber, born July 14, 1995, and Adam Laib
Schreiber, born Feb. 10, 1999.

        Photo: The Meinhart Laib family: (front, from left) Doris, Melissa,
        Mike, Harold; (back) Margaret, Meinhart, Carl; (insert) Marvin.

Meinhart & Doris (Renfrow) Laib

Otto & Louise (Heinle) Laib

Otto Laib was born Feb. 6, 1912, to Friedrich Laib and Karolina (Kleingartner)
Laib at Mercer, N.D. He was raised and educated five miles south and about two
and one-half miles west of Mercer where he helped his parents farm until he was
22 years old.

        Photo: Louise and Otto Laib on their 25th wedding anniversary, October
        1959.

On Oct. 11, 1934, he married Louise Ida Heinle born Aug. 3, 1914, to Andrew
Henry Heinle and Elizabeth (Walcker) Heinle of Wilton, N.D. She was raised and
educated 10 miles south of Wilton.

Louise, at the age of 19, left home to help with the household chores at the
Fred and Martha Laib home while Martha was sick. After a few months, she was
hired by Frederick Just to do the cooking and cleaning for his children and to
take care of his invalid wife, Rosina (Foederer) Just, who suffered from a
paralyzing stroke and remained bedridden until her death on Sept. 23, 1934. All
this very young experience made her a very good cook and baker. She worked there
until her marriage to Otto.

Otto and Louise were married in the church parsonage in Mercer. The reception
was at his parents' home and they lived with them until that next spring when
they moved to Otto's grandparents, Balzer and Louise Kleingartner's farm. This
is where their first daughter, Eunice Louise Laib, was born on July 8, 1936.

The 1930s were some dry, hot and difficult years for farming. In April of 1937,
they bought Louis Baardson's farm that was about two and one-half miles west of
his parents' farm. Winters were cold and lots of snow was shoveled by hand in
those days. Horses were used to feed cattle and to take the cream and eggs to
town to sell so that they could buy some groceries.

On Sept. 19, 1943, Frances Burneice Laib was born in Turtle Lake at the home of
Rudolph and Ida (Korner) Heinle. This was during the World War II years and
certain foods were rationed like sugar, coffee, etc. On Dec. 29, 1945, Milbert
Lavern Laib was born in Underwood and died on Jan. 6, 1946.

During the summer of 1949, they built a big kitchen onto their little house.
During all this hard work, Calvin Otto Laib was born June 9, 1949, in Bismarck.

Otto farmed until his death at the age of 53, Sept. 22, 1965. At the age of 16,
Calvin had to take over the farming with his mother. Louise moved to Mercer in
January of 1979 and died Sept. 2, 1990. They are both buried in the Turtle Lake
cemetery.

Otto and Louise Ida (Heinle) Laib had four children:

Eunice Louise Laib married Richard Hausauer, Frances Burneice Laib married Lloyd
Rittenbach, Milbert Lavern Laib passed away after living nine days, Calvin Otto
Laib married Selena Looch.

Ronald & Sue (Carroll) Laib

Ronald John Laib was born Aug. 4, 1941, in Turtle Lake. He is the first child
(first son) of Edwin and Elizabeth (Bauer) Laib. For two years he attended
Turtle Lake High School, being the first person in Turtle Lake High along with a
classmate, able to complete high school in three years instead of four. He had
to transfer to Mercer High School and graduated in 1959.

He graduated from Concordia College in Minnesota in May of 1963 with a
Bachelor's degree in physics and math. He entered the U.S. Navy in June of 1963.
On March 12, 1964, he graduated from Airborn Radar Intercept Operator School at
the Naval Air Technical Training Center, Glynco, Georgia.

        Photo: Ronald Laib, 1983

He fought in the Viet Nam War and in 1966 was awarded one of the nation's
highest military declarations, the Air Medal, while serving with Fighter
Squadron 41 aboard the carrier "for meritorious achievement in aerial flight."

He graduated with a Master's Degree in Aeronautical Engineering in California in
1971. He also graduated with a USN Aviation Safety Officer School in 1971.

In 1975 he graduated from USN Test Pilot School. He graduated with an AeUSN
Aviation Safety Officer in 1977. In 1980 he graduated with a USAF JetEngine
Accident Investigation Degree. In 1982 he graduated from US Naval Postgraduate
School in AeEAE degree.

From 1985 to 1992 he graduated with degrees in optics, IR and propulsion. He
retired in June of 1983 as a LC Test Pilot. He was an experienced "instrument
rated" pilot, logging over 8500 flight hours in his military career, 850 flight
hours after, 600 aircraft carrier landings, 400 combat missions and received the
Distinguished Flying Cross Award.

In 1985 he joined Teledyne/Brown Engineering in Huntsville, Ala., as a senior
systems top secret engineer managing the Arrow Missile Program, Anti-Satellite
Missile, ODA Task and the Blue OSS task program.

        Photo: Sue and Ronald Laib, 1995.

In February of 1967, he married Sue Carroll, born December of 1945. She works as
an RN in a cardiovascular surgical ICU in Huntsville, Ala. They are the parents
of two children; Karen Lynn Laib and Kristy Lee Laib. Ronald died in 1997 when
the airplane he was piloting exploded in mid air.

        Photo: Karen Laib

Karen Lynn Laib was born in 1970 in California. She graduated from Huntsville
(Ala.) High School and graduated with Bachelor of Science in Nursing at the
University of Huntsville in 1993. She currently lives in San Diego, Calif. and
works as an RN.

Kristy Lee was born in 1971 in California. She graduated from Huntsville (AL)
High School and graduated from Opelika College in Auburn, Ala. with a Bachelor
of Science degree in nursing. She married Robby Sharp in August of 1997. They
had one son, Wyatt, born in 2000. They are currently living in Athens, Ala.,
where Kristy works as an RN at Lincare Home Infusion and is attending college
for a physician assistant. Robby owns and manages a construction company.

        Photo: Kristy, Robby and son Wyatt.

Wilbert & Gertrude (Strobel) Laib

Wilbert Laib was born July 29, 1930, to Fred Laib Jr. and Martha (Schlafman)
Laib. He went to school in Mercer. On July 1, 1954, he married Gertrude Strobel
of Denhoff who was born March 3, 1936, to John Strobel and Anna (Mertz) Strobel.
They moved in with Wilbert's parents and helped with the farming.

In the fall of 1955 they moved to Bismarck where Wilbert worked at B & R Grocery
and Gertrude did some house cleaning.

In 1957 they decided to move back to the farm with Wilbert's folks. Later they
built a little house on that farm. Besides farming they bought some milk cows
and sold the cream.

After 1963 they again decided to move the family to Bismarck and Wilbert again
went back to work for B & B Grocery. Gertrude then got a job at St. Vincent's
nursing home.

In 1971, they again decided to try farming and this time bought the home place.
They sold the farm to their son Bob in 1984 and moved to Carrington, N.D. and
bought the DelClaire Motel. In 1993 they retired and are now living in New
Rockford.

They have five children:

Renee Kay (Laib) Fields, born April 25, 1955; Dale Eugene Laib, born Oct. 25,
1958; Jean Diane Laib, born Jan. 27, 1962; Robert James Laib, born June 6, 1963,

Herbert & Sylvia (Erdmann) Leupp

Herbert Robert Leupp was born December 19, 1933, at Mandan, North Dakota to
Christ "Herbert" and Beatrice (Schow) Leupp. He had one sister, Dorrine Strecker
(1935-1973). Leupp's lived at Stanton, North Dakota where Herb's dad ran a café
and bar. Herb's mother, Beatrice, died in 1942, at the age of 38 from a CVA.
After she died, the Leupp family moved to Washburn where his dad ran Herb's
Café.

Herb graduated from Washburn in 1951, and attended UND for one and one half
years. In November 1953, he took a job with Meyer Broadcasting, KFYR. In
December 1953 KFYR went on the air with TV. Herb worked as a technical engineer,
radio switching, and playing records, etc. for a couple years.

Herb then took a job at KCGU at Mandan for nine years as engineer and announcer.
Around 1975 he went back to KFYR as chief engineer until 1996, when he retired.

On November 10, 1957, Herb married Sylvia Erdmann at Golden Valley, North
Dakota. She was born April 10, 1935 at Dodge, North Dakota to William and
Caroline Erdmann. She graduated from Golden Valley in 1953. She worked as an
accountant for Viking Homes for fourteen years and King Coal for thirteen years.
Sylvia obtained a Business Administration Degree from the University of Mary in
1991.

Herb and Sylvia had three children: Mitch, Terri and Ronald. Mitch was born June
29, 1959. He married Tamara Lenertz and they had three children: Kellen, Jordan,
and Seth. They live at Stanley, North Dakota where Mitch is the Administrator of
Mountrail County Nursing Home and Hospital.

Terri was born January 25, 1962 and married Mark Wilhelm at Brush Lake in 1993.
They have one daughter, Hailey and live at Bismarck. She was a reporter for KFYR
for seven years, and now works in Public Relations at the State Library.

Ronald was born May 1, 1965. He married Mary Greff and they had two girls,
Amanda and Amy. They later divorced and he is a regional manager for Schwan's at
Houston, Texas.

Sylvia and Herb purchased a cabin at Brush Lake in 1972 and, in 2000 they
purchased Larry Harr's home in Mercer where they now reside.

Ted &  Gladys (Lindteigen) Levi

Ted Levi was born Aug. 4, 1907, to Jacob and Emelia (Haase) Levi. He was born in
Eureka, S.D., and attended schools there until moving to Mercer in 1921 to a
farm northwest of Mercer. He graduated from Mercer High School in 1927. He
farmed with his father.

        Photo: Ted Levi

He and Gladys Lindteigen, born Feb. 2, 1919, were married on Oct. 4, 1942.
Gladys attended Turtle Lake High School and Minot State College. She taught
school for six years in Aurena and Wise Townships prior to her marriage.

The Levi family farmed near Mercer for many years, but retired in 1967 and moved
to Turtle Lake. They live in the house formerly owned by the Walt Endersgords,
early-day businessman to the city of Turtle Lake.

Gladys died on May 1, 1995, and Ted died on Feb. 13.1999.

The Levi's had one son, Gary, who is married to Caroline Deck of Harvey. They
have three children: Kevin born Nov. 27, 1961; Kim born Dec. 8, 1964; and
Karleen born May 1, 1967.

Compiled from the obituary and the McLean County Historical book, 1979.

Tony & Pamela (Freeberg) Lill

Pamela Candace Freeberg, the fourth child of Evelyn and Conrad Freeberg, was
born in 1947. She attended school in Mercer and graduated from Mercer High
School in 1965.

She went to college at Bismarck Junior College and received a one-year
secretarial certificate and Associate of Arts Degree. She continued her
education by going on to Valley City State College and received a Bachelors of
Science Degree in education. For two years she taught physical education and
business in the Mercer High School and with the closing of the school she worked
as an aide in the McClusky Elementary for two years.

In 1972 she married Tony Lill, Jr., from Bremen, N.D. They resided in Mercer.
They had two daughters, Stephanie, born in 1979 and Tonia, born in 1980. Tony
worked for Clairmont Construction for many years and for Falkirk Mining for 20
years. After their girls were born she quit full-time teaching and became a
full-time mom and did substitute teaching in the surrounding schools.

Stephanie graduated from Turtle Lake-Mercer School in 1997 and continued her
education in Grand Forks at the University of North Dakota. She graduated in
2003 with a major in Psychology. She is currently attending medical school at
the University of North Dakota.

Tonia graduated from Turtle Lake-Mercer School in 1998 and then attended
Moorhead State University, Bismarck State College and University of Mary in
Bismarck. She is currently attending Cal Poly at San Luis Obispo, California,
with plans of majoring in Recreation Administration. Tonia has a daughter, Kaia
Grace Lill, born in June of 2002.

The girls were very involved with sports and other activities in high school and
Tony and Pamela enjoyed golfing, boating and softball. They were involved with
farming along with regular jobs.

Tony died in 2001 and Pam still resides in Mercer.

Merle & Doris (Makeeff) Lindteigen

        Photo: Doris and Merle Lindteigen

Doris married Merle O. Lindteigen on Nov. 4, 1956, in the Baptist Church at

Doris is a member of the Turtle Lake Baptist Church and has been church clerk,

They had two children:

Ernest & Edna (Bender) Littke

At an early age, Ernest became interested in anything mechanical and started
fixing cars for other people. The first car he overhauled was for Fred Marzolf
and he received the amount of $5 for the job. Sometimes he fixed things for
someone without pay just to have something to do.

Ernest Littke married Edna Bender, daughter of Jacob and Louisa (Gessele) Bender
in 1940.

After their marriage they farmed ten miles north of Mercer until 1947 when they
bought a farm six miles north of Mercer known as the Keller farm. Rev. W.W.
Keller homesteaded it in the early 1900s, the house was built in 1905.

In 1951 they moved to Coulee City, Wash., where Ernest was employed as a
mechanic for five months. When they came back to North Dakota, they farmed and
he also worked as a mechanic at Just's Standard Service in Mercer for a time.

In 1975 they sold the farm to Russell Makeef, but continued to live there until
1991 when they moved to Bismarck.

Ernest died in April of 1991 and Edna died Nov. 24, 2004. Both are buried at
Hillside Cemetery at Mercer.

        Photo: The Littke family at the 50th wedding anniversary of Edna and
        Ernest: (from left) Susan, Edna, Jerry, Ernest and Janet.

Ernest and Edna's children are:

Janet married Albert Schadler and they had three sons: Alan lives at Fargo, Lyle
lives in Bismarck and Jeffery lives in Lincoln.

Susan married Eugene Brown of McClusky and they have two daughters: Teresa of
Fargo and Stacy Dawkins of West Fargo.

Jerry, who is an electrical engineer, lives at Hillsboro, N.D.

Karl & Christina (Schlechter), Christina (Schmidt) & Christina (Rieger) Littke

Karl Littke was born Nov. 18, 1880, in Neufreudenthal, South Russia. At age two
he moved to Romania where he grew up and was employed as a blacksmith and also
worked in a flour mill.

He married Christina Schlechter. She died at the birth of their first child,
Lydia, who remained in Romania with relatives and later married Rev. Herman
Derman.

        Photo: (Kneeling) Ernest; (seated) Karl and Christina; (back)
        Pauline, Walter Rieger, Bennie and Ernestine, 1928.

Karl immigrated to the United States in 1901. He lived at Kaylor, S.D., at
first, then came to McLean County and settled in Medicine Hill Township, 11
miles north and one mile west of what is now Mercer, N.D., in 1902.

In 1903 he married Christina Ulbright Schmidt. She had two sons, Gust and Carl
Schmidt.

Karl and Christina had four sons and two daughters.

Annie married Albert Hauf of Makoti. He died and she married Henry Monk and they
had one daughter. Henry died and she married Albert Schoenfish.

Emelia (Pauline) married Ben Bauer of Butte and they had five children.

William married Millie Parrow and they had three children.

Ferdinand (Vernon) married Emma Bohnet at Butte, and they had two daughters.

David married Ida Rittenbach of Turtle Lake, and they had two daughters.

Bennie married Elizabeth Fuerst of South Dakota, and they had three children.

Christina died in 1913.

In 1914 Karl, married Christina (Wagner) Rieger and she had three children. Her
three children are Mollie married to Bill Rauser and they had three children;
Emelia married Frank Russ and they had two sons; and Walter married Mollie
Schlettenhardt and they had one daughter.

Karl and Christina (Wagner) Littke had four children.

Ernestine married Earl Olson at Washburn and they had two sons. Ernest married
Edna Bender of Mercer, and they had three children. Edwin married Grace Thiele
at Wahpeton and they had five children. Carl married Elsie Laib and they had
three children.

        Photo: Karl and Christina (Wagner) Littke, 1938.

Karl and Christina lived in Medicine Hill Township until 1928, when they moved
to Mercer, where Karl owned the John Deere Implement dealership until 1943. He
sold the business to Christoph Schell, Jr. They moved to California and both
died there.

Christ & Gena (Peterson) Lockrem

Christopher O. Lockrem was born in Granite Falls, Minn., in 1880. His parents,
Ole K. and Anne Bakken immigrated to the United States from Vang, Valdres,
Norway in 1873. In 1903 they moved to Turtle Lake.

Nearby, another pioneer family homesteaded. A romance blossomed and on July 29,
1914, Gena Peterson became Chris' bride. Gena's family had moved to North Dakota
from Black River Falls, Wisc., in 1905. Her parents also were immigrants from
Norway.

Chris and Gena continued to live on the farm where they raised their family
until 1946 when they moved to Mercer.

Christ died in 1958 and Gena in 1992. Both are buried at St. Olaf Lutheran
Church Cemetery, rural Turtle Lake.

        Photo: (Front, from left) Gena and Christ; (back) Gertrude, Pearl,
        Garner and Chester.

Their five children were:

Gertrude Cecilia (Mrs. Glenn Love) and Pearl M. (Mrs. Archie Kline), and son,
Oliver B., who died in infancy.

Cousins Garner Webster and Chester (Webster) Lockrem were raised by the Lockrems
after their mother, Ella (Lockrem) Webster died.

Ole & Ragna (Nelson) Lockrem

Ragna Nelson was born at Dexter, Mower County, Minn., on June 25, 1887. She was
the oldest of seven children: Ragna, Marcus, Theodore, Norman, Elmer, Clara and
Ida.

At the age of 15, Ragna moved to Turtle Lake, to homestead with her family. She
met Ole Lockrem of Turtle Lake, and they were married when Ragna was 18. Ole's
favorite instrument was the violin and Ragna loved music too, and they would
often play together, the violin and organ.

They homesteaded northeast of Turtle Lake on the W½ of E½ 33-148-79. Their home
and all their earthly possessions burned to the ground about 1916.

Ole and Ragna retired from farming in 1943 due to Ole's health. Ole died in
1966. Ragna lived with her daughter Agnes until confined to a nursing home in
Bismarck where she died in 1971.

Ole and Ragna had seven children:

Clarence was the oldest and married Margaret Christensen in 1930. Clarence died
in Seattle on Jan. 8, 1973. Agnes married John Bergo in 1928 and has three
children and they live in Minot, N.D. Lillian died in infancy. Olie married
Willa Boehm and died in 1976.

Ruth died in infancy. Leo married Martha Kirby and died in 1973. They have three
children.

Irene married Jerry Hofrenning and lives in Chicago, Ill. They have five
children, one died in infancy.

Taken from the McLean County Heritage Book.

Alfred Clinton & Doris (Jorgenson) Lowe

Alfred Clinton Lowe was born on Nov. 9, 1930, in Big Timber, Montana to Rev.
M.L. and Genevieve Lowe.

Alfred Lowe taught and coached basketball in Alamo, N.D. from 1957-1959. He
moved to Golden Valley, N.D. and was a teacher and coach from 1959 to 1963. He
then moved to Mercer, N.D. and was a teacher and coach from  1963 to 1972. The
last three years in Mercer he was the superintendent. After moving to Washburn,
N.D. in 1972 he was principal at the school and did some teaching and coaching.

He was in the U.S. Army from November 1949 to November 1952 in the Army Security
Agency. He was in Korea from March 1951 to October 1952.

Alfred is retired and makes his home in Washburn. He enjoys golfing. If you
can't find him at home, look on the golf course.

        Photos: Doris and Clint Lowe

Alfred Clinton married Doris Marie Jorgenson on October 23, 1952, in Mercer.
Doris was born on Sept 9, 1934 in Wilton, N.D. Doris is the daughter of Louie
Jorgenson and Dora Ellen Davenport. Dora Jorgenson ran the telephone company
switchboard for many years in Mercer. They have three children:

Brenda L. Lowe was born August 7, 1953, in Bismarck, North Dakota. Brenda
married Kevin Vossler on July 1, 1973 in Washburn. Kevin was born on Jan. 5,

Rev. M.L. & Genevieve (Rhoades) Lowe

Marcus Lionel Lowe was born Feb. 22, 1902, in Cave In Rocks, Ill. He went to
Montana about 1925 and entered the ministry.

He met Genevieve Dean Rhoades, who was born in Melville, Mont., on March 18,
1908.

To this union seven children were born: Gladys, Alfred Clinton, Donald, Juanita,
Calvin, Glenn and Deloris.

M.L. Lowe ministered in the states of Montana, North Dakota, Minnesota and
western Canada.

In the fall of 1947, the family moved to Mercer. Gladys taught school seven
miles south of Mercer. The other children attended the Mercer School.

The three oldest children married Mercer people. Gladys married Arnie Makeeff,
June 5, 1949. Alfred Clinton married Doris Jorgenson, Oct. 23, 1952. Juanita
married Meinhardt Wagner, April 16, 1952.

In 1949 the Lowes, except the three oldest, moved to Lignite, N.D., and from
there to Michigan. M.L. Lowe died Nov. 17, 1979, and Genevieve died April 8,
1985. There are both buried at the Grace Memorial Cemetery in Aripeka, Florida,
where they retired.

Jerald & Arlis (Wagner) Lundgren

Arlis (Wagner) Lundgren is the second child of Fred and Louise Wagner. She was
born on May 3, 1941, and raised on the family farm 12 miles south of Mercer. She
attended rural school until the eighth grade and then attended Mercer High
School. Arlis graduated in 1959.

After high school she went to Minot State College and then taught fifth grade in
the Washburn North Dakota elementary school for two years and then moved to and
taught four years in Minot, North Dakota.

She married Jerald D. Lundgren from Mora, Minn., in December of 1963. They had
four children: Jerald II from St. Cloud, Minn.; Melanee from Minneapolis, Minn.;
Heather from St. Cloud, Minn. and Gretchen from St. Cloud, Minn.

Arlis has worked at varied jobs over the years but has worked as a one-day tour
director for Utopia Tours for about 13 years.

Arlis and Jerald started and owned Insurance by Lundgren in St. Cloud, Minn.

Jerald passed away in August of 2000 and Arlis continues to live on the hobby
farm near Sartell, Minn. She enjoys her eight grandchildren, working part-time,
sewing, reading, summers at the lake and life in general.

Emanuel & Rosella (Fried) Makeeff

Emanuel Makeeff, son of Michael and Sophie Makeeff, was born on Dec. 7, 1901, in
Romania. Emanuel entered the United States Sept. 11, 1902, with his mother
Sophie and his maternal grandparents Johann and Rosina Pfeifer and family. He
came from Romania aboard the SS Arcadia and landed at Halifax, Nova Scotia.

He grew to manhood in the Butte and Mercer area and married Rosella Fried,
daughter of Fredrich and Wilhelmina Tetzlaff Fried on Dec. 29, 1925, at
Washburn, North Dakota. The ceremony was performed by Emanuel Brockel, Minister
of the Gospel.

        Photo: The Makeeff family around 1935: (from left) Doris, Perry Irene,
        Arnie, Emanual and Rosella with the baby, Deloris.

        Photo: Emanual Makeeff home in 1935 (left) and the home in 1950 (below).

They farmed one mile north of Mercer from 1925 until 1966, and raised eight
children. They moved into Turtle Lake upon retiring.

They celebrated their Silver Wedding Anniversary in 1950 and their Golden
Wedding Anniversary in 1975.

Emanuel died on Saturday, May 29, 1976, in Bismarck, North Dakota. Funeral
services were held at 2 p.m. Wednesday at the Turtle Lake Baptist Church.
Burial was at the Turtle Lake Cemetery, Turtle Lake, North Dakota.

Rosella was born on July 13, 1906, in Benedict, North Dakota. She died on April
26, 1988, in Turtle Lake, North Dakota. She was 81 years old at the time of
death. Funeral services were at 2 p.m. in Turtle Lake Baptist Church. Rosella
is also buried in the Turtle Lake Cemetery, Turtle Lake, North Dakota.

Rosella's hobbies were gardening, quilting, sewing, her grandchildren and
genealogy before it became popular. Can you imagine her doing genealogy now in
the days of computers and microfilms instead of letter writing. She'd be in
seventh heaven.

        Photo: Emanual and Rosella Makeeff

Emil & Ruth (Hovis) Makeeff

Emil Makeeff, son of Michael and Sophie Makeeff was born on Jan. 7, 1905, in

several years in the Mercer and McClusky areas.

        Photo: Emil Makeeff in the 1920s.

After spending some time traveling, he settled in Bismarck, North Dakota, where
he was engaged in building and interior decorating. He was active in the Non-
Partisan League. He was employed in R.E.A. Construction contracting work in
Montana, Wyoming and South Dakota. He also had some interests in oil well
drilling in Wyoming.

He died on Sept. 6, 1968, in Hot Springs, Fall River County, South Dakota, at
the age of 63. He was buried in Turtle Lake Cemetery, Turtle Lake, North Dakota.

Emil married Ruth Winifred Hovis daughter of Clinton Powel Hovis and Louise
Berger on Aug. 26, 1941, in Bismarck, Burleigh Co., North Dakota. They were
married in the Assembly of God Church.

moved to Wyoming where she attended school. In 1930 she moved to Canada with
her parents. In 1938 she entered nurses training at Bismarck, North Dakota,

Lake, North Dakota.

John & Dorothy (Lentz) Makeeff

John Makeeff, son of Michael and Sophie was born Feb. 1, 1914, in Butte, North
Dakota. He grew up on a farm northeast of Turtle Lake, North Dakota. He
received his education there and graduated from eighth grade in 1928.

John married Dorothy Lentz on June 26, 1938, in Turtle Lake, North Dakota.
Dorothy was born on Dec. 20, 1923, in Turtle Lake, North Dakota, and was
educated there.

        Photo: Dorothy Makeeff

        Photo: John Makeeff

After their marriage they moved to Michigan and lived there a few years. They
moved back to North Dakota and went into farming with his father for a time
until he bought a farm northeast of Mercer, North Dakota. He then operated a
café in Mercer after which he sold the farm and moved to Wisconsin. He operated
a dairy for some years.

Later he organized and headed a group called "The Makeeff Family Gospel
Singers", composed of some of his family members. They were John, Dorothy,
Bernice, Larry, Dwight and Dennis. They traveled extensively and also made
recordings.

John died on June 30, 1990, in Eau Claire, Wisconsin.

Mike & Vehona (Kirschenman-Helm) Makeeff, Jr.

Mike Makeeff, Jr., son of Michael and Sophie was born on Oct. 3, 1903, in Butte,
(Dogden) North Dakota. He received his education in North Dakota.

Mike married Vehona Kirschenman Helm on June 4, 1944, in Mercer, North Dakota.
Mike and Vehona were married by Rev. Ralph Brostrom at the Church of God.

Vehona was born on May 16, 1902, in Oacama, South Dakota. Vehonas parents were
George Kirschenman and Katherina Buchmiller. As a small child she moved with
her parents to Streeter, North Dakota, and later to Lincoln Valley where she was
married to Louis Helm. He died several years later leaving Vehona and four
sons.

        Photo: Vehona and Mike Jr. Makeeff

Mike took up farming as his livelihood and farmed in different areas and later
settled on a farm northeast of Mercer, in the area called the Prophet Mountains
in Sheridan County. He lived on the farm until selling out and moving to
McClusky, North Dakota, where they operated a café for several years. They sold
out and moved to Turtle Lake, North Dakota, where they again opened up a café
and operated it until retiring.

Mike and Vehona celebrated their silver wedding anniversary in 1968. Mike died
at 7:26 a.m. at the age of 68 on Oct. 10, 1971, from asthma and acute myocardial
infarction in the Turtle Lake Hospital. He was buried Oct. 13, 1971, in the
cemetery at Turtle Lake, North Dakota. Vehona died at 11:57 p.m. at the age of
68 on April 22, 1971, of acute pulmonary edema and myocardial infarction in
Turtle Lake, North Dakota. Vehona was buried April 26, 1971, in the Turtle Lake
Cemetery, in Turtle Lake, North Dakota.

Stanley was born on May 14, 1939, in Benedict, North Dakota.

Michael &  Sophie (Pfeifer) Makeeff, Sr.

Michael Makeeff, Sr. was born on Oct. 12, 1878, in Alexandrovsh, Russia. Later
this city's name was changed to Zapororzhe. Michael grew up in this area and
when a young man moved to Romania and settled there. Here he met Sophie.

Michael married Sophie Pfeifer, daughter of Johann Pfeifer and Euphrosina
Jasmann on March 2, 1901, in Gushaluk, Romania. Sophie was born on March 22,
1885, in Bessarabia, Romania.

In 1901 they came to the United States, and settled in the (Dogden) Butte, North
Dakota, area. A few years later they moved to a farm northeast of Turtle Lake,
North Dakota. They farmed here until they retired and moved into Turtle Lake in
1942, where they lived until their death.

        Photo: Mike and Sophie Makeeff, Sr.

They celebrated their silver wedding anniversary in 1926 and their golden in
1951.

Mr. and Mrs. Makeeff were members of the Baptist Church.

Michael died of a heart attack at his home in Turtle Lake, at the age of 76, on
Dec 4, 1954, in Turtle Lake, North Dakota. He is buried in the cemetery at
Turtle Lake, N.D.

Sophie died at the age of 83, on Jan. 14, 1966, of a stroke in the hospital at
Minot, North Dakota. She is also buried in the cemetery at Turtle Lake, North
Dakota.

The Makeeffs had a family of eight children, six of whom are still living. They
are Emanuel and John of Mercer; Mike, Turtle Lake; Emil, Hot Springs, South
Dakota; Tillie, Mrs. Christ Heim, Mercer; and Maggie, Mrs. Otto Kolshifski,
Ruso.

Some excerpts from The McLean County Heritage Historical Society: 1978.

Mr. Makeeff came to the United States in April 1902 leaving behind his wife and
child.

He settled at Anamoose, North Dakota and worked at the livery stable hauling
mail to country post offices. Within six months he had saved enough money to
bring his wife and child to this country. They arrived at Anamoose in September
1902.

        Photo: The Mike Makeeff Sr family, circa 1921.

In 1903, he quit his job and went out to look for a homestead. He rented a team
of horses and started out.

After much scouting around he filed on a homestead about 20 miles northeast of
Turtle Lake. After getting his family settled in a one room shack adjoining the
homestead, Mr. Makeeff began breaking 40 acres of sod and putting in flax which
later was destroyed by cattle. Next came the task of building a home for his
family. The Makeeffs worked together in building their first home and in 1903
they moved into their little sod house.

Mr. Makeeff went out threshing and did odd jobs to make extra money to buy seed
for his next year's crop.

Again, his crop failed leaving him empty-handed. But with the will to get ahead
and hopes of better days he worked hard and finally the break came with a few
good crops. About the same time Turtle Lake was being built and in 1905 the
Northern Pacific built a branch line in the new town site.

Mr. Makeeff soon purchased a threshing machine. It was run by eight head of
horses walking around in a circle. The machine had a feeder for a blower and a
person had to pitch the straw away into the stack to keep the feeder clean.

He often thought of selling his homestead and settling closer to Turtle Lake. It
was a long distance to come for supplies and very hard on the horses to travel
so far. He was called to the service of his country in 1918. But the day he
reported to his station, word came that the war had ended. This was a very
happy day for Mike and his family.

In 1919, he gave up his homestead and bought a farm 13 miles northeast of Turtle
Lake. Once again the Makeeff's endured many hardships. On July 8, 1924, at
about one o'clock a tornado struck and destroyed all the buildings except the
house and granary. So the task of rebuilding what was destroyed began. With
this all completed the Makeeff's decided to build a new home. They built a 28 ×
32 two story house. By 1926, the Makeeff's had a very nice farm.

Other information:

Mike Makeeff entered the United States March 9, 1902, at Ellis Island. The ship
he was on was the SS Moltke. Accompanying him was his brother-in-law Johann
Pfeifer. Mike showed his age as 25, occupation as laborer country of origin was
Romania. His wife (Sophie) and son (Emanuel) were not with him on this ship.
They stayed behind in Romania and came to the United States six months later,
aboard the SS Arcadia landing in Halifax, Nova Scotia Sept. 11, 1902. Sophia
gave her age as 18 years old and final destination was Anamoose, North Dakota.

Mike filed for citizenship in the United States on March 2, 1908, and took the
Oath of Allegiance on June 9, 1908. Affidavit of Witnesses for Mike's Petition
were Fred Skyss of Maxwell, North Dakota, and Frank Putz of Martin, North
Dakota.

        Photo: Violet Makeeff, granddaughter of Sophia Makeeff.

Daniel & Christine (Degg) Mayer

Daniel Mayer was born in Borodino, Bessarabia, South Russia, on May 26, 1883.
His parents were Johann Mayer, a farmer and Margaretha Mayer nee Sackman. He was
baptized shortly after birth and confirmed in the village of Kloestitz at the
age of 14 years.

On March 14, 1902, Daniel married his stepsister, Christine Degg, in a double
wedding with sister Karolina and Gotlob Ehni.

        Photo: Daniel and Christine Mayer

In May of 1902, Daniel, Christine and other family members immigrated to North
America on the S.S. Arcadia. The crossing took about 14 days and the ship was
dirty and stinky with all the cattle on board. The ship landed at Halifax, Nova
Scotia where Daniel and Christine departed for South Dakota to the homestead of
Margaretha's sister, Karolina and husband Frederich Obenauer.

Following a short stay, the Obenauers gave them a wagon and horses, a cow and a
hen with five chicks. Daniel and Christine then departed for North Dakota and
acquired a homestead about three miles from Mercer. A sod house was built and
Regine, John, Christine, Pauline, Otto, Amelia, Olga, Daniel and Helen were all
born there. The sod house had dirt floors, with the exception of the parent's
bedroom, which had a wooden floor.

In 1913 a new sod house was built, about one and one-half miles from Mercer.
This house, with its thick walls, was the birthplace of five more family
members, namely Carl, Bertha, Anna, Theodore and Dorothea.

Daniel was a prominent farmer in the area and a faithful member of the country
Lutheran Church (St. Paulus) and also of Hope Lutheran Church in Mercer. He was
a deacon for many years and also served as treasurer.

Daniel died on Sept. 6, 1935, from injuries received earlier in an automobile
accident. Christine moved to Mercer in 1938. The last 10 years of her life were
spent in Underwood at the F.E. Anderson home. She died in Bismarck on June 21,
1960.

Daniel and Christine had 14 living children, 45 grandchildren, and several
great-grandchildren, at the time of Christine's death.

        Photo: The Daniel Meyer family: (front, from left) Helen, Theodore,
        Anna, Bertha, Carl; (back) Dorothea, Daniel, Amelia, Pauline, Christine,
        and Regine. Not pictured: Olga, John and Otto.
