Soren & Maren (Andersen) Petersen

In 1904, Soren and Maren Petersen and son, Peter, from Hutchinson, Minnesota,
came to Wise Township. They helped their daughter, Juliana Petrea Hanson, build
a three room house on her homestead in Section 2 just south of the Danish
Cemetery. After a year, they filed on a homestead of their own just east of Rev.
Keller's home.

Soren "Miller" Petersen was born August 2, 1840, in Astrup, Vejle County,
Denmark, to Peter Jensen and Juliana Plett. Maren Andersen was born October 14,
1847, in Rarap, Vejle County, Denmark to Anders Rasmussen "Stamper" and Maren
Jensdatter. Her youngest brother, Soren Andersen "Stamper," lived in Minneapolis
and died around 1945.

Maren and Soren were married at Vejle, Denmark, where seven of their eight
children were born. They were Andrew, Juliana Petrea, Christine, Mary, Sine,
Amelia, Peter, and Valdemar.

        Photo: Soren and Maren Petersen

Soren owned and operated a wind propelled flour-mill in Vejle. He also had a
small dairy farm and often delivered flour by boat to the nearby islands. His
children sometimes accompanied him on these trips and also helped him load flour
onto wagons.

Because of their flour mill, they were referred to as the "Millers."

        Photo: Soren Petersen's flour mill in Denmark.

In 1885, they traveled by steamship for three weeks to New York City. The stormy
journey made them all extremely seasick. From New York they traveled by train to
Hutchinson, Minnesota, where they lived on a farm.

Andrew, the oldest, was born around 1867 and came to the U.S. before the rest of
the family, about 1884. He served in the U.S. Army during the Spanish American
War of 1898. Upon his discharge he worked in Chicago, and eventually was never
heard from again.

Juliana Petrea was born August 11, 1869. She walked to school in wooden shoes
and said the Christian faith was taught in Denmark right along with the 3 R's.
She came to the U.S. when she was 16. She married James Hansen in 1891 at
Hutchinson, Minnesota, and they had one daughter, Carlie. James died of
tuberculosis in 1897. Juliana then worked at various jobs, including practical
nursing until she homesteaded at Mercer in 1904. She married Jonas Christensen
in 1906, and they had two children, Shirley and Walter.

Christine was born in 1872. She married Andrew Nelsen and lived at Hopkins,
Minnesota. She died in 1897 or 1898, leaving a baby boy, Carslie. Her sister,
Juliana, "Anne", took care of him, but he died of diphtheria when he was two
years old.

Mary was born March 17, 1874. She married Christian W. Christensen, brother of
Jonas, in November 1898 at Hutchinson. In 1903, they homesteaded in Medicine
Hill Township in Section 34. They had two girls and five sons. Mary died in 1934
in Spokane.

Sine was born in 1876. She worked for many years in Minneapolis as a cook in
private homes. She married Fred Rasmussen in 1901, and they lived in Hutchinson,
Minnesota. They had twin sons and three daughters. Sine died March 1954 in Rice
Lake, Wisconsin.

Amelia was born August 5, 1881. She worked as a maid in Minneapolis and, later,
worked in Spokane and Seattle. She married Charles Munding at Bakersfield,
California, on June 5, 1912. They had three sons and two daughters.

Peter was born in 1883. He helped his father on the homestead and also worked on
the railroad at Mercer in 1906. In 1908 he began working for the railroad at
Hillyard, near Spokane, Washington, where he worked for several years. He
married a lady with six children.

Valdemar, the youngest, died at birth in 1885 in Hutchinson, Minnesota.

Soren was described as a warm, kind, loving person with a terrific sense of
humor. He suffered from asthma and thought the drier climate in North Dakota
would be good for his health. He enjoyed four years of fairly good health on his
homestead until he died of pneumonia in March 1908. His family felt joy when he
became a Christian two weeks before he died.

Soren's dog, Tray, a black shepherd, followed the funeral wagon to the Danish
cemetery one mile north of their farm and saw his master lowered into the grave.
Everyday after that, the dog trotted over to lie on the grave for awhile before
returning home. Soon after the funeral, Maren and Peter moved their little house
into Mercer, and Peter continued to work for the railroad. Although Mercer was
seven miles south of the cemetery, Tray frequently continued to visit the grave.
Family members were deeply touched by the depth of the dog's devotion for his
dead master.

Maren and Peter moved to Spokane, Washington, the fall of 1908, and Amelia
stayed with them for a time. Maren helped her daughter, Mary, and Chris
Christensen when their twins, Roy and Ray, were born in 1911. When Peter married
in 1916, Maren left for California to stay with Amelia.

In 1919, when the flu epidemic raged through the Mercer area, it claimed the
life of frail Maren. She died in March and her funeral was held outdoors at
Jonas and Juliana's home, as people did not enter the homes of flu victims.
Juliana was also sick with the flu and unable to attend her mother's funeral.
Maren was buried in the Danish Cemetery and is remembered as a very happy-go-
lucky type of person.

Elmer & Esther (Rust, Bohnet) Peterson

Esther (Rust) was born Oct. 25, 1910, to Lena and Samuel Rust Sr. She grew up 14
miles north of Mercer where she attended rural school.

Esther married Benjamin Bohnet in 1930 and later they moved to Lodi, Calif.,
where he died in 1933. She returned to North Dakota with her infant daughter,
Leona. Then she worked at the school library and lunchroom.

She married Elmer Peterson in October of 1941 in Turtle Lake. They lived and
farmed three miles south of Mercer until they retired and moved into Mercer in
1964. He died in May of 1991. Elmer was a member of the First Baptist Church,
taught Sunday school, deacon, Senior Citizen and Mercer school board holding
various offices in each organization.

Esther continued to live in Mercer until April of 1995 when she moved to the
Sheridan Memorial Home in McClusky. Esther was a charter member of the Mercer
Senior Citizens Club, charter and 50-year member of the Hustling Homemakers in
Mercer. She was a member of the First Baptist Church and the Women's Missionary
Fellowship where she held various offices.

Elmer and Esther leave behind two daughters. Mrs. Richard (Leona Bohnet)
Neumiller, living in Bismarck and Mrs. Dick (Dorothy) Tretter from Hope, N.D.
They have seven grandchildren and several great grandchildren.

Joseph & Minnie (Jones) Peterson

Joseph Benjamin Peterson was born June 4, 1881, in Lake Park, Becker County,
Minnesota. His parents, Nels and Johanna (Olson) Peterson were immigrants from
Skawna, Sweden. He was the last of twelve children, having seven older brothers
and four older sisters.

Joseph was seven years old when his father died. Three years later, the family
moved from Minnesota to McHenry County, North Dakota, where they homesteaded. In
1904, Joseph came to McLean County and filed on a homestead eight miles north of
Mercer in Section 33 and 34 in Medicine Hill Township. Over the years he built
up his farm to 960 acres.

Joseph married Minnie Cordelia Jones on January 8, 1912, at the Lutheran
parsonage of Rev. Keller, who lived north of Mercer. She was born on April 24,
1887, in Claremont, Minnesota, in Dodge County to Rensular (Rensselaen) Jones
and Mary Ann Kerr. They were of Welsh/Pennsylvania Dutch and Scotch/Irish decent
respectively. Her father was a carpenter and harness maker.

Minnie was the fifth of eight children, having four sisters and three brothers.
Her brother, Hugh Jones, born March 20, 1884, homesteaded in the SE¼ of Section
6 in Prophet's Township in 1908. He married Genevieve Guyer of Claremont,
Minnesota, in 1909. Three of Minnie's sisters also lived in the Mercer area.
Grace, born May 18, 1879, married Walter Lemmings, and later, Fred Sorenson;
Irene, born February 9, 1881, married Dave Norton; Mary (Mabel), born June 15,
1889, married George Heinze.

Minnie received a good education and became a school teacher in Huron, South
Dakota. Then she came to Mercer, North Dakota, after answering an advertisement
for teaching positions. She taught in Mercer and in Wise and Medicine Hill
Townships in one room schoolhouses. The August 27, 1909, Mercer Telegram
reported, "Minnie Jones is a most efficient teacher and we all know this is an
extraordinary hard school to teach successfully." She was a member of the
Bloomer Girls sports team in 1910.

Minnie met Joseph Peterson by having to go to his home once a month to get her
paycheck. He was a school board clerk, as he was one of the few that could read,
write and speak English at the time. Every summer Minnie had a big box of books
sent out to her home, and she loaned them out to students.

        Photo: Minnie, Pearl and Joseph Peterson

Joseph was a leader in politics and community activities. He ran for County
Commissioner in 1912. He was also a diversified farmer. He had an Avery tractor
and threshing machine and, with hired hands, threshed grain for many farmers who
lived around the area. Later, Joe had a Holt combine that was pulled by six
horses and took several men to operate. The duties of the men were: a teamster,
a header man, a sack sewer, and a machine mechanic. The combine was operated
with an auxiliary engine. One man filled and sewed the sacks with grain, and a
second man released them down a side chute at regular intervals in windrows. The
header man had the duty of adjusting the height of the sickle bar for minimum
straw length, and the mechanic kept the machinery in working order. The teamster
drove the six horses.

        Photo: Joe Peterson's Holt combine, Earl and Richard Postel watching.

It is said that Joe believed in a "fair deal" for each man. Minnie continued to
teach school at Mercer. The union of Joseph and Minnie produced four children,
but only one survived past infancy. Her name was Pearl May Peterson, born May
14, 1914. Later Joseph and Minnie also raised Echo Mae Webster, who came to them
at the age of two after her mother died.

After Pearl graduated from high school, she attended Jamestown College. She then
taught school in Mercer for two years, 1935 and 1936. In 1937 and 38 she taught
at a consolidated school called Hamilot, near Mohall, North Dakota, before
teaching for one and one half years in Ross, North Dakota. She then resigned
from teaching and began her career as a social worker. Her first position was in
Napoleon, North Dakota, and, then, Carson, North Dakota. She also worked at the
Indian Reservation at Fort Yates, North Dakota.

In 1951, she achieved a Masters Degree in social work at the University of
Nebraska. She then took a job in Clackamas County, Oregon, and after two years
went to Portland where she became a city consultant for child welfare.

On June 12, 1955, Pearl married Eddie Schultz, whose first wife had died from a
sudden brain aneurysm. He had five children: Darrel, Kenneth, Wanda, Gene and
Dorothy.

Pearl and Eddie had one child together, Joseph Eddie Schultz, born August 29,
1957. After one year, Ed and Pearl moved to Buhl, Idaho, where Ed developed a
dairy farm. Pearl worked for Twin Falls County Dept. of Public Assistance. She
held this job until her illness prevented her from working. Pearl died in July
of 1971. Her son, Joe, a Lutheran pastor, lives in Buckly, Washington, with his
wife, Dorothy, and son, Tobie.

Joseph and Minnie moved to Buhl, Idaho, to retire near their adopted daughter,
Echo. Echo married Hanvy Shearl in 1942, and they had two children, Judy and
James. In 1947, Echo married Eddy A. Dalos and they had three children, Coral,
Dennis, and Eric.

Joseph Peterson died December 12, 1950, and Minnie died March 27, 1974. They are
buried in Buhl, Idaho.

Maria Peterson family

After the death of Anton Peterson in 1905 in DeKalb, Ill., his widow Maria
Peterson moved to the McClusky area with her family.

In 1908 Martin (son) accompanied his oldest brother Peter and his wife to
Sheridan County, traveling in an emigrant train. A land company agent was
traveling in Illinois to induce residents to buy land from the Northern Pacific
Railroad, which ran through Sheridan County and terminated in Turtle Lake in
McLean County. Peter and his wife moved to John's Lake Township, Sheridan County
and when Maria and her children came in 1909, she rented a farm 12 miles south
of McClusky near Peter's place.

In 1910, she moved her family to Edgemont Township south of Pickardville. After
two years she rented a farm in Pikard Township, Sheridan County. William married
Ella Hedahl in 1915 and the rest of the family moved to a farm near William's
place in Sheridan County. Maria, who was born in 1855, died in 1938 while living
with Chris and Elmer.

There were 11 Peterson children:

Peter Peterson, born on May 1, 1879, and settled in the McClusky area.

Anna Peterson, born on Oct. 2, 1880, married Christ Jorgenson and died in 1965
in Williston.

Albertina (Tina) Peterson, born Oct. 27, 1884, married Chris Swendson. She died
Dec. 26, 1970.

Hattie Peterson married Gail Brown and they farmed south of Pickardville. She
was born on April 2, 1881, and died on June 30, 1960.

Martin Peterson, see family history.

Nels Peterson, born Dec. 12, 1888, farmed in Edgemont Township, Sheridan County,
until his death in August of 1941. He is buried in the Mercer Cemetery.

William Peterson, see family history.

Elizabeth Peterson born Aug. 8, 1893, married Perry Van Vleet and lived in the
Pickardville area.

Margaret (Maggie) Peterson, born July 1, 1885, was a country schoolteacher for
44 years near Westhope, Harvey and Reeder. She died on Sept. 25, 1893, and is
buried in the Mercer Cemetery.

Chris Peterson was born Jan. 21, 1896. He was a widower and lived with his
mother until he retired and moved to Bismarck.

Elmer Peterson, married Esther Rust Bohnet, see family history.

Martin & Darrell (Biggs) Peterson

Martin Peterson was born on Nov. 18, 1886, to Anton and Maria Peterson.

He married Darrell Biggs on April 11, 1909. She was born on May 25, 1890. They
lived on the "Davidson Ranch" south of Mercer and then moved into Mercer.

        Photo: Martin and Darrell Peterson

Martin co-owned the pool hall with Halfdon Berge, and he was also a rural mail
carrier. He had a Standard Oil Service station and worked for the North Dakota
State Highway Department for many years.

Darrell died on July 27, 1946, and Martin lived in Mercer and in the Sheridan
Memorial home in McClusky until his death on June 23, 1983.

Martin and Darrell had one daughter, Mary Frances, and an adopted granddaughter,
Mary Frances Crum.

Martin loved the outdoors and enjoyed gardening, both flowers and vegetables. He
planned and landscaped his yard. The sunken garden at his home was a playground
for the children in Mercer. Many receptions were held there.

William & Ella (Hedahl) Peterson

William Peterson was born on Dec. 31, 1890, in Big Rock, Ill., to Anthon and
Maria Peterson. His father died on Oct. 26, 1905. William grew up and attended
school in Waterman, Ill. In 1909, Maria and nine of her children came to
Sheridan County. They lived on a farm 12 miles south of McClusky which was near
the older son, Peter. In 1910, Maria's family moved to Edgemont Township south
of Pickardville.

        Photo: William and Eva Hedahl, married in 1915.

William married Ella Hedahl on Nov. 24, 1915, in Minot and homesteaded 3½ miles
southeast of Mercer. Ella, the daughter of Nels and Inga Hedahl, was born in
1885 in Minnesota and died on March 6, 1926, with the birth of her son, Wilbur.
William and his daughter Margery, born in 1916, and sons Ervin, born in 1918,
and Wilbur, born in 1926, continued farming for 17 more years. In 1943, he
turned the farm over to his daughter, Margery, and son-in-law Ralph Burck.

In 1943 Bill moved to Mercer and worked for the North Dakota State Highway
Department until 1958 when he retired. His route was old ND #7 (now 200), #41
Mercer to Wilton and #14 to Wing.

After retirement, he worked for area farmers. While on the farm he served on
township and school boards. After he moved to Mercer, he was on the town board.
For many years he served on the Our Savior's Lutheran Church Council and was on
the building committee for the present church. He was the caretaker for the
church for many years. He donated the land for the new addition of the Mercer
Cemetery.

        Photo: William Peterson

At the age of 83 he took up painting. In 1987, he moved to the Sheridan Manor in
McClusky where he lived until his death on March 4, 1991, in the Turtle Lake
Hospital at the age of 100 and 2 months. He and Ella are buried in the Mercer
Cemetery.

Richard & Eunice (Christensen, Bergan) Pfliger

Eunice was born June 6, 1944, at the Bismarck Hospital, the second child of
Walter and Ruth (Ovre) Christensen. She was baptized August 1, 1944, at Our
Savior's. Her sponsors were Reed and Martha (Ovre) Argent and Sid and Mollie
Nielsen.

        Photo: Eunice Pfliger, graduation picture, 1961

She attended Medicine Hill School #4 for eight years. Mollie Nielsen was
teaching this country school when Eunice graduated from 8th grade in 1957. She
then attended one year of high school in Mercer, and three years at Dakota
Lutheran Academy in Minot where she graduated in 1961. She was confirmed by Rev.
Robert Dirks on June 5, 1960, at Our Savior's Lutheran Church.

She attended the Lutheran Bible Institute in Minneapolis, Minot State, and
Bismarck Junior College, graduating in 1964.

She married Terry Bergan on June 18, 1965. They were divorced in 1988. They had
three daughters: Denise (Bruce) Martin, Linton, N.D., (Matthew, Alexis, Trevor,
and Justin); Shyla (Mike) Anfinson, Bismarck, N.D., (Christopher and Josie); and
Jill Bergan, Plymouth, Minn.

Eunice married Richard Anthony Pfliger on March 17, 1990, and has six
stepchildren: Gwen Bishop, Paula Graner, and Burton, Mindi, John and Jesse
Pfliger. Richard was born March 11, 1940, on a farm near Bismarck to Leonard and
Appolonia (Brown) Pfliger. Eunice and Dick had lived near Embden, N.D., for
nearly 14 years when Dick died on November 8, 2003.

Eunice worked for a variety of Federal Agencies, including Soil Conservation
Service, Farmer's Home Administration, Federal Crop Insurance Corporation, and
the Internal Revenue Service from which she retired in 1997. After that time she
worked for crop insurance companies including Great American and Fireman's Fund.

In the summer of 2004, she moved to Bismarck to be closer to her family, and
took a job with Farm Credit Services, Mandan, North Dakota.

Minnie (Seyfert) Philip

Minnie Seyfert was born on the "old Philbrick" farm south of Turtle Lake, North
Dakota. Her parents, George and Margaret Seyfert, came to Turtle Lake in 1910.
George was born in Nebraska and Margaret was born on a ship coming over from
Germany. Later the Seyferts moved to Mercer, North Dakota, where Minnie and her
siblings attended school. Minnie graduated from Mercer High School in 1932.

In Ruth Ovre Christensen's 1990 biography, daughter Pat Mohrbacker wrote the
following, "In her senior year, Ruth and Minnie Seyfert became good friends.
Minnie was the editor of The Cricket, the school newspaper, and Ruth was the
assistant. They both loved poetry and sometimes when they worked on The Cricket
at night they would read poetry and "waste" time in other ways. One night Ruth
didn't come home until 2 a.m. and Martha, her sister was worried sick. Their
teacher, Miss Bangert had been with them all the time, however. Sometimes Ruth
went home with Minnie after school and she especially remembers the delicious
cinnamon rolls Mrs. Seyfert made."

After graduation Minnie lived in Bismarck until 1938, when they moved to
California. She was active in community services, church groups and scouting.
She was a member of Bible Baptist Church in Vista, Calif. Minnie had three
children, Jeanne Wells, Connie and Peter and many grandchildren.

Minnie's sister, Lillian Seyfert, also graduated in 1932. She married Fred
Meiers in 1933. They lived in Bismarck for eight years and then moved to
California in 1941. They lived at Oceanside and had one son, Frederick William
Jr. Lillian is deceased.

Minnie was widowed in 1958. After several years she moved to Indio, Calif. In
1972 she came out of retirement and worked until 1976 when she had open-heart
surgery. Health problems caused her to retire permanently after that. She lived
at San Clemente, Calif., in 1980. She died April 22, 1990. Minnie wrote the
following poem in her book "Portraits," published in 1983 in Carlsbad, Calif.

  God has given many blessings
  In so many different ways,
  And for those we come professing
  Adoration, thanks and praise.

  Priceless are the gifts He's given
  With one word foundation laid,
  Lofty mountains, vales and heaven
  From a void of darkness made.

  But the gift most deeply treasured
  Is a love that never ends,
  Which by time is tested, measured,
  In the hearts of Christian friends,

  Love that is but the reflection
  Of a greater love - our Lord's
  As he binds in deep affection
  Hearts, with friendship's golden cords.

Edward & Lillian (Carlson) Plowman

Edward Plowman was a realtor in Mercer. He was born in 1883 in Missouri and was
a landowner/homesteader in Holmes Township.

He married Lillian Carlson who came from Wisconsin to teach in the Mercer
District. Their son, James, was born in Mercer.

Lillian's father, Gustav Carlson, lived with the family in Mercer. He was an
emmigrant from Sweden who came to America in 1886.

This information is from items in the Mercer Telegram, the 1910 and 1920 US
Census.

Earl Albert & Rose (Mayer) Postel

Earl Albert Postal was born in Independence, Iowa, around 1905 or 1906. Earl
homesteaded and built a small shack north of Mercer. Rose and Earl were married
in 1914 or 1915. He eventually built a house north of his homestead claim. The
house was very small at first but they kept adding to it. Six children were
born to Earl and Rose in that house.

        Photo: (Above, from left) Maletta Rauser, Laura Anna Postel, Echo
        Peterson, and Dorothy Postel on Medicine Hill Rock

        Photo: (From left) Herb Rauser, Richard Postel and Elsie Postel.

        Photo: In Seattle, about 1943, (from left) Dorothy, Richard, Elsie,
        Lawrence and Laura.

Rose Mayer was born in Romania. Her parents moved to Ellendale, North Dakota,
when she was a baby. She came to Mercer when she was in her teens and lived
with her sister, Katherine, who was married to Jake Skaley. Rose lived with
Katherine for about a year. She went to work at the Turtle Lake Hotel making
beds and cleaning rooms. While Rose lived with her sister, they went to country
dances. Rose met Earl Albert Postel at one of the country dances.

Rose and Earl had six children; Evelyn (died in 1928 at about 12 years of age),
Richard (born1918), Elsie (born 1919), Dorothy (born 1921), Laura Anna (born
1922), and Lawrence (born 1925).

Richard stayed on the farm and continued to farm the land until his retirement.
He married Lolly.

Dorothy lived with Richard on the farm.

Laura Anna is the only child still living. She was born on December 29, 1922.
Laura Anna Postel married Olie Jacobsohey had three sons; Elwood,
Bremerton, Wash., (born 1951), Dean, Spokan. Tne, Wash., (born 1955), Wayne, Port
Orchard, Wash., (born 1958).

Ernest & Rose (Blatter) Presser

Ernest Presser was born Jan. 1, 1908. He is one of the 12 children born to the
late Konrad and Marie Fiesel Presser.

Rose was a daughter of the late Christ and Elizabeth Rieb Blotter. She was born
March 10, 1913. She was raised on her parent's farm 24 miles northwest of Turtle
Lake in the Benedict area.

Rose remembers the fun and excitement she and the other school children had.
They would sleigh in the evenings on homemade sleighs, play
Anti-I-Over-the-Shanty and baseball at school, walk long distances to visit the
neighbors and ride in horse drawn sleighs in the winter with the bells on the
harness jingling merrily.

Ernest and Rose were married Nov. 21, 1934. Ernest had a Model A Ford that took
them for many rides, even through a lot of snow.

On drives through the countryside they could see the progress being made in
clearing land for farming. The many rock piles meant that the forefathers and
their families had worked hard with picks and crowbars to prepare the land. The
rockpickers and various other machines came at a much later date.

Rose remembers the baking and cooking that was done on a coal/wood cook stove.
The coal was put in one side and the ashes removed from the other side. Only the
bare necessities were on the market, so everyone had a big garden, butchered
their own meat, milked cows, separated the milk and made their own butter. There
was no "running water" in the homes, so they carried it from the windmill or
from nearby creeks. Their evening lights were kerosene lamps and later Aladin
lanterns, which were brighter.

Ernest and Rose had a gasoline lamp, which really seemed bright. After moving to
their farm north of Mercer, they had a wind charger plant of 32 volts, which
served them until REA put in electricity in 1949.

Four children were born to Ernest and Rose. They are William Dale on March 28,
1936; Marlin Ernest on Oct 1, 1938, (these two were delivered by Dr. Heinzroth);
Verna Mae on June 24, 1940, at Underwood by Dr. Anderson; Gary Eugene on Sept.
5, 1942, at Trinity Hospital in Minot.

The Presser children went to the first eight grades at country school. For high
school in Turtle Lake, William stayed with his grandparents, Mr. and Mrs. Christ
Blatter, Marlin stayed with his grandmother, Mrs. Konrad Presser. Verna and Gary
stayed in town during the school years too, although Gary did drive when weather
was nice and picked up others attending school on the way to Turtle Lake. There
was bus service to Mercer High School the last two years of Gary's high school
but he'd started at Turtle Lake and wanted to finish there so his parents paid
his tuition.

William went to boot training for the US Army at Fort Leonard Wood, Missouri in
1954. He was then sent to Fort Bragg, N. Carolina. He served 12 years in the
Army. He met Joan Hamilton at Washington, D.C. on one of his trips there. Joan
is from Richmond, Virginia, and worked at Washington, D.C. In August of 1956,
William and Joan were married at Bennetsville, South Carolina. Later they moved
to Newfoundland, then to Massachusetts, where Donna Marie was born on Dec. 2,
1957. She died on Dec. 16, and was buried at Turtle Lake. William and Joan were
later transferred to El Paso, Texas, where Dennis Wayne was born Nov. 10, 1958.
Debora Lynn was born there too on July 4, 1960. David Eugene was born in
Okinawa, Japan, on Feb. 19, 1962. William and Joan and family then went to
Travis Air Force Base in the U.S. and Douglas was born on July 5, 1964. William
died on March 14, 1973.

Marlin married Marlene Konapacki of California. He had served in the U.S.
Marines for three years. In 1969, Marlin and Marlene farmed near Mercer for a
couple of years when their trailer house and belongings were destroyed in a
fire. Shortly after that they returned to Haywood, Calif. where they live at the
present. They have three children, Debbie Renae, born Feb. 18, 1961, Mark Kevin
born Feb. 19, 1963, and Ronald Paul born on July 21, 1964. Debbie is a junior in
high school and Mark and Ronnie are in the eighth grade as Mark waited a year to
start school when Ronnie died.

Verna Mae married John Eikel and lived in Gladstone, Missouri, for a few years,
then in Tampa, Florida, where Tawn Jae was born April 6, 1971. Verna and Tawn
now live in Minnesota.

By Mrs. E. Presser from the McLean County Heritage book 1978.

Gary & Judith (Zingg) Presser

Judith (Zingg) Presser, the youngest child of Willie and Gordon Zingg; and Gary
Presser, youngest child of Rose and Ernest Presser, were married on Sept. 1,
1963, at Trinity Lutheran Church in Turtle Lake. Rev. Clyde Carelton officiated
and the maid of honor was Lavina (Fueller) Zingg and the best man was LaMont
Zingg.

Their first home was on a farm they rented from J.M. Dockter, 11 miles north of
Mercer. All three children were born while living there. Troy was born on Jan.
9, 1965, and was the New Year Baby for Turtle Lake that year. Trent was born on
June 29, 1966, and Trudy was born on Oct. 18, 1967. All three were born in the
Turtle Lake Hospital with Dr. Harald Kuplis delivering them. Mrs. Caroline Lynch
was the nurse for all three and she also delivered Judy as Dr. Heinzeroth didn't
make it on time.

The first years they farmed and milked cows but neither of them liked it, so
sold the cows and rented another quarter of land. It truly was a family farm, as
the kids helped pick rocks, haul bales and rode in the tractors when they were
doing the fieldwork.

Their vacations were camping trips to Crooked Lake and they did go to Canada a
couple times. One year while camping in Canada, they had a bear visit their
tent. They soon realized just how thin a tent is. Luckily the bear left but it
is a camping experience they still talk about and Gary shares with his
grandchildren.

        Photo: Gary and Judith at a Welsh chapel.

        Photo: The Gary Presser family: (back, middle) Judith and Gary; (at
        left) Troy and Annette and children Megan, Tyler and Heather; Trent
        (back, right) (at right) Trudy and Tom and children, Tatum and Turner.

All three children attended Turtle Lake kindergarten as Mercer did not have a
kindergarten, but they attended Mercer School until it closed in the fall of
1976. They were bused to Turtle Lake-Mercer School and all three graduated from
there.

Mercer School was a big family as classes were small so the teachers had time to
help each student and the cooks made homemade buns and cookies every day. They
even had German dishes like knoephla. The kids enjoyed Turtle Lake-Mercer School
too as there was band, tumbling and sports.

In January of 1974, Gary's sister's daughter, Tawn Eikel, came to live with them
until June of 1975 when she went to live with her mother in Burnsville, Tenn.
Tawn came every summer to be with them until her teen years when she was old
enough to help her mom in the beauty shop.

In December of 1974 they bought Gary's folks farm and moved there in August of
1977 and they still live there.

Gary attended grades one through eight at Medicine Hill Dist. #4 and high school
at Turtle Lake graduating in 1960. He helped his dad on the family farm for a
while then went to California to work for a short time. Returning to North
Dakota, he worked at the Peavey Elevator in Mercer; Darvin Fischer was the
manager at that time. Farming was his first love, so the spring of 1963 he
rented the farm from J.M. Dockter and they still rent the farm from Walter
Dockter.

Judy attended grades one though seven at New Home Dist. #3 and eight through 12
at Turtle Lake graduating in 1963. In the summer of 1963 Judy worked as a nurses
aide at the Turtle Lake hospital until she and Gary were married. She returned
to work there in 1986 until 1993 when she gave it up to become a full-time
Grandma.

Judy and Gary have three children.

Troy attended NDSU for a time, but decided he wanted to farm. He did work for
the North Dakota Highway Department for a while. He married Annette (Jorgenson)
on Feb. 9, 1991, they live northeast of Turtle Lake. Troy raises registered Red
Angus cattle and farms. Annette works at Falkirk Mine. They have three children:
Megan born Feb. 28, 1992; Tyler born Aug. 13, 1993; and Heather born Oct. 8,
2001.

Trent attended NDSU for a short time, then worked in Minnesota, attended and
graduated from Barber School there. He then moved to Hawaii where he worked on a
cruise ship for eight years. He moved back to North Dakota and attended BSC for
power plant technology and graduated. Being unable to find a job, he joined the
Navy and at the present time is stationed in Maryland where he works at Bethseda
Naval Hospital as a surgical technician.

Trudy attended and graduated from the University of Mary. She taught
kindergarten in Goodrich and then taught fourth grade in Menoken. She married
Tom Gunderson on June 26, 1993, and they make their home in Eden Prairie, Minn.
She teaches second grade in Shakeope, Minn. Tom has his own business as a
computer programmer and consultant. They have two children: Turner born on July
11, 1997, and Tatum born Aug. 25, 2000.

Gary and Judy have traveled in the United States and Canada and in 2003 they
went to Wales and Scotland.

Gary and Judy are members of the Trinity Lutheran Church, Gary is the township
supervisor and a member of the Turtle Lake Wildlife Club. Judy is on the Turtle
Lake Hospital Association Board and both were on the church council. They enjoy
their grandchildren and try to spend as much time with them and the rest of
their families.

Gary enjoys hunting geese, ducks, deer, elk or whatever. He taught the children
to enjoy it also and now takes his grandchildren out. It is a special time for
all of them. Judy enjoys her gardens and loves to read. She hasn't gotten the
hunting bug like the rest, but does go out for deer each fall.

Konrad Jr. & Marie (Fiesel) Presser

Mr. and Mrs. Konrad Presser immigrated to this country from Austria in 1902, but
each came at a different time and each came with their parents. Konrad Presser
Jr. was born in Austria on Oct. 18, 1879, to Konrad and Annie Eisenhower
Presser. He grew to manhood in Austria and immigrated to America with his family
when he was 23 years old.

Mr. Presser's brothers and sisters are: Caroline (Mrs. Joe Stadler), Frank
(married Sophie Mehrer), Annie (Mrs. Ben Kitler), Leo (married Marie Troyer),
Minnie (Mrs. Charles Mason), Louise (Mrs. Bill Eggebrecht), John (married Bertha
Neumiller), Minnie Mason, Louise Eggebrecht and Bertha Presser are still
living.

Marie Fiesel, born Aug. 18, 1889, was a young girl of 13 years when her parents
brought her to this country along with all her family that were born in Austria.
Her father was Joseph Fiesel and her mother was Caroline Wolf Fiesel.

Mrs. Konrad Presser's brothers and sisters are: Katie (Mrs. William Schon),
Ferdinand who died as a young man while threshing, Rosie (Mrs. John Weltz),
Caroline (Mrs. Frank Eggebrecht), Elizabeth (Mrs. Jake Ackerman), Annie (Mrs.
Mike Begonic), Joe (married Adline Ekart), Barbara (Mrs. Harry Peerboom), Lena
(Mrs. Herbert Johnson). Mrs. Elizabeth Ackerman, Mrs. Rosie Weltz, Mrs. Annie
Begonic, Mrs. Barbara Peerboom and Mrs. Lena Johnson are still living. Mrs. Lena
Johnson has remarried. The Fiesel family went to Hawley, N.D., and from there
moved to Martin, N.D., where they lived until homesteading 14 miles northeast of
Turtle Lake, N.D. The first thing they did was build a sod barn for two horses
and one cow.

On Feb. 1, 1905, Konrad Presser Jr. took for his bride, Marie Fiesel. On the day
they were supposed to be married, a bad snowstorm came up. Rev. Keller, who
lived near Mercer, was unable to get there so the best man went to get Rev. W.
Keller after the storm subsided. Because all the guests had arrived before the
storm they had to stay a few days before the wedding could take place. The food
supply ran out and there were no stores nearby so the wedding day feast was
pancakes and biscuits. There were no extra beds for the guests so they slept on
the floor. After the weather settled, the young couple moved to their own
homestead 18 miles north of Turtle Lake. The Presser's lived in a little shack
and the sunshine was not always in their lives. They, with many others, bore the
trials of settling on new land, without the conveniences of today. To the
Pressers were born 12 children. They are Albert (deceased), Ernest, Gust, Conrad
(deceased), Alvina (deceased), Marie, Annie, Herman, Esther, Reuben, Verona and
Leona.

Albert and Marie Blotter Presser have five children: Lois and Gerald Lutman who
have 10 children: Lyle, Lynae, David, Daneene, Pamela, Paul, Jennifer and Denise
and twins Mark and Michael  - all at home. Allen and Diana Godfrey Presser have
three children: Deanna, Allen and William - all at home. Leon and Mavis Elhard
Presser have two children: Belinda and Chad - at home. Lona and Pat Dinnell have
two sons: Monty and Michael - at home. Gloria Presser.

Ernest and Rose Blotter Presser have four children: William and Joan Hamilton
Presser have five children: Donna Marie (deceased), Dennis (in the US Army),
Debora, David, Douglas - at home. William is no longer with us, he was taken
March 14, 1973. Marlin and Marlene Konapacki Presser have three children: Debra,
Mark and Ronald - all at home. Verna and John Eikel have one daughter, Tawn - at
home. Gary and Judy Zingg Presser have three children: Troy, Trent and Trudy -
all at home.

Gust and Ruth Oltervick Presser have one son. Jerry and Janet Krause Presser
have three children: Jeffrey who is married to Debbie Neumiller and live on Gust
Presser's farm. Joan who is attending college and Jimmy is at home.

Conrad and Ida Bentz Presser have two daughters: Patty and Rick Martel who have
three children: Terry, Eric and Stacy. Karen and Dennis Schauer have two
children: Kim and Craig.

Alvina and Otto Bauer had one son who died in infancy.

Marie and Theodore Lindteigen had four children: Wayne and Shryll Borgen
Lindteigen have three children: Jolene, Lonnie and Jerri. Shirley and Elmer Skar
have three children: Randi, Tracy and Jay Dean. Donna and Kenneth Grabinger have
two children: Karla and Cory. Carvell and Paulette Belgarde Lindteigen have one
son, Christopher.

Annie and George Lelm have four sons: the eldest was stillborn. Kenneth and
Carol Peterson Lelm have four children: Lori, Lona, Lyle and Lynn. Vyron and
Jeanette Kraft Lelm have four children: Lonnie, Dean, Allen and Shawna. Jerry
and Charlene Schumann Lelm have two daughters: Allison and Jenny Ann.

Herman and Etta Rae Andrews Presser have five children: Charlette and John
Bonner have one daughter, Cindy. Gloria and J. Brown have one daughter, Lynn.
Larry and Betty Presser have no children. Carolyn and Ray Anthoney have one
daughter, Carrie. Douglas and Dianna Presser have no children.

Esther and Ernest Sondrol have five children: Sharon J. and Les Gerhing have two
sons: Blaine and a son who died in infancy. Elray and Lynettte Renfrow Sondrol
have two children: Ranie and Shawn. Clyde and Michelle Lanz Sondrol have no
children. Vicky Sondrol. Evon and Gordon Nelson have no children.

Reuben and Beulah Burchell Presser.

Verona and Jim Jameson have four children: Ralph and Wylene Parker Jameson have
two children: Angel and Richard. Jim and Sheri Streeter Jameson have one
daughter, Kelly. Vicky Jameson - at home and Dennis Jameson - at home.

Leona and Westly Snyder have five children: Ginger who died in 1972, Ellen and
Dan Woods, Peggy and Gerald Kraft have two sons: Kevin and Keith Westly Jr. and
John Snyder has one daughter, Dana, the youngest child was stillborn.

Konrad Presser died on Aug. 23, 1942, and Marie Presser died on March 2, 1963.

By Mrs. Ernest Presser, Turtle Lake. From the McLean County Heritage, 1978.

Edward & Wilhelminna (Ebel) Rauser

Martin Rauser, Edward's father, was born in Katzbach, Bessarabia, South Russia,
on Dec. 18, 1839, and Christina (Fiedler) Rauser, Edward's mother, was born in
the same place on Dec. 22, 1840. They later moved from Katzbach, South Russia,
to Cogealac.

Edward Rauser was born in Katzbach, Russia, on April 23, 1874, and his wife,
Wilhelminna (Ebel) Rauser, was born on Sept. 2, 1878, also in Katzbach, Russia.
In their early youth, they moved with their parents from Russia to Cogealac,
Romania. They grew up in this place to adulthood with very little schooling and
they were married on Nov. 16, 1895.

Living conditions were very simple and land was very scarce and thus they set
their sights to a new country, U.S.A. They arrived in the U.S.A in 1902, and
homesteaded about 60 miles north of Bismarck, N.D., in Medicine Hill Towhship.
Many of their relatives and friends came at about the same time.

        Photo: Wilhelminna and Edward Rauser

Twelve children were born to them, seven sons and five daughters, in the
following order: John, William, Lizzie, Martin, Edward, Henry, Gustave, Reka,
Benjamin, Rose, Minnie and Laura. The three older children were born in Romania
and the fourth one was one the way when they left Romania. None of the children
can ever imagine the ordeal they went through being on board the ship for over
three weeks with three small children, and then the long trip from New York to
Bismarck to begin a new life.

Their first dwelling was a sod house and while that was being built, they camped
out on the prairie, sleeping under a grain truck. As soon as they were able,
they built a more permanent house, which is still standing on the same place
today. The upstairs had only two bedrooms, and the walls were about four feet
high and then the roofline started. The center of the rooms was between seven or
eight feet high. The main floor had a fair sized kitchen, dining room, a small
living room and one bedroom. In this small house, 14 people lived very happily,
peacefully (most of the time) with much love, joy and understanding. There was
no running water in the house and no indoor plumbing. All the water had to be
carried in from the well with pails. Life was simple in those days, however, it
was also full of happiness and contentment.

The immediate family is as follows:

John Rauser was born on March 9, 1897, in Romania. He married Emelia Mollie
Knippelberg and they had four sons: Herbert, John, Roland and Ernold. They also
had 18 grandchildren.

William Rauser was born on Dec. 19,1898, in Romania. He married Mollie Reiger
and they had five children, two sons and three daughters. The sons died in
infancy, and the daughters are: Stella (Mrs. Ernie Adam), Melita (Mrs. Ruben
Fandrich) and Lorraine (Mrs. Peter Gravens). They had eight grandchildren and 18
great-grandchildren.

        Photo: (From left) Laura, Minnie, Rose and Reka Rauser.

        Photo: (From left) Gust, Henry, Ed, Martin, Bill and John Rauser.

Lizzie Rauser (Mrs. Jacob Berrette) was born in Romania on Sept. 6, 1901. They
had two children, Arnold and Bernice (Mrs. Jim Ressler). They had five
grandchildren.

Martin Rauser was born on Nov. 19, 1902, in Mercer, N.D. He married Lydia Russ
and they had one son and three daughters: Frieda (Mrs. Ed Bise), Deloris (Mrs.
Bill Pallesor),  Ieleen (Mrs. Ed Parson) and Minard. They had nine grandchildren
and two great-grandchildren.

Edward Rauser Jr. was born on May 22, 1904, in Mercer. He married Olga Meyer and
they had two sons: Norman and Marvin. They had three grandchildren.

Henry Rauser was born on Dec. 14, 1905, in Mercer. He married Ruth Fandrich.
They had three sons and one daughter: Duane, Carl, Grace (Mrs. James Pierson)
and Timothy. They had six grandchildren and two great-grandchildren.

Gustave G. Rauser was born on July 25, 1907, in Mercer. He married Sarah Miller
and they have two daughters: Jean (Mrs. James Collier) and Alice (Mrs. William
Bauer). They have three grandchildren and one great-grandchild.

Reka Rauser (Mrs. Emil Mayer) was born on Feb. 27, 1909, in Mercer. They have
three children: Norma (Mrs. Wilbert Wolf), Diana (Mrs. Larry Maynard) and
Delton. They have seven grandchildren.

Benjamin Rauser was born on May 3, 1910, and died on Feb. 5, 1912.

Rose Rauser (Mrs. Jake Presser) was born on Dec. 7, 1911, in Mercer. They had
six children, two sons and four daughters: Beverly (Mrs. Steve Heinz), Leon,
Erna May (Mrs. Bill Tayler), Jake, Betty (Mrs. Larry Sullivan) and Barbara (Mrs.
Angel Stalis). They had 17 grandchildren.

Minnie Rauser (Mrs. Frank Mantz) was born on April 10, 1913, in Mercer. They had
five children, one son and four daughters: Jennett (Mrs. Willis Hinsz),
Arvadelle (Mrs. Marvin Hieb), Arlene (Mrs. Don Collins), Gary and Shirley, who
died at the age of five years. They have eight grandchildren.

Laura Rauser (Mrs. Jake Mantz) was born on Feb. 21, 1915, in Mercer. They have
three children, one daughter and two sons: Evie (Mrs. Mel Schauer), Allen and
Larry. They had three grandchildren.

The 11 children of Edward Rauser had 40 sons and daughters and 93 grandchildren
and 18 great-grandchildren, a total of 151 people.

Carl Jr. & Louise (Kleingartner) Rennich

Carl Rennich was born November, 10, 1904, in Markawa, South Russia. He
immigrated to the United States with his parents, Karl and Christina (Engel)
Rennich in 1909 first settling in Turtle Lake for a year and then moving to
Mercer in 1911.

In 1929 he married Louise Kleingartner, daughter of Balzer and Katharina (Hofer)
Kleingartner. Louise was born December, 18, 1911, in Maxwell, North Dakota,
about 15 miles northwest of Mercer.

After attending elementary school in Mercer, Carl worked in his father's
blacksmith shop before going out on his own. He owned a large team of horses
which he used for threshing and moving buildings.

        Photo: Carl Jr. and Louise Rennich

In 1937, he and Louise along with their son Meinhardt moved to McClusky where
Carl was associated with the International Harvester Company as a parts man and
mechanic. Later he worked for Wentz Implement, also as a partsman and mechanic,
and Louise worked part time for Wentz Implement as a bookkeeper until 1967.
Carl was widely known for miles around as an excellent mechanic and machinery
repairman. He and Louise then managed the Oliver Trailer Court and Laundromat
until 1975. Carl and Louise were members of St. John's Lutheran Church.

Louise died on August 15, 1976, in McClusky and Carl died February 2, 1985, in
Turtle Lake. They had five children.

Meinhardt, born December 29, 1929, in Mercer, married Jane Lang. He was killed
in action in Korea on 3 October 1951.

Loretta, born September 22, 1933 in Mercer and died November 11, 1933.

Mervin, born February 1, 1938, in McClusky, married Joy Fleming; four children:
Michael, Steven, Patrick, and Joel.

Douglas, born August 20, 1944, in Bismarck, married Joan Vogelsang; died June
10, 1990, two children: Christen and Daniel.

Joann, born March 15, 1954 in Bismarck, married Darrell Dahl; five children:
Jason, Tyler, Janae, Travis, and Jackie.

Karl Sr.  & Christina (Engel) Rennich

Karl Rennich Sr., the son of Anton and Luise (Boerkirchert) Rennich, was born
Feb. 2, 1876, in Waterloo, Beresan District, South Russia. He and Christina
Engel were joined in marriage on Feb. 18, 1903, in Hoffnungstal, Odessa, South
Russia. He died on Oct. 2, 1933, in Bismarck. Christina, the daughter of
Friedrich and Julianna (Vogel) Engel, was born Nov. 16, 1880, in Fontal, South
Russia. She died Oct. 22, 1953, in Mercer.

        Photo: The Karl Rennich family: (front, from left) Karl Sr., Edwin,
        Christina, Emma; (back) Carl Jr., Richard, Amelia, Helen, Emanuel, and
        Johnny.

As a young man, Karl had been a non-commissioned officer in the Tzar's Army and
had fought in the Russian-Japanese War. He was a blacksmith by trade. In 1909,
he and Christina sailed from Liverpool, England, to Halifx, NS aboard the S.S.
Southwark. They immigrated to the United States via Canada with their three
oldest children: Carl Jr., Amelia and Emanuel. They settled in Turtle Lake. In
March of 1911, Karl moved his family to Mercer and opened up a blacksmith shop
that he bought from Tom Gardiner. Among his blacksmith skills, he also forged
cemetery crosses and cemetery lot fences and gates for area cemeteries.

In 2002, some of his cemetery crosses were featured in the Prairie Public
Television documentary "Prairie Crosses, Prairie Voices: Iron Crosses of the
Great Plains." He was the Mercer blacksmith until his death in 1933. Karl and
Christina are buried in the Mercer Hillside Cemetery, where a forged iron cross
stands over their graves.

Karl and Christina had 15 children, seven of whom died in infancy.

Carl Jr. born Nov. 10, 1904, in Markawa, South Russia, married Louise
Kleingartner, died on Feb. 2, 1985. They had five children: Meinhardt, Lorreta,
Mervin, Douglas and Joann.

Amelia, born March 10, 1906, in Waterloo, South Russia, married William Stute
and died Sept. 7, 1969. They had one child, Lenora.

        Photo: The Rennich family forged iron-cross grave marker.

Emanuel, born Feb. 8, 1909, in Waterloo, South Russia, married Elizabeth Brown
and died on Aug. 27, 1986. They had one child, Carol Ann.

Johnny, born April 4, 1911, in Mercer and died May 4, 1928.

Richard, born May 22, 1914, in Mercer, married Donny Morgan and died in August
of 1971. They had three children: Richard, Cleora Kay and Tommy.

Helen, born April 19, 1916, in Mercer, married John Corrigan and died in
childbirth on March 23, 1940. They had three children: Betty, Paula and Colleen.

Emma, born Nov. 3, 1918, in Mercer, married Robert Townsend and died March 21,
1998. They had four children: Robert, Jerry, Patrick and Michael.

Edwin, born March 3, 1920, in Mercer, married Elvira Jean Van Dewalle and died
on June 17, 1977. They had five children: Daniel, Victoria, Ronald, Gary and
David.

PFC Meinhardt R. Rennich

PFC Meinhardt R. Rennich was born Dec. 29, 1929, in Mercer to Carl and Louise
(Kleingartner) Rennich. He entered elementary school in Mercer and in 1937 moved
with his parents to McClusky. He attended the McClusky schools and in 1948 he
began working for the local Chevrolet dealer, McClusky Motor Co.

On Aug. 5, 1950, he married Jane Mae Lang of McClusky and they set up
housekeeping in a small unit behind the Moore Hotel.

        Photo: PFC Meinhardt Rennich

On March 26, 1951, he was drafted into the U.S. Army and completed his basic
training at Camp Roberts, Calif. After a brief furlough home, he was sent to
Korea on Aug. 13, 1951, arriving there on Aug. 28, 1951. He was a machine gunner
with Company G, 2nd Battalion, 7th Cavalry Regiment, 1st Cavalry Division.

In a campaign to give UN forces a favorable position should an armistice be
signed, Company G was ordered on Oct. 3, 1951, to take hill number 418 located
about 10 miles north of the small town of Yonchon. In the process of taking the
hill, Company C suffered over 90 percent casualties. Meinhardt was killed in
action by enemy fire. He had been on the front for 32 days.

His body was returned to the United States and on Jan. 24, 1952, a military
funeral was held for him at the McClusky High School auditorium. He was buried
with military honors in the McClusky City Cemetery.

John & Elizabeth (Wagner) Reuer

John Reuer came to America from Neu Glueckstal, South Russia in November of
1901. He was the only son of John and Louise (Wall) Reuer. He was born on March
17, 1879. His parents did not emigrate. John's father drowned as a young man
while working with a crew trying to break up an ice jam on a river. He left his
wife and five children. Their names are: John, Louise (Strobel), Christina
(Mertz), Rosina (Schlaht) and one daughter, name unknown. The later two remained
behind with their mother in South Russia.

John married Elizabeth Wagner on Feb. 16, 1898, in the colony of Berlin, South
Russia. They settled in Walworth County, South Dakota, near Bowdle in November
of 1901. According to history from the family Bible, there were seven sons and
two daughters, only two sons survived, John and Theophil.

In 1920, after living in South Dakota for 18 years, they moved to McLean County,
10 miles southwest of Mercer in Park Township. The farm was purchased from Fred
Wagner. A niece of Elizabeth's came to live with them for 13 years after the
death of her mother. Her name was Martha Schlafman. She married Fred Laib and
lived in the Mercer area.

In 1927, John and Elizabeth moved to Turtle Lake and son Theophil and Martha
remained on the farm. The land is now owned by Melvin Strobel. Elizabeth passed
away in July of 1932 at the age of 54. After her death, John married Rosina
Markel from Jamestown, N.D.

In 1936 John and Rosina moved to Lodi, Calif. John returned every summer to look
after farming interests. He drove to North Dakota by himself and didn't know you
could dim the headlights on the car. After a number of years, he decided to move
back to North Dakota and they moved to Bismarck in 1943. Rosina passed away on
Jan. 7, 1958, and John married Elizabeth Neigert Kies in 1958. She passed away
on Feb. 1, 1965, and John followed on March 11, 1965, four days short of his
86th birthday.

John Jr. married Emily Wagner. They farmed most of their lives next to the
farmplace. They spent a few years in Lodi, Calif. during the 1930's and later
retired to Bismarck. They have both passed away.

Theophil married Martha Wolt at Tappen, N.D. Children born to them were: Leo
married to Jean Freborg. They had three sons, Robert, Minot; Richard Riverside,
Calif.; and Leo Jr., Fargo. Leo was killed in an auto accident in October of
1953. Jean married Vilo Melhoff and they have both passed away.

Eleanor married Edwin Gessele and they farmed south of Mercer. Their children
are: Larry married Kathleen Pfahl and they have three children, Joshua and
Christopher, college students and Ann in high school Vernon married Mary
Tennessen and they live in Fargo. Mark passed away in 1994. Edwin passed away on
Christmas Eve, 1990. Vernon passed away September 23, 2005,

Idella married Ernest Neumiller. Their children are Gordon, married Joel'l Schon
and live in Stanton, N.D. Their children are: Emily, Fargo and Joey, Bismarck.
James married Tamara Blumhagen and they have three daughters: Lacey, Crystal and

Twins were born on Oct. 14, 1941. Doris married Lester Mauch who died in April
of 2002. She lives in Sidney, Mont. Dorothy lived in Detroit, Mich. and died in

Two girls died in infancy.

In 1956, Theophil and Martha moved to Bismarck. Theophil passed away on Jan. 7,
1971, and Martha in April of 1971.

James William & Gertrude (Martineson) Rice

James William Rice was born on a farm near Reedsburg, Wisc., in 1873. He came to
the Mercer area about 1903. In July of 1908, he accepted a position as a
traveling salesman for the International Harvesting Machine Co. In 1909, he
opened his own implement business. He also worked at the Mercer Elevator. In
August of 1909, he purchased the Dick Thompson quarter south of Mercer. In
September of 1909, he opened the Regan & Lyness Elevator and built a new house
in Mercer.

He married Gertrude Martine-son on Feb. 22, 1910, in Fargo. She came to Mercer
to see her sister, Mrs. E.N. Hedahl. She was born at Ada, Minn., on Oct. 12,
1885. Gertie taught school at No. 2 School of Mercer in 1909. She was a member
of the Mercer Women's Study Club. James Rice served in the 15th Session of the
North Dakota State Legislature, 1917-1918.

        Photo: James and Gertrude Rice

        Photo: The Rice family: (from left) Mary Ardis, Margaret Aileen,
        Gertrude, James and John Duane.

James was in poor health so they moved to Brownsville, Texas, in the fall of
1928. He sold his implement business that same year. They moved back to Mercer a
year later and this is where he died in 1939. Gertie moved to Bismarck and
married Leslie Rice in the 1950s. He died a few years later. Gertie died July
31, 1976. They are both buried in the Mercer Cemetery.

Samuel & Lena (Mehrer) Rust

Samuel and Lena Rust were both born and reared in Atmacha, Dobrogea, Romania.
Sam was born to Vernon and Louisa Rust on June 19, 1879. Lena was born to Jacob
and Carolina Mehrer on Feb. 23, 1883. Sam Rust's father was a miller and Lena's
father was a prosperous farmer. They were married in 1901 and came to America
the following year in February of 1902.

They never regretted this move, especially in the later years, when Romania was
taken over by Communism. There was much hard work and poverty, but they had a
strong conviction that the word of God should be taught to their children and
others also. As time passed and more people homesteaded near them, they started
meeting in homes for Bible study and prayer. Out of these meetings came the
organization of a church built in 1906. This is still in existence today known
as the First Baptist Church of Mercer. Samuel was deacon of this church for 51
years, served as pastor much of the time.

        Photo: The sod/mud house was built in 1903 by Sam Rust, Sr. on his
        homestead 11 miles north and one mile west of Mercer. His 12 children
        were born there.

        Photo: The Rust family: (front, from left) Jacob, Mary, Lena, Samuel
        Sr., Lydia, John; (back) Helen, Vernon, Katie, Sam Jr., Esther, Elvina,
        Andrew, and Erdina.

Samuel and Lena Rust homesteaded on a quarter of land 12 miles north of Mercer
where they lived until they retired and moved into Mercer in 1943. To this
union, was born a family of 14 children. Their first child was stillborn and
buried at sea. A 13-year-old son fell from a loaded coal wagon and the wheels
rolled over him and he died.

During the long winter months, Lena knitted and crocheted many an item of
clothing, sewed most of the clothes for the family and all without a pattern.
She belonged to the church missions society in which she shared her handwork in
many a bazaar. When there was a funeral in the community, the casket was always
covered with a wreath of her handmade flowers for this was her expression of
love and sympathy.

Samuel passed away on Jan. 4, 1959, and Lena followed him the same year on
November 4.

        Photo: Jacob Rust on his father's tractor in 1922.

Andrew & Regine (Mayer) Sackmann

Andrew Sackmann was born in Borodino, Bessarabia, South Russia, on Jan. 4, 1896,
to Johann Sackmann and Christine Sackmann nee Weishaar. The family immigrated to
American in 1898 on the "Kaiser Wilhelm Der Grosse," which landed at Ellis
Island, New York. From there the family went to South Dakota and settled on a
homestead near Bowdle, in the county of Walworth, in the township of Spring
Lake.

The family farmed until Andrew's father was killed in a haying accident in 1916
and his mother died in the 1918 flu epidemic. Shortly thereafter, Andrew and his
brothers John and Rudolph moved to North Dakota. Andrew's Uncle Christopher had
previously settled in the village of Mercer and was instrumental in bringing the
brothers to the area.

In December of 1920, Andrew married Regine Mayer, the daughter of Daniel and
Christine (Degg) Mayer of Mercer. The family lived in both the Mercer and Turtle
Lake areas, where their eight children were born. Andrew worked with his
brothers in the blacksmith shop in Turtle Lake, as a local farmhand, school
janitorial work and the WPA during the depression. In 1942 the family moved to
Washington State and settled in Startup, Wash. In the 1940s Andrew worked in the
Everett shipyards. After the war, he bought a berry farm and both he and Regine
worked for the Sultan School District.

Andrew died in 1958 and Regine continued to live in Startup among her family and
friends. She spent her final years in a nursing home in Moses Lake, Wash., where
she was visited and cared for daily by her twin daughters. Regine died on July
20, 1993 and is buried in Sultan, Wash., with her first husband Andrew.

Their children are (family histories are included) Vera, Verna, Laverne, Myron,
Donald, Ralph, Dallas and Douglas.

        Photo: The Andrew Sackman family: (front, from left) Douglas, Dallas;
        (middle) Myron, Verna, Ralph, Vera, Donald; (back) Regine, LeVerne, and
        Andrew.

Christoph & Christina (Peters) Sackmann

Christoph Sackmann was born Feb. 22, 1869, in Borodino, Bessarabia, South
Russia. His parents were Andreas and Eva Beutel Sackmann. He came to the United
States in 1891 and lived with his sister and family, Karolina Sackmann Obenauer
near Java, S.D. until he bought land in the area.

        Photo: Christina Sackmann

        Photo: Christoph Sackmann

He married Christina Peters who was born on Dec. 22, 1876, in Rohrbach,
Bessarabia, South Russia, to Andrew and Julianna Schneider Peters. She came to
the United States and the Java, S.D., area in 1887.

They married on March 5, 1894, in Bowdle, S.D., and lived on Christoph's farm.
In March of 1906 the family traveled to the village of Denhoff. In the McLean
County Heritage Book of 1978, son Julius described the arrival, "The depot was
still under construction when they arrived so they were unloaded on top ofa
five-foot snow drift! They managed to get to a little store and waited for Uncle
Carl Degg. He came in with a bob sleigh and took us to the farm which was one
mile north of Mercer. We lived there for several months until the house in
Mercer was finished." This house is believed to be the first family residence in
Mercer.

        Photo: The Christoph Sackman home in Mercer in 1924. The boy is Paul
        Winklemann, a grandson.

        Photo: Some of the Christoph Sackmann family: (from left) Christina,
        Edna, Ella, Nettie, Ted, Bertha and Tillie.

Christoph and his brother-in-law, Carl Degg, built the first livery stable and
Christoph operated it for two years. He then built the first meat market. Later
he also rented the hotel which the family operated. After operating the hotel
and meat market, Christoph worked for the Ed Hedahl hardware store. When that
business was sold in 1928, he returned to the meat market and operated that
until he retired in 1935.

Christina was one of the first women in Mercer and she died on May 8, 1960, in
Eureka, S.D. Christoph died on June 11, 1937, in Mercer. Both are buried in the
Mercer Cemetery.

There were 10 Sackmann children:

Emma, Ottilie (Tillie), Lydia who was born in 1898 and died in 1899 and is
buried in Java, S.D.; Bertha, Julius, Edward, Theodore, Annetta (Nettie), Ella
and Edna.

(See family histories.)

Julius was born on Aug. 12, 1901, in Walworth County near Java, S.D. He came to
Mercer with his family in March of 1906. He attended school in Mercer and as an

the United States with her family. At the present time she lives in Hettinger.

Leverne & Lorraine (Hodges) Sackmann

Leverne Robert Sackmann was born April 26, 1925, in Mercer to Andrew and Regine

Myron & Myrna (Ackerman) Sackmann

Myron Daniel Sackmann was born June 12, 1927, in Mercer. The family moved to
Washington State in 1942. Myron attended Mercer school and went to Sulton Union
High School and graduated in 1945. He was inducted into the Army and served
during WWII. Following his discharge he attended Everett Junior College and the
University of Washington.

In September of 1951 Myron married Myrna Jean Ackerman, daughter of Roy and Emma
Ackerman of Marysville. Myron worked and lived in Marysville, Spokane, Lynnwood
and Startup, Washington. His entire career was devoted to the Loan and Mortgage
fields. He also served for many years as commissioner of the Startup Water
District.

Myron and Myrna have two children: Mark Myron, born in 1956 and Marcy Anne, born
in August of 1958 and two grandchildren. Myron and Myrna are both deceased.

Ralph Sackmann

Ralph Gene Sackmann was born in Mercer on May 13, 1933. He was baptized in 1934
in Hope Lutheran Church in Mercer. He attended early schooling in Mercer until
the family moved to Washington State in 1942. Ralph completed his elementary
schooling in Startup and high school in Sultan, Wash. He graduated from high
school in 1952.

He served in the Air Force in England during the Korean War. Following his
discharge he attended the University of Washington where he obtained his degree
in 1958. Ralph spent his entire working career in social work with the
Department of Social and Health Services.

        Photo: Ralph Sackmann

Ralph never married and retired in 1996. In the year 2000 he moved to Arizona
where he died on Oct. 12, 2001.

Theodore & Marie (Walcker) Sackmann

Theodore (Teddy) Sackmann was born on March 4, 1905, in Walworth County near
Java, S.D. He was the son of Christoph and Christina Peters Sackmann. He came to
Mercer with his family as an infant.

He attended school in Mercer and spent his high school years at Phelan Academy
in St. Paul in preparation for attending the seminary. His dream of becoming a
Lutheran pastor was ended when he ran out of money. His son Wesley later became
a pastor - Ted's dream. He returned to Mercer where he worked in road
construction in Eureka, S.D., before beginning his life career in the grocery
business. He began his grocery career working in the Mercer Cash Store.

In 1942, the family moved to Eureka, S.D. where he was a part owner of a grocery
store with his brother-in-law Otto Just. He bought Otto's share in the grocery
store and continued as a grocer until he retired. Teddy died on Sept. 10, 1981,
in Eureka and is buried in the Zion Lutheran Cemetery in Eureka.

        Photo: Theodore and Marie Sackmann

Teddy and Marie Magdalene Walcker were married on Aug. 3, 1930, in Turtle Lake.
Marie was the daughter of Frederick Walcker and Louisa Klukas and was born on
April 21, 1910, in Parkston, S.D. Her mother died when she was 18 months old and
she was raised by her father and two older brothers. The family came to Turtle
Lake where Marie was educated and graduated from the Turtle Lake High School in
1928. She was active in sports and church activities. She died on May 10, 2004,
in Hermiston, Ore., and is buried in Eureka, S.D.

Ronald & Darlene (Schlafman) Sahr

Darlene Schlafman was born July 11, 1943, at St. Alexius Hospital in Bismarck to
Carl and Emelia Schlafman. They lived on the farm south of Mercer until Darlene
was three years old when they moved to Bismarck in 1946. They lived in Bismarck
until 1953 after the death of her father. Her mom remarried and they moved to
Jamestown where she graduated from high school.

She married Ronald Sahr in 1962 and lived on a farm south of Jamestown. Ron
owned S & S Wholesale Feed Business and Jamestown Hatchery. They moved into
Jamestown in 1987 where Darlene ran a daycare for 12 years. In the years of
raising a family, she also worked as an Avon Lady, school bus driver and in the
nursing home.

        Photo: The Ronald Sahr family in 1984: (front, from left) Darlene and
        Ronald; (back) Robin, Rodney, Racquell and Richard.

After many years of working in the church and involved in Gideon work, they
decided to sell all their goods and do what God had been telling them to do and
that is to tell the message. They got their answer when they were called to
South Dakota.

In 1996, Ron and Darlene moved to the Pine Ridge Reservation and took over the
mission church working with the Lakota Sioux Native Americans. Ron became an
ordained pastor of the Southern Baptist Church. They served there for six and
one-half years. In January of 2003, they moved back to North Dakota going to the
Mission Church at Mandaree. They are working with the Three Affiliated Tribes on
the Fort Berthold Reservation.

They raised three sons and one daughter but also took care of some foster
children.

Robin Sahr was born May 13, 1962. He married Lynn Olson on Aug. 20, 1988. They
live in Minneapolis, Minn., and have one son Christopher.

Rodney Sahr was born Oct. 4, 1963. He married Janelle Steckler on Nov. 26, 1988.
They live in Gordon, Neb., and have two children, Renen and Halie.

single.

Raquell Sahr was born on Nov. 11, 1969, and married James Novotny on Aug. 28,
1990. They have three sons: Dylan, Trustin and Wyatt.

Christoph Jr. & Olga (Just) Schell

Christoph was born Nov. 11, 1908, at Mercer to Rosina (Brandner) and Christoph
Schell.

Olga Mathilda was born to Katharina (Vossler) and Jacob Just.

They entered the first grade the same year at Park School south of town and
continued on through the eighth grade together.

        Photo: Olga and Christoph Schell Jr.

The years passed by and on March 11, 1931, they were married in the bride's
home. Rev. Huetmeyer heard their marriage vows. Their attendants were Helen
Singer, Esther Huetmeyer Emil Just and Christian Schell. They spent the first
two years on a farm owned by Christoph, two miles south of Pickardville. Then
they moved to a farm south of Mercer where they lived three years. Once again
they moved, this time to the farm east of town.

In 1941, they moved to Mercer where they owned and operated Schell's Hardware
Store for 20 years. They were members of Hope Lutheran Church and Our Savior's
Lutheran Church. Olga was active in church and Sunday school and Christoph
served on the council. He was on the town board for 18 years, was town cop for
five years, member of the Mercer School Board, president of the Brush Lake
Community Development Organization, member of the Sportsman Club and served on
the Board of Directors of the Turtle Lake Community Hospital and received a
lifetime membership in the association. He was also a rural mail carrier for
many years. Christoph died at the Bismarck Hospital on March 5, 1962, at age 53.

Olga sold the hardware store and their home in Mercer and moved to Eureka, S.D.,
where she was employed at the Lutheran Home for Aged until her retirement. She
had many hobbies and loved visiting in Colorado and being with her
grandchildren. She died on May 4, 1986, at the age of 77. Both are buried in the
Mercer Cemetery.

They had two children: Luella Jane, who was born March 12, 1933, and Tony
Eugene, born Oct. 24, 1936.

Christoph & Rosina (Brandner) Schell

Christoph Schell was born on Dec. 4, 1882, to Jacob and Katherina Bollinger
Schell in Glueckstal, South Russia. Jacob died in Russia on May 24, 1905,
Katherina and sons Christoph, Gottlieb and George came to America through Ellis
Island. The brothers Jacob, John and Fred had come to America earlier. Christoph
became a citizen on June 27, 1906.

Mother Rosina Brandner was born on July 26, 1885, in Bowdle, S.D. Christoph and
Rosina were married on Jan. 4, 1908, and they homesteaded five and one-half
miles south of Mercer in McLean County. They lived in a sod house until 1917
when they built a new house. Grandmother Schell lived with them until her death
in 1918. George also made his home with them from the age of eight until he was
15.

Times were hard but they were happy. When WW I was on, flour was scarce and
often they had to sift out the worms to bake the bread. The pastures were not
fenced in and the grass was tall, so many evenings, Rosina walked many miles to
find the cows. There were many prairie fires in those days. Many of these came
close to home and once they had gone through, it was hard to tell where they
started or ended. At one time a fire swept over 10 year-old George, who was out
plowing with horses, and he was severely burned. He was cared for by Rosina
because there were no hospitals nearby. You could not buy gauze so she used
white dishtowels. There were no washing machines and they were afraid that he
might get infection. The Lord was their strength and guide and George recovered.

During the winter of 1918, there was a flu epidemic and the Mercer area was hard
hit. Four year-old Emma died from the flu.

        Photo: The Christoph Schell Sr. family: (from left) Albert, Christian,
        Christoph Jr., Father Christof holding Martha, Mother Rosina with Otto
        and Emma.

        Photo: Otto Schell in 1942.

They lived on the homestead until 1941 when they moved into Mercer. On May 3,
1947, while preparing to plant his garden, Christoph died of a heart attack.
Rosina lived on until February of 1965 when she had a stroke and died.

There were six children:

Christoph Schell Jr. was born on Nov. 11, 1908. He married Olga Mathilda Just
and they had two children, Tony and Luella. Christoph died March 5, 1962, and
Olga on May 4, 1986. (See separate history).

Christian Schell was born in April of 1910. His first marriage was to Emma
Bender and they had two children, Dale and Phyllis. They divorced and his second
marriage was to Elizabeth Job Schuler. He had five stepdaughters. Christian died
June 11, 1984. (See separate history).

Albert Schell was born June 11, 1911. He married Regina Bossert on Aug. 30,
1936, and they had six children. Albert died on Sept. 27, 1999. (See separate
history).

Emma Schell was born in 1914 and died in 1918.

Otto Schell was born July 23, 1915. He attended rural school and high school in
Mercer. He was drafted into the Army and served at Pearl Harbor. After his
discharge, he worked for a telephone company. Due to an accident, he retired,
and from 1965 until his death in 1988, he lived in the Lisbon, N.D. Soldier's
Home.

Martha Schell was born Dec. 31, 1917, and married Alvin Schlafman on Oct. 17,
1940. (See separate history)

Ervin & Eileen (Laib) Schell

Ervin Schell was born Feb. 6, 1930, to John and Ida Gaub Schell in Mercer. He

Ervin married Eileen Laib, the daughter of Fred and Martha Schlafman Laib, on

After their marriage, they lived in Bismarck until 1953 when they moved to a

Gordon Schell

Gordon Schell was born to Ervin and Eileen (Laib) Schell on July 8, 1961. He

He presently lives in Mercer. He is a member of Our Savior's Lutheran Church and

John Sr. & Margarert (Deile) and Christine (Kramer) Schell

John Schell was born Jan. 24, 1880, in Glueckstal, South Russia to Jacob and
Katherine Bohlender Schell. In infancy he was baptized and instructed in God's
work in the Lutheran Church and was confirmed in the Lutheran faith.

In 1901, he came to the United States with his brothers and stayed in the area
of Eureka, South Dakota. In 1903, he came to North Dakota and homesteaded in
Edgemont Township, McLean County (now Sheridan County) and worked at different
farms around McClusky and Mercer. He began to work his own land in 1905, built a
house, barn and other buildings.

In 1905 he married Margaret Deile at Wishek. They had seven children: John
Schell Jr.; Julius who died at an early age; Gottlieb who died at the age of 17;
Hilda (Grosz); Frieda (Schindler); Elsie (Bossert); and Edwin.

He bought land in McLean County in 1916, which was two miles west of his first
homesite because it was closer for his children to go to school. He was
treasurer for Park School District #1 for many years.

Margaret died in November of 1918 during the flu epidemic. In 1919 he married
Christine Kramer and they had one daughter, Emma Schell.

John lived and farmed his homestead until 1945 when he retired and he and
Christine moved to Turtle Lake. Even in his old age, he was usually a healthy
man. He helped with the building of the new Lutheran Church almost every day
while it was under construction. While he was working at the church around 3
p.m. on Oct. 12, 1948, he said he didn't feel too good and was taken to his home
in Turtle Lake where he passed away about 5:45 p.m. of a heart attack.

His funeral service was at Zion Lutheran Church, rural Mercer on Oct. 18, 1948.
He had been a member since the church was built in 1906. He was the church
treasurer for many years. He is buried in the Zion Lutheran Cemetery.

Carl & Emelia (Laib) Schlafman

Carl Schlafman was born on May 22, 1897, in South Russia. He was the son of Karl
and Kathrine (Wagner). He came to America in 1901 and they lived in Heaton
Township in 1920. They moved and farmed in McLean County in the Mercer area.

He married Emelia Laib on Sept. 14, 1918, at Washburn. She was born on May 7,
1901, in South Russia and moved to America with her parents in 1902. They came
to McLean County.

Carl and Emelia farmed in Burleigh County, then moved to McLean County, then on
to Sheridan County in 1920. In the  1930s during The Depression, Carl kept four
families going by supplying them with a cow and some chickens. They moved to
Bismarck in 1946 where Carl worked at the State Penitentiary until he retired.
They attended Zion Lutheran Church south of Mercer. He loved his family and
especially his grandchildren. When he went to town he would go by Alvin's farm
so he would leave candy on the fence post out by the road for the grandchildren.
Carl died on Jan. 2, 1952. After Carl's death, Emelia married Emmanuel
Kleingartner. She died Nov. 3, 1983.

        Photo: Carl and Emelia Schlafman

on Sept. 1, 1923. Rueben was born on Nov. 22, 1924. Arnold was born on March 20,
1926. Eugene born on Nov. 5, 1934. Darlene was born on July 11, 1943. She
married Ronald Sahr.

Herbert & Irene (Neumiller) & Bertha (Lassie) Schlafman

Herbert Schlafman was born Dec. 11, 1920, in Wilton to Carl and Emelia Laib
Schlafman. He was raised in the Pickardville area and attended school there. He
worked on the family farm until he entered the U.S. Army in December of 1942. He
received his military training at Ft. Snelling, Minn., after which he was
assigned to the 1358th Military Police Co. as a military policeman in Normandy,
northern France, Rhineland and Central Europe. He was honorably discharged as a
Corporal in November of 1945.

After his military service, he returned to farming. Herbert married Irene
Neumiller on Dec. 31, 1946, and they lived on the farm south of Pickardville
until Irene's death in 1952. They had two children, Larry and Carol. He moved to
Bismarck where he was employed by SuperValu Warehouse for 30 years until he
retired.

He married Bertha Lassie on Dec. 5, 1953. They had two daughters, Brenda and
Mavis.

He was a pioneer member of Faith Lutheran Church in Bismarck, a lifetime member
of the VFW, American Legion and the Teamster's Union. He likes ice fishing in
the winter and also fishing in the summer. He is an excellent mechanic and loved
to tinker with cars. He enjoys summer vacations with his family, camping and
fishing on weekends. After his retirement he remained busy fishing and spending
time with his children and grandchildren. He will always be remembered as a hard
working man by family and friends, and especially for his crooked little smile
and the sparkle in his eyes.

Larry Schlafman, son of Herbert and Irene, was born on Sept. 30, 1947. He
married Anastasia Norstedt on March 20, 1971. They live in Bismarck and have two
children, David and Kari.

Carol Schlafman, daughter of Herbert and Irene, was born on Aug. 16, 1949. She
married Richard Roehrich on Sept. 7, 1967. They had two daughters, Paula and Amy
Jo.

Brenda Schlafman, daughter of Herbert and Bertha, was born on July 5, 1954. She
married Dwight Monger on Feb. 24, 1973. They have four children: Michael,
Sandra, Betsy and Kate.

Mavis Schlafman, daughter of Herbert and Bertha, was born Aug. 28, 1957. She is
single and lives in Bismarck.

John & Laura (Reiser) Schlafman

John Schlafman was born Sept. 1, 1923, to Carl and Emelia Laib Schlafman. He
grew up on his parent's farm six miles southeast of Mercer where he attended
rural school. As a young man he farmed and ranched with his father. He married

They farmed and ranched on a farm southwest of McClusky. In 1961, they moved to

dealership called the Lake Farm Store. In 1971, he began working as a truck
driver for the Lindteigen Construction Co. of Turtle Lake. He retired in 1984
and died on Jan. 11, 2001.

He was a handyman and enjoyed helping friends and neighbors. He had hobbies of
hunting, fishing and gardening. He was well known in the area for his pickles.

They raised four children: Melvin, Elaine, Linda and Loren.

Mark and Paul.
