Lewellyn & Florence (Hughey) Tewksbury

Lewellyn and Florence Tewksbury came to live on the former Fred Wanner ranch,
located eight miles southeast of Mercer, in June of 1954. Lewellyn was born in
Grafton, N.D., in 1928. Florence was born in East Waterloo, Maine, in 1930.
Lewellyn's father and mother, Warren and Nettie Tewksbury, purchased the ranch
and lived there a short time to help Lewellyn and Florence start ranching after
completing his duty in the Air Force.

Warren Tewksbury was a county extension agent in McLean and Sheridan counties
for many years. Nettie died in 1971 and Warren in 1993. Sheep and then
registered Angus cattle were the major livestock operations on the ranch.

Florence was a teacher in Mercer Elementary school for 10 and one-half years.
Florence was a member of the Mercer Federated Women's Study Club and has led a
Bible study for many years. Lewellyn was involved as a 4-H leader in McLean and
Sheridan counties for 15 years.

        Photo: Florence and Lewellyn Tewksbury on their farm in November of
        1996.

Loreve, their only child, was born in 1965. She married Madairick Harris in
1991. They have two sons, Matthew and Caleb, and reside near Chicago, Ill.

A major activity is the camping program started at the ranch in 1969. It is
called the "Box T Ranch Bible and Saddle Camp" and was started with the desire
to use the ranch to glorify Jesus Christ their Savior. The camps continued to
grow so that in the early 80s they retired from the ranching business and
devoted their summers completely to the camping program. This has progressed to
six two-week camps and about 120 teenagers each summer, who come to learn how to
ride a horse, learn the truth of the Bible and learn how to work. Thirty saddle
horses are maintained for the summer camping program. They have attended the
Brethren Assemblies most of their lives. See page 81.

Life in this rural Mercer community has brought many joyful blessings.

Christ & Olga (Olson) Thompson

Aalge (Olga) Agnette Olson was born in a log cabin northeast of Washburn on May
4, 1883. She was the first white child born in McLean County. Her parents came
to McLean County by riverboat with the Hudson colony. She recalled her father
leaving for work with the Great Northern Construction crew, working into Montana
and of her mother being left alone with eight children.

Often, she would take a pail of eggs packed in oats in one hand and a crock of
butter in the other and walk seven miles to town to exchange it for a sack of
flour which she would carry home on her back.

She recalled, at the time of the McLean County Diamond Jubilee in 1957, the
severe winters of 1890s when the snowdrifts of 15 to 20 feet deep covered the
ground for many weeks. Steps would have to be dug in the drifts at the doorway
to get to the barn.

        Photo: Olga and Christ Thompson in September of 1945.

She also recalled a terrible prairie fire, which burned the barn and granary on
her father's farm.

She attended school where the Everson School had been more recently located. Her
first teacher was Miss Lydia Staley of Coleharbor. There were about 12 pupils at
the time and a few finished the 8th grade. Her first church services were with
the late Rev. Diesen.

She could recall the visits to their farm of the Indians. Her mother would give
them lunch, and they would bow their thanks and depart.

At an early age she left home to seek work. She traveled by stage to Garrison
where she worked for a time, then decided to homestead. She filed on a quarter,
a mile south of Mercer. She lived there for three years all by herself. She
recalled the trips by horse and buggy, 25 miles away, to visit her mother.

        Photo: The children of Olga and Christ Thompson, Gladys and Herbert.

On Nov. 27, 1908, she married Christ Thompson at Washburn and they farmed south
of Mercer until 1932. They lived for two years in Washburn and then moved to
Mercer. Mr. Thompson died in 1956.

They were the parents of two children:

Herbert Russell, born Sept. 22, 1910, at Mercer. A farm laborer, he married
Martha Diede, of Pickardville, a teacher born Aug. 1, 1917, at Bowdon on July
12, 1941. They lived in the vicinity of Mercer moving from a farm into town.

Gladys Josephine Thompson, born Sept. 14, 1909, at Mercer. She became a
schoolteacher and married Austin Ness on June 2, 1938 at McClusky.

Olga Thompson died Aug. 7, 1961, at Mercer.

Haldor B. & Elisabeth (Osse)/Regina (Knudtson) Thompson

Haldor Bue Thompson was born Sept. 25, 1822, at Utne, Hardanger, Norway, to
Haldor and Regine Knutdtson Thompson. He married Elisabeth Osse also born in
Norway on June 24, 1835. After their marriage, they migrated to the United
States and settled at Hudson, Wisc. Three children born to them: Martha Helena
on March 19, 1867. She became Mrs. Lorentz Lorentzen. Thom Thompson, born on
Jan. 7, 1869. He married Bertina Bagley. Elisabeth Emelia, born on Dec. 8, 1870.
She married James Larmer, White Earth, N.D. On Jan. 28, 1871, Elizabeth
Thompson passed away leaving three very young children to care for.

Regine Catherine Knudtson migrated to the United States in 1871 from Norway
where she was born at Vestre, Wallesverd, on June 9, 1841. She came to Baldwin,
Wisc., where she was employed at a hostelry. She became the second wife of
Haldor B. Thompson, thus becoming the stepmother to his three small children.
She became the mother of four sons, all born in Baldwin: Knudt Oliver, born June
22, 1872. Helmer Bue, born March 19, 1877. Richard Walsaar, born April 24, 1879.
Christian, born Sept. 8, 1882.

        Photo: The H.B. Thompson old horse ranch, around 1888.

The family lived in Baldwin, Wisc., until 1885 when they came to North Dakota.
To encourage growth of timber on the western prairies, the government gave the
settlers an opportunity to file a tree claim. They were required to plant trees
on a quarter section of land and after a period of time could receive the patent
for it, thus becoming the owner. Mr. Thompson's tree claim was located on the
SW¼ Sec. 24, Twp. 145, R.81. He received the patent for it Nov. 23, 1895. He
also filed on a homestead, SW¼ Sec. 32, Twp. 145 R. 81 where he established his
home, It was located one mile north of Washburn and situated near a route the
Indians used when they traveled through the country from one region to another.
Many times they stopped in and were given food and whatever else the family
could give them for their wellbeing. When they did any trading and money was
involved, the joints on the fingers were used to indicate the amount of money
they expected to receive. They never rapped at the door when they came, instead
they would stand outside the house and look in through a window, when Mr.
Thompson would beckon for them to come in. It was when the family lived here
that son Christ remembered seeing a buffalo in the wild for the last time - a
large one walking down the road all by itself.

On June 12, 1905, Helmer B. Thompson purchased the SE¼, Sec. 33, Twp. 146, R. 79
from the N.P. Railroad. This parcel of land was located five and one-half miles
southwest of Mercer. Here the four brothers established a horse ranch and lived
together for a year when their parents came to live with them. Their father
passed away June 12, 1909, at home. Their mother continued to live with her son,
Helmer, after proving up on her homestead S½, SW¼, NW¼ SW¼, Sec. 34 on Feb. 18,
1914. She passed away at home on May 18, 1919.

Knudt Oliver married Lena Philbrick, Turtle Lake, who was born April 16, 1882.
They lived on his homestead NE¼, Sec. 34, Twp. 146, R.79 located southwest of
Mercer for a time, then moved to a farm south of Turtle Lake. He passed away May
27, 1935, at his home and Mrs. Thompson passed away April. 30, 1956, also at
home. There were five children:

Delbert Haldor, born Feb. 8, 1905, at Turtle Lake. He was a farmer and laborer
and now resides in Underwood.

Raymond Ellsworth, born June 20, 1907, at Mercer, married Irene Welch of Clyde,
Kansas, Feb. 17, 1945, at San Diego, Calif., where he was serving in the
Construction Battalion of the U.S. Navy. They still reside there.

Their daughter Carolyn Faye, born July 16, 1946, married Roger Compton, New
Baltimore, Mich. Children are Patricia, Melissa, Sharyl and Melody.

Grace Lillian, born at Turtle Lake on Sept. 7, 1908, a teacher on Dec. 7, 1927,
was married to Louis Holznagel, a farmer from Washburn, born Feb. 14, 1902. They
lived on a farm west of Washburn where their children, except the oldest one was
born.

Milton Louis, born on June 29, 1928, at Underwood, a farmer, married Lola
Skager, Beulah at Underwood on Oct. 7, 1951. They live on a farm west of
Washburn. Children are: Julie; Laren married to Joan Huffman, Minnewaukan on
June 5, 1976; Roger and Milo.

Harold John, born Oct. 16, 1929. An Aeronautic Specialist, married Janyce
Anderson, Washburn on April 29, 1951, and reside in Bismarck. Their children
are: Mindy, married to Tom McDuff, both serving as medics in the U.S. Air Force,
California; Wayne and has a daughter, Jennifer.

Elton Richard, a truck driver, born Nov. 19, 1931. Married Joan Young, Duluth,
July 16, 1953. Reside in Saginaw, Minn. Their children all born in Duluth are:
Kathleen, Colleen married to Roger Johnson, Sept. 6, 1975, and Lori.

Howard Eugene, a laborer born July 21, 1934, married Linda Thomas, Bismarck, May
22, 1972, and have a daughter, Deborah by a previous marriage.

Maxine Margie, born June 26, 1939, a secretary, on Sept. 4, 1960, married at
Washburn to Dr. Derald Rothmann, a professor in math at Moorhead University,
Moorhead, Minn. Children are Kimberly, Mark and Karla.

Marlene Mavis, born July 28, 1939, a secretary, married James Gerving, a farmer
from Glen Ullin in Bismarck on Sept. 9, 1961. Children are: Tamara, Glenn, Dean
and Allen.

Alida Fern, born Jan. 16, 1941, a secretary, on June 9, 1962, married Nick
Kassian, farmer from Wilton. Children are: Valerie, Kevin, Terry, Ladine and
Steven.

Doretta Grace, born Aug. 1, 1943, a secretary, married to Henry Rasmussen, part
owner of the R & S Oil Co. in Underwood on Sept. 5, 1964, at Birka Lutheran
Church, rural Washburn. Children are: Pamela, Denise, Nicole and Andrea.

Dale V., born Sept. 26, 1914 and was married to Mildred Barlow, Washburn. They
lived on a farm south of Turtle Lake for several years then moved to Pendleton,
Ore. Dale passed away on Sept. 28, 1973. His wife still resides there as does
her son, Sidney and his family. The other son, Gary and his family live at
Kennewick, Wash. Both boys were born at Turtle Lake.

Irma Berneice was born Oct. 20, 1916, at Turtle Lake. She married William
Rutter, Ruso, March 14, 1940. They live at Drake, N.D. Children are: Elaine,
Donna and Ione.

Helmer Bue married Mrs. Laura O'Connor of Leechburg, Penn., in 1911. She had
three children: George, Laura and Mortimer. The family lived on his farm
southwest of Mercer until they moved to Baldwin a few years later. In 1923, Mrs.
Thompson and Laura returned to Pennsylvania where she (Mrs. Thompson) passed
away on Dec. 6 of that same year. Her son George and daughter Laura now reside
at Eureka Springs, Ark. Mortimer is deceased. Mr. Thompson moved to a location
north of Bismarck where he lived until Dec. 7, 1956, when he passed away.

Richard W. married Minnie Merry at Fessenden, N.D., in 1903. She was the
daughter of the William Merrys, pioneers living on his homestead near Brush
Lake, north of Mercer. The Merrys relocated several times; when they lived in
Bismarck, Mr. Merry was employed by the Oscar Will Seed Co. putting small
cottonwood trees on sandbars. Mrs. Richard Thompson, who still resides in
Mandan, tells about a steamboat trip she, her mother and three sisters took up
the Missouri River to Williston where her father was working. When they returned
home they used one rowboat to travel in - the family and all the trees that had
to be taken back to Bismarck. At night they stopped to sleep in woods along the
riverbank. There were Indians nearby in the woods; only one approached then and
asked for tobacco, a frightening experience for the children. The Richard
Thompsons lived on his homestead the N½, SE¼ Lots 1 and 2, Sec. 28, Twp. 146,
R 79, for a time. They moved to a farm five and one half miles southwest of
Mercer. After a few years, they moved to Baldwin, N.D. In 1945 they made their
home in Mandan. Soon after this, the same year, Mr. Thompson died form the
results of a farm accident involving horses. There were three children:

Florence, a registered nurse, married John Helfenstein, in Bismarck, where they
lived until her death in 1929. There was a son, Richard, who lives with his
family in St. Paul, Minn.

Edith Regine, born Jan. 30, 1906, was a teacher. She passed away in McClusky in
1930.

Clarence Richard, born April 17, 1908, was a teacher, then purchasing agent for
the John Iverson Co. in Mandan, married Amelia Mayer in 1929, a daughter of the
Daniel Mayers who settled near Mercer in1902. Children are:

Haldor, a laborer, born at Mercer in 1930 married Orvilla Ereth in Mandan where
they still reside. Children are: Toni, Haldor, Bue, Frankie and Richie.

Dick, born at Mercer in 1932. Married Betty Henderschott in Bismarck. Is
employed by the N.P. Railroad, they live in Dickinson. Children are: Mary Jane,
married to Gary Ridl, Dickinson, patty and Richie.

Edith, married to Ray Leingang in Mandan in 1970. He is an employee of the
Mandan Schools. Children are: Danny, Ryan, Bradley and Aimee Ann.

Christian was married in 1908 to Olga Olson, the daughter of the Jens Olsons,
Washburn. She was the first while child corn in McLean County. They lived on her
homestead a mile south of Mercer for a year so she could receive the patent for
it. Then they moved to his homestead.

Herbert Russell, born Sept. 22, 1910, at Mercer. A farm laborer, married Martha
Diede, Pickardville, a teacher, born Aug. 1, 1917, at Bowdon, July 12, 1941. She
is presently serving as McLean County Superintendent of Schools. They live in
Mercer. Children are: (See family history)

Karen Jean, born Dec. 27, 1942, at Turtle Lake. A teacher, married to Roger
Boyko, Ruso, at McClusky, Nov. 23, 1961. They live on the Charolais Valley
Ranch, Ruso. Children are: Trent, Grant, Sarah, Kara and foster children, Monte
and Bonnie Malnourie.

Paulette Aalge, born Nov. 2, 1946 at Turtle Lake. Married David Cochenour,
Wichita, Kansas, Aug. 30, 1968. A son, Matthew, was born in Yerington, Nev. Both
are employed with the Dakota Adventist Academy, Bismarck. He serves in the
capacity of vice-principal and English teacher and she teaches business courses.

From the McLean County Heritage Book, 1978.

Herbert & Martha (Diede) Thompson

Herbert R. Thompson was born on Sept. 20, 1910, to Christian and Olga (Olson)
Thompson. Herb worked on the family ranch while attending the country school and
later the Mercer Public School. He found employment at various ranches in the
area working as a thresher. He worked in heavy construction as a cat skinner
(caterpillar) until 1941 when he married Martha Diede.

Martha was born on Aug. 1, 1917, in Sheridan County, McClusky. Martha was the
youngest of 14 children, the daughter of an immigrant German Russian farming
family. She learned the importance of hard work as well as the value of
education. Martha attended high school in both McClusky and Hurdsfield,
graduating from Hurdsfield in 1935. Following graduation, Martha took an
examination, which certified her to teach, she then embarked on one of the
limited careers then available to women. (See page 145)

        Photo: Herbert, 6, and his sister Gladys, 7.

After their marriage, Herbert and Martha moved to the Thompson ranch, northeast
of Mercer, where they lived for 17 years. During that time, they had two
daughters, Karen born in 1942 and Paulette born in 1946. Martha continued
teaching while Herbert worked as a rancher. In 1961, the Thompsons made the move
to Nevada where teachers commanded a higher salary. For the next 15 years, Herb
and Martha divided their time between Nevada and their home in Mercer, finally
returning to North Dakota permanently in 1976.

        Photo: Martha and Herbert Thompson.

Always an avid sportsman, Herbert used his skills as a carpenter and jack-of-
all-trades to maintain somewhat of a "floating" schedule, which allowed plenty
of opportunity for hunting and fishing. Herb served his community as a town
Marshall, city council member and auditor. For the past several years Martha has
been involved with volunteer work and teaching and assisting those with
disabilities. She is a member of Mercer Golden 50s.

Herbert and Martha have been members of the Turtle Lake Seventh Day Adventist
Church since the mid 70s. In addition to their daughters, they have been blessed
with grandchildren: Trent Boyco, Grant Boyco, Matthew Cochenour, Sara Klein and
Kara Frandsen and seven great-grandchildren: Colby, Christian, Chandler, Cadi,
Carli, Brady, Jacob and Gabriele (deceased). Members of this Thompson family
live throughout the United States - North Dakota, Texas, Nebraska, Minnesota and
Montana.

Herbert died March 11, 2003. Martha died January 21, 2005.

Friedrich Karl Sr. & Katharina (Kercher) Thurn

Katharina Kercher was born March 6, 1863, in Neudorf, Odessa, South Russia, to
Anna Marie (Kirschenmann) and Johann Georg Kercher.

She married Friedrich Karl Thurn on Nov. 24, 1881, in Glueckstal, Odessa, South
Russia. Friedrich Karl Thurn was born Oct. 6, 1856 in Neudorf, Odessa, South
Russia to the parents of Friedrich Thurn and Margaretha Obenauer.

Their oldest child, Friedrich Karl Thurn, was born May 13, 1883, in Neudorf,
Odessa, South Russia. They immigrated to America in 1883 and settled near
Eureka, S.D. where they lived for 15 years. They moved to Harvey and lived there
for six years. In 1904, Katharina and Friedrich and the children all moved to
southwest of Mercer.

Friedrich Thurn died May 15, 1921, and was buried in the Zion Lutheran Cemetery
seven miles south and one mile west of Mercer. Katharina went to live with her
daughter, Paulina and son-in-law, Johann Georg Singer. Before her death she
suffered a form of paralysis that left her almost totally helpless. She died
nine months after her husband on Feb. 23, 1922, from pneumonia and is buried in
the Hillside Cemetery in Mercer next to her son, Friedrich Karl Thurn.

Katharina and Friedrich Thurn had five sons and two daughters. Two sons had
preceded their parent's death. Their children were: Friedrich Karl Thurn, John
Thurn, William Thurn, Paulina Thurn and Lydia Thurn.

Friedrich Karl & Paulina (Laib) Thurn

Paulina Laib was born May 17, 1887, in Hoffnungstal, Bessarabia, Russia, to
Georg Laib and Christina (Weishaar) Laib. She came to America with her parents
on April 29, 1902, at the age of 15.

Friedrich Karl Thurn was born May 13, 1883, in Neudorf, Odessa, South Russia, to
Katharina (Kercher) Thurn and Friedrich Karl Thurn. He came to America with his
parents in 1883.

        Photo: Paulina Thurn

        Photo: (At right) Friedrich Karl Thurn, March 30, 1926.

Paulina Laib married Friedrich (Fred) Karl Thurn in 1907 and lived about six
miles southwest of Mercer. On Jan. 27, 1921, Friedrich (Fred) and Paulina were
visiting his parents when a fire started and burned down the house. None of the
household belongings could be saved and the children survived by fleeing from
the house. When the parents returned in the evening, the house was engulfed in
flames and the children were walking barefoot without almost no clothing on
their way to the neighbors. Then they moved into Mercer.

Paulina got sick and died Sept. 20, 1922, and is buried at the Zion Lutheran
Cemetery seven miles south and one mile west of Mercer. Friedrich (Fred ) Thurn
was then taken to the Fargo nursing home because of his health and died in 1935.

Friedrich (Fred) and Paulina had seven children:

Otto Thurn, born March 30, 1908; Willie Thurn, born Jan. 19, 1910; John Thurn,
born March 15, 1913; Emma Thurn, born Feb. 24, 1915; Louise Thurn, born Nov. 23,
1917; Walter Thurn, born March 21, 1919; Frieda Thurn, born Oct. 13, 1920.

John Thurn

John Thurn was born March 15, 1913, to Fred Thurn and Paulina (Laib) Thurn. He
was raised west of Mercer.

John died on March 18, 1923.

Otto Thurn

Otto Thurn was born March 30, 1908, to Fred Thurn and Paulina (Laib) Thurn. He
was raised west of Mercer on a farm.

        Photo: Otto Thurn, (at left)

Walter Thurn

Walter Thurn was born March 21, 1919, to Fred Thurn and Paulina (Laib) Thurn. He
was born west of Mercer. When his mother passed away, Walter was three years
old. His aunt Pauline (Thurn) Singer and uncle John Singer took him to live with
them, but after a few days it just didn't work out. So Walter and his sister,
Frieda, were taken to their aunt Magdalena (Laib) Schoell and uncle Fred Schoell
and were raised there on the farm. Walter lived with them until he was drafted.

        Photo: Walter Thurn

After his military duties, he moved to California. In 1983 to 1992, due to his
disease, he moved to Washington and lived with Leontine (Schoell) Olson who took
care of him.

Walter, after battling a long disease, died April 19, 1994, and is buried in
Washington.

Wilhelm Thurn

Wilhelm "Willie" Thurn was born Jan. 19, 1910, to Fred Thurn and Paulina (Laib)
Thurn. He was raised west of Mercer and was on his own at the age of 13 when his
mother died and all the children had to find a home. He went to 13 families to
work on the threshing crew and farms just to have food and a place to stay.

He then went to California in 1930 when times were really tough and lived in
cardboard boxes until he found a job in the vineyards. There he was employed as
a vineyardist. He later worked for the Thornton Cannery for eight years and
retired in 1975 in Lodi, Calif. He was a member of the First Baptist Church in
Lodi.

        Photo: Wilhelm Thurn, 1991

He served in World War II from 1943 to 1945 and was stationed at one time in
France.

His church and friends were very special to him. He passed away April 4, 1995,
and is buried in Lodi, Calif.

Brian & Allan (Haibeck, Rhoads) Tinker

Allan's grandparents, the Halfdan Berges, were early residents of Mercer and the
grandfather Halfdan was active in community businesses.

The grandmother Anna wrote the social news for the town for two newspapers for
many years also. She was an avid gardener, seamstress and church worker.

Halfdan and Anna's children were: June Fettig who taught school in Mercer for
many years. She married Matthew Fettig and they have three children; Peter,
Polly and Sarah. (See history).

Merle was a mail carrier, general handyman and mechanic who later moved to
Bismarck where he worked for the ND State Highway Department. He was married to
Doxie Noris who ran Doxie's Café after her husband Sam died and left the
business to her. (See family history on page 206)

Marion married Richard Haibeck and they lived north of McClusky on a farm until
moving to Jamestown to run the Starlite Motel in the early 1960's. They had
three daughters, Jame Meckle, Crystal Moser, and Allan Tinker.

Allan married Brian Tinker and they live on the family farm north of McClusky
and are both employed off-farm as well. Allan attended Bible School in Mercer
for 10-plus years at Our Savior's Lutheran. This holds many fond memories for
her, as do the continuing contacts with area residents.

Allan considers Mercer to be her hometown in her heart, although she later
graduated from McClusky High School in 1959.

Allan has six children; Jerri Van Sandt, Darcie Crumpton, Gable Nuckols, Nathan
Rhoads, Daniel Rhoads and Dakota Lasher. Brian and Allan have 12 grandchildren.

Allan is employed first and foremost as a farmer and as the current McLean
County Journal and McClusky Gazette Editors, simultaneously.

Allan is a graduate of the University of Mary and UND with degrees in education
and behavioral science. She also attended two years of law school at UND.

Gust & Emma (Thurn) Torno

Emma Thurn was born Feb. 24, 1915, to Fred Thurn and Paulina (Laib) Thurn. She
was raised west of Mercer. She moved to Lodi, Calif., in 1937. She worked for a
short time in the local (Lodi) cannery and vineyards.

On Sept. 10, 1939, she married Gust Torno at Lodi, Calif. Emma passed away May
21, 1974.

        Photo: (At right) Emma and Gust Torno in 1969.

Ancher O. & Noretta E. (Cunningham) Totdahl

Ancher O. Totdahl was born May 15, 1910, at Mercer to Oscar and Anna (Skomsvold)
Totdahl. He attended school in Mercer and graduated high school in 1930. He then
went to Minot State Teacher's College and graduated from Luther College,
Decorah, Iowa. He did graduate work at the University of North Dakota in high
school administration from 1938 to 1941.

He taught in rural McLean County from 1930 to 1932 and was a principal at
Scranton, N.D., between 1935 and 1937. He was superintendent of schools in
Pettibone, N.D., from 1937 to 1941 and at Beulah from 1941 to 1958. In 1951 he
was elected president of the North Dakota Association of School Administrators.
He became a fraternal insurance counselor in 1961 and a member of the State
Fraternal Congress as Lutheran Brotherhood underwriter from 1961 to 1972. He
passed away July 6, 1973, in Bismarck.

        Photo: Ancher and Noretta Totdahl

Ancher married Noretta E. Cunningham on June 3, 1937. Noretta was born Feb. 5,
1905, in Rochester, Minn., the youngest of seven children, to Mary (Golberg) and
Thomas Cunningham. Her family moved to North Dakota in 1907 and homesteaded on a
farm south of Scranton, N.D. After her father's death, the family moved to
Scranton in 1919. After high school graduation, she attended Dickinson Normal
School and graduated from Valley City Teacher's College in 1929. She then taught
school at Scranton Public School until 1937. She too taught school at Pettibone
from 1937 to 1941 and in Beulah from 1941 until retirement when they moved to
Bismarck 1961. She entered the Missouri Slope Lutheran Care Center in 1996 and
passed away on Nov. 20, 1998. They had no children.

Ludwig & Vivian (Scarvie) Totdahl

Ludwig J. Totdahl was born Aug. 11, 1903, in Turtle Lake to Oscar and Anna
(Skomsvold) Totdahl. He attended school in Mercer and graduated from high school
in 1923. He received his BA degree at Luther College in 1929, and a MS degree at
University of North Dakota in 1940. He was the principal of schools at Portland,
N.D. during 1929-1930, superintendent of school in Mercer 1930-1933, at Steele
1933-1944 and at Crosby 1944-53. He was a salesman from 1952 to 1962, 1962 to
1966 administration of nursing home and in 1966 to retirement he was employed by
the Social Service Board of North Dakota.

        Photo: The Ludwig Totdahl family: (from left) Vivian, Arne, Orval,
        Ludwig and Lorna.

Ludwig married Vivian Scarvie who was born July 7, 1907. Vivian taught at Mercer
school in 1929 to 1931 then became a housewife while living in Steele and
Crosby. In 1953 she went back to teaching until 1966 when she retired.

Ludwig died on June 12, 1984, in Racine, Wisc. Vivian died Feb 13, 1997. They
had three children: Lorna, Orval and Arne.

Oscar & Anna (Skomsvold) Totdahl

Oscar Totdahl was born Jan. 25, 1875, at Totdahl, Namdalen, Norway, to Ove and
Olea Totdahl. He was baptized and confirmed in Norway. After completing his
education, he entered military service, serving in the medical corps in the
Norwegian Army. He then married Anna Skomsvold who was born July 29, 1875, to
Mr. and Mrs. Jens Skomsvold at Oteroen, Namdalan, Norway. They were married on
Feb. 27, 1901. Two weeks after their marriage, they immigrated to America and
arrived in Minneapolis where Oscar Totdahl was employed for a year and a half by
the Milwaukee Railroad.

In 1903, they came to Washburn and after living there for a short time, they
homesteaded in Koenig Township, McLean County, where they resided for 37 years.
In 1940 they moved on a farm near Steele, N.D., where they resided until 1946
when they then moved to Bismarck.

        Photo: Anna and Oscar Totdahl

Oscar became ill in July of 1956, when they then moved and stayed with their
son, Ludwig Totdahl at Crosby. Oscar passed away Nov. 4, 1956. Anna then made
her home with her sons until 1959 when she entered the Bethel Lutheran Home at
Williston. Anna passed away June 15, 1962.

Oscar and Anna had two boys: Ludwig J. Totdahl and Ancher O. Totdahl. They also
had three grandchildren: Lorna, Orval and Arne Totdahl.

Gerald & Arlis Elaine (Laib) Tweeten

Arlis was born on March 14, 1945, to Edwin and Elizabeth (Bauer) Laib at Mercer,
N.D. She grew up on the family farm 12 miles south of Mercer with five other
children in the family. It consisted of two brothers, Ronald the oldest and
Byron, the youngest and three sisters: Darlene, Verdeen and Marilyn.

She attended grade school in the country, which was three-quarters of a mile
south of the family farm, and always walked to and from school with the older
children except in snowstorms when Edwin would take them by horse and sled.
There were always farm chores to do, like milking the cows, feeding chickens and
pigs and helping her dad at harvest time and in making hay. She remembers when
her dad would take the horses and rake and haul hay with them and feed the
cattle in the wintertime.

Her dad and mother believed in raising the family in a Christian home and so it
was to go to church every Sunday, even if it meant to start the car with the
horses pulling it in the winter. They only had two horses and they did the job
very well. She remembers hard times for the family, but through their prayers,
they have survived.

In the fall of 1957 at the close of the county school, she attended Mercer
School. She graduated from Mercer High School in 1963. Working in Bismarck after
her graduation, she met Gerald Tweeten during the summer and on Oct. 2, 1964,
she got married and lived on Gerald's folks farm. They started a family of their
own and had five children. They are Rebecca, the oldest; married to Curtis
Benedict; Gerald Jr., (Jack) married to Shelby Sellon; Troy, married to Jodi
Anderson; Darin, married to Christy Hirschkorn; and Quana, the youngest, married
to Richard Fiddler. Moving around with various jobs until 1980, they settled
back at Turtle Lake. The children all graduated from Turtle Lake High School and
have all married and given them 16 grandchildren.

James & Frieda (Thurn) Van Vleet

Frieda Thurn was born Oct. 13, 1920, to Fred and Paulina (Laib) Thurn. She was
two years old when her mother died and she had to live with John and Pauline
Singer. After a month they were not able to raise her so she went to live with
her mother's sister, Magdalena (Laib) Schoell, and Fred Schoell. There she and
her brother Walter were raised and educated about seven miles south of Mercer.

Frieda married James Van Vleet on Oct. 12, 1940. James was born Jan. 25, 1912,
to Elizabeth (Peterson) and Perry Van Vleet at Pickardville.

They lived on a rented farm north of Pickardville. Frieda loved plants and
gardening. She could make anything grow. She hatched out chickens the first year
they were married. Their first child was born north of Pickardville and the
other five south of Pickardvile. She was a great wife and mother.

Frieda started showing signs of ataxia at the age of 34, at this time no one
knew anything about the illness. She was sent to Minneapolis twice for tests,
etc., but it kept getting worse. When James's parents moved to Bismarck they
bought their place in Pickardville and sold the farm as James could not take
care of the farm and give Frieda the care she needed.

She went to St. Vincent's home in Bismarck in 1974 and was loved by all the
people there. She was alert until she went into a coma and passed away Jan. 18,
1976. She is buried at McClusky. Jim lived in Pickardville until 1996 when he
moved into an apartment in McClusky where he is living now.

        Photo: The James and Frieda Van Vleet family: (front, from left) Mary,
        Frieda, Anna; (back) John, Edmund, Marvin, James and Robert.

Children:

James Edmond, Marvin Dale, Mary Louise, Robert Perry, Anna Mae and John Anton.

Each of his children have married and each have two children so James has 12
grandchildren. Marvin served in the National Guard. Jim, John and Bob were in
the Army. Anna serves in the Navy. Mary served for a year or two on the
Selective Service Board.

Marvin & Lynn (Freeberg) Van Vleet

Lynn Freeberg is the daughter of Conrad and Evelyn (Norberg) Freeberg. She grew
up in Mercer and as a young girl worked at the Mercer Cash Store for her
parents. She graduated from high school in 1962. After graduation she attended
Bismarck Junior College receiving a secretarial certificate. She was active in
drama.

In 1964 she married Marvin Van Fleet from Pickardville. He passed away in 1995.

They had two sons: Scott (Pam), parents of one son and one daughter and Mitch
(Staci), and parents of one daughter. Scott and his family reside in
Bolingbrook, Ill., and Mitch and his family reside in West Fargo.

The family spends as much time as they can at their cabin at Brush Lake. Lynn
has been employed with the United States Postal Department in Sawyer, N.D., for
30 years.

David & Bonnie (Wagner) Volk

David and Bonnie (Wagner) Volk were married on Aug. 2, 1975. David is the son of
Matt and Isabel Volk of Selfridge. He was born Feb. 18, 1952, and was raised on
a farm near there. He is a Sioux County Commissioner and drives bus for the
Selfridge School.

Bonnie is the daughter of Fred and Louise Wagner. She was born May 8, 1952, and
grew up on a farm 12 miles south of Mercer. She attended the Mercer School,
graduating in 1970. She attended Mayville State College for one year,
transferred to Dickinson State College and graduated in 1974 with a BS degree in
elementary education.

The couple bought a ranch 10 miles west of Selfridge in 1979 where they continue
to live. Bonnie taught in the Selfridge School system from 1974-1979. She
decided to take a break from teaching and clerked in the SuperValu store for
nine years. She returned to the school system as a Title I teaching job, which
she is still doing. In October of 2002, Bonnie received the first time "Caught
in the Act" State Title I award for her efforts in teaching reading and math.

Dave and Bonnie continue to live on the farm even though they have had to battle
all the weather extremes of 110 inches of snow in the winter of 1996-1997 to the
drought and fires of the summer of 2002. They have three sons who enjoy the farm
and have been very helpful to their parents.

David Steven, born July 25, 1979, graduated from Selfridge School, farmed with
his parents and worked for area farmers, accepted a job in Mobridge, S.D., in
February of 2003 and is now living there.

Brant Allen was born May 12, 1983, graduated from Selfridge School, learned to
weld while working for a neighbor and is now busy making all kinds of cattle
panels, shoots, crowding tubs and repairing many things. He continues to live at
home.

Michael Frederick was born June 21, 1984, graduated from Selfridge School, busy
helping his parents with the duties of ranching and farming. He is also hauling
hay with a semi-truck and is waiting until he is 21 so he can drive anywhere.

Arley & Aletha (Gessele) Vossler

Arley Rex Vossler and Aletha Irene Gessele were married on Oct. 22, 1950, at the

Edward C. & Susana (Wall) Vossler

Edward C. Vossler was born at Wishek, N.D. on Feb. 22, 1900. He was one of eight
children born to Christian and Christina (Anhorn) Vossler. Edward, known as Edd
had two brothers and five sisters. He received his education at Wishek.

Edd married Susana Wall on Dec. 13, 1927. Susana, better known as Susy, was one
of three children born to Phillip Jr. and Katherine (Rueb) Wall. She had one
brother and one sister. Susy was born Oct. 21, 1907, in Sheridan County, N.D.
She was educated in McLean County. Edd and Susy were married at Wishek, and
lived there until the early 30s when they moved to McLean County. They shared
the original homestead of Susy's grandparents, and where Susy's parents were
living at the time.

Edd and Susy were blessed with seven children, four sons and three daughters.

Arley married Aletha Gessele in 1950, farmed 12½ miles south of Mercer, has two
sons, Kevin and Bryan, and two daughters, Tamara and Lori and one grandchild.
Arley died Nov. 15, 1985.

Leland married Eunice Hinsz in 1952, lived on the original homestead nine and
one-half miles south of Mercer. They have a home in Mercer. They have three
sons, Lamoyne, Michael and Todd and one daughter, Kimberly.

Deloris married Reuben Dockter in 1954, have one son Leslie and one daughter
Bonnie and one grandchild. They live just north of Bismarck.

Wesley married Verdelle Braun in 1955, have one son Darryl and two daughters,
Candy and Sherry. They live in Minneapolis, Minn.

Darlene married Roger Kendall in 1958, have one son Faren and two daughters,
Darla and Sharmin. They live in Bismarck.

James married Koleen Overbeck in 1964, have two sons Wayne and Gary. They live
in Bismarck.

Jeanne married Loren Soule in 1965, have two daughters Melanie and Mindy, and
two sons Matthew and Jason. They live in Bimidji, Minn.

Edward farmed with his father-in-law until 1943 when he purchased the homestead.
He was active in community affairs. He worked for ASCS and contributed much time
and effort into building the new Bethel (Evangelical) United Brethren Church in
Mercer.

He and Susy joined that church in 1953. That church merged with the Methodist
congregation and has disbanded. Susy also was a member of the W.S.W.S. ladies
group.

Edd died Jan. 21, 1955, of a heart attack, was laid to rest in the church
cemetery ten and one-half miles south of Mercer on Jan. 27, 1955. Susy had an
auction sale in the fall of 1955, and sold the farm to her son Leland and moved
to Bismarck. She then worked to help put the three younger children, Darlene,
James and Jeanne through school.

Susy retired from employment at the Drumstick Café in 1984. In 1999 her home on
14th St. was sold and she now lives with her daughter, Darlene.

Leland R. & Eunice I. (Hinsz) Vossler

Leland Vossler, second son of Edward C. and Susana (Wall) Vossler, was born Nov.
16, 1930, in McIntosh County, Wishek, N.D. At a very young age he moved with his
parents to Burleigh County, 11 miles south of Mercer. In 1934 he moved again two
miles north now in McLean County. Leland's family consisted of three brothers
and three sisters. He attended country school for eight years of elementary
education. In the fall of 1944, he enrolled at Bismarck High School, graduating
in 1948.

        Photo: The Leland and Eunice Vossler: (front, from left) Eunice, Kim,
        Todd; (back) Leland, LaMoyne, and Michael.

        Photo: The Vossler family: (front, from left) Savannah, twins Cooper and
        Brody; (middle) Renae, Eunice, Jocelyn, Katie, Sarah, and Kim; (back)
        Todd, Leland, Mike and Christopher.

That same year Leland enlisted in the U.S. Air Force, taking his basic training
at Wichita Falls, Texas, and later stationed at Cheyenne, Wyoming and Panama
City, Fla. He served one year, then returned home and farmed with his parents
until 1950 when he was recalled to active duty during the Korean conflict. At
this time he served another year. He was stationed at Walker Air Force Base,
Roswell, New Mexico. He returned home in September of 1951 and found employment
at Bismarck. He worked at Anderson Hardware, in the spring he again farmed with
his parents.

Eunice I. Hinsz, oldest daughter of Emanuel and Emma (Gessele) Hinsz, was born
Jan. 27, 1933, at her grandparent's farm home eight miles south and one mile
east of Mercer in McLean County. At a young age, she moved with her parents to
Pickardville, N.D., then back to Mercer east of town to the farm known as they
Roy Nielsen place. In 1936 they moved to Martin, N.D. and here is where Eunice
started the first grade. At age 10, the family moved back to Mercer. Eunice
continued her education in Mercer and graduated from Mercer High School in 1951.
While attending high school, she babysat for area families and later worked at
Sam's Café and Gardiner's U-Save food store. At the same time working on the
family farm helping where most needed. After graduation she moved to Bismarck
and was employed at Heulets' Grocery Store and Provident Life as a clerk filer.

On Oct. 12, 1952, Leland and Eunice were married at the E.U.B. Church in Mercer,
the first couple to be married in the new church with Rev. Edwin Werner
officiating. Following their marriage, they moved south of Mercer to a farm.
They purchased that farm in 1955. Here they raised their family, three sons and
one daughter:

LaMoyne, farmer from Mercer.

Michael, brick and block business from Mesa, Ariz.

Kim, Bismarck, a RN at Medcenter One.

Todd, heating and air conditioning business, Gilbert, Ariz. He is a Gulf War
Veteran (Desert Storm).

In 1982, Leland and Eunice built a new home in east Mercer. Leland continues to
farm. He also served on several boards, 13 years on the Mercer City Council,
five years as mayor. He also serves on the Baptist Church board. Eunice worked
part-time at the Schell's Food Market and other small jobs in the area.

In 1986 they started spending winters in Arizona and in 1990 they purchased a
winter home in Apache Junction, Ariz. They have nine grandchildren and one
great-grandchild, keeping them busy in the community, church and grandchildren.

Arvid & Donna (Fiedler) Wagner

Arvid was the son of Fred and Louise Wagner of rural Mercer. He attended the
Mercer School and served in the U.S. Army for two years. He then lived in Minot
and worked for a moving company and the Ward County Highway Department.

Donna is the daughter of Edwin and Mary Fiedler of Mercer. She graduated from
the Mercer School, attended Minot State Teacher's College and taught one year at
Renville Consolidated School near Mohall.

After the couple married, Arvid began working for Granite Springs and Donna
worked for Mann's Automotive and Union Insurance Agency. After Arvid was
transferred to Bismarck, Donna was hired by Kirschmann Mfg. Co. where she did
bookkeeping, production control and secretary to Mr. John D. Kirschmann.

        Photo: Donna and Arvid Wagner

Arvid later joined the North Dakota Truck Regulatory Department and in 1966 was
transferred to Hillsboro, N.D. Their first daughter was born during this move.
The family raised sheep as a sideline and Donna had many piano students while
staying at home with their new baby.

In 1971, they purchased a farm in the Mercer-Turtle Lake area, purchased more
sheep and started a dairy. The family was active in the Mercer Baptist Church.
Arvid served as trustee and then deacon for many years. Donna helped in the
music and teaching departments as well as the Women's Mission Group. Arvid was
part of the Men's Brotherhood and the couple served as youth directors for a
number of years and taught Good News Club in their home.

During the later 1970s there were some dry summers and severe winters. They lost
10 dairy cows in a two-week period due to frozen lung (according to the vet).
The substantial loss made it necessary for Arvid to seek additional employment.
He worked as a security guard at Falkirk Mine for approximately three years.
They sold the farm and moved to Mercer in October of 1981. Arvid then did over
the road trucking for Circle G of Bismarck. He also served on the Mercer City
Council.

Donna did part-time work at the McLean County Journal, Rust Manufacturing
Company and Prescription Design. She also developed a rummage shop called "The
New To You Shop" which operated approximately four years in conjunction with the
closure of Freeberg's Store in Mercer and the retirement of Evelyn Freeberg.
Donna then worked 11 years as receptionist and bookkeeper for Washburn Power and
Equipment until its closure in 2001. Donna has filled the office of Mercer City
Auditor and Assessor since 1984.

Their children all graduated from the Turtle Lake-Mercer school:

Tamara Marie, born Aug. 30, 1966, attended BJC in Bismarck, married Jeffrey
Schatz, is employed at the Bureau of Criminal Investigation. The couple lives in
Bismarck.

Timothy John Wagner, born June 2, 1971, was married to Sandra Hayes, employed at
Harvey Tire and is the owner of the new Buckshot Pheasant Farm, have one son
Cordell Wagner, they live in Harvey.

Thomas Arvid, born Jan. 20, 1974, attended Northwestern Technical College in
Moorhead, Minn., employed at AgChem, a division of the Agco Corporation, lives
in Mercer.

Tonya Marie, born April 20, 1976, attended Bismarck Junior College,, employed at
Young America, son Terell Lee Wagner, they live in Mankado, Minn.

Arvid passed away in his home on June 10, 1996, after five difficult years with
pancreatic and liver cancer.

Christ & Margaret (Weisz) Wagner

Christ Wagner was born Aug. 26, 1884, to Mr. and Mrs. Godfried Wagner, peasant
farmers who lived near a small German village Huffnungstal, Bessarabia, in South
Russia. He received a minimum education and served in the Russian Army.

On being discharged, he married Margaret Weisz in June of 1909, at Huffnungstal,
South Russia. Margaret was born Jan. 10, 1884, in Neudorf, South Russia to Mr.
and Mrs. Jacob Weintz

In the fall of 1909, they decided to join a group of people to migrate to the
United States. This group included his father and mother, his two brothers, Fred
and Henry and his adopted sister, Marie. With them traveled the Fred Fischer
family and the Jake Heil family. They had all received letters from Jake Wagner,
a cousin who had arrived in North Dakota earlier, telling about the free land
they could receive in the United States. The group went by wagon to Odessa on
the Black Sea to board a small ship which carried them to Istanbul. There they
boarded the South Arc, a cargo ship which journeyed to Liverpool, Eng. and after
a week layover they traveled to New York. The Atlantic trip took 13 days and the
seas were rough. After arriving in New York, they boarded the train, which took
them all the way to Washburn. They arrived Jan. 1, 1910. Their trip took them
almost two months.

The group all stayed at the William Wagner farm until they purchased farms. The
Wagner and Fischer families purchased adjoining land about 11 miles southeast of
Turtle Lake.

They were charter members of the Zion Lutheran Church in rural Mercer. They
retired from farming in 1944 and moved to Turtle Lake where they were members of
Trinity Lutheran Church.

Christ and Margaret Wagner raised eight children: Emil, Turtle Lake, deceased in
2002; Godfred, Turtle Lake, deceased 1990 (see separate history); Ernie, Turtle
Lake, deceased in 1987; Rose Swope, Turtle Lake, deceased in 1983; Caroline,
Turtle Lake, deceased in 1979; Amelia, Turtle Lake, deceased 2000; Margaret of
Bismarck and Edwin of Bismarck.

The Wagner's have 15 grandchildren and 21 great-grandchildren. Mrs. Wagner
passed away October of 1966 and Mr. Wagner passed away in September of 1967.
They are buried in the Turtle Lake Cemetery.

Godfred & Esther (Flemmer) Wagner

Godfred was the son of Christ Wagner and Margaret Wentz. They came from South
Russia with their parents and settled eight miles southwest of Mercer.

Times were hard; fieldwork was done in the early days with horses. The older
children, especially the boys, got very little schooling, as they were required
to help with all the chores. Godfred harnessed 18 horses at the age of 10. He
met his future wife while visiting and going to a country church. It was a long
way to church with horses, especially in the winter months when snow was deep
and no roads. Some of the neighbors would go part way and change horses. The
Wagner place was a stopping off place.

Eight children blessed their lives: Rose, Caroline, Emil, Godfred, Amelia,
Ernest, Margaret and Edwin.

As the years went by, tractors replaced horses and combines replaced threshing
machines.

Esther was the daughter of Karl Flemmer and Katherina Warner and one of 13
children: Christina, Christ, Martha, Phillip, Edward, Lydia, Walter, Marie,
Esther, Albert, Ruby and Martin.

Karl Flemmer emigrated from South Russia to Selby, S.D. There he met his future
wife, got married and moved to North Dakota where he homesteaded eight miles
southeast of Turtle Lake. Eight children were born there. Times were very hard
and they heard of the wealth in California so they moved to Lodi but work was
not so plentiful except in the fruit factories and odd jobs. Two children were
born in California, Esther and Albert. The family thought farming was better so
back to North Dakota where a farm was bought, southwest of Turtle Lake, there
three more children were born.

When Esther was a young girl, she had to help with all the fieldwork, mow hay
with the horses, help with the shocking of grain, running the header boxes and
threshing. She met Godfred while visiting at the Wagner place.

One day while helping her dad spread grasshopper poison with a '28 Chevy truck,
which was new at the time, she could barely see over the steering wheel but she
had to drive it. She was heading for home when one of the back wheels came off
and past her - she was so scared, figured she had done something wrong. She
didn't want to walk home, but decided it was the only thing to do, she didn't
get a licking.

Godfred and Esther were married in the Zion Lutheran Church south of Mercer.
They lived on a rented farm 12 miles southwest of Mercer. Here their son, Karl
(Kelly), was born. Their first years were lean ones. They milked cows by hand,
turned cream separator, farming done with horses. Esther always helped with the
field work too - run the horse drill, dragging the fields, walking behind the
drag until the second year, when Godfred bought a cart to hook behind the drag
to sit on. She did the family washing with a washboard. A few years later things
got easier, machine washing clothes, tractors, then combines.

One day Esther was pulling a swather made from an old header with an old John
Deere tractor when she came to a straw pile - the tractor started to climb it.
She couldn't turn any more, so she jumped off right into the path of the
swather. By the quick thinking of her husband, he raised the platform and turned
so she wouldn't get cut. The tractor tipped but everything came out all right.

In 1944 they bought a farm four and one-half miles south of Turtle Lake.
Gottfred died in 1990. Esther died March 24, 2003.

Kelly is in the trucking business at the present. He is married to Marilyn Ness.
They have two children, Kimberly and Thomas, and they live in Turtle Lake.

Taken from the McLean County History Book, 1978 and updated.

Johannes & Karolina & Christina (Schmidt Seibold) Wagner

Johannes and Karolina Wagner came to the United States from Hoffnungstal in the
Odessa Region of South Russia in March of 1902. They homesteaded 12 miles south
of Mercer. At the time, they had one son named John.

Three additional children were born to Johannes and Karolina who all died within
a two-month period from disease. They were Mathilda, born Oct. 14, 1905, died
Dec. 18, 1908; Heinrich, born Nov. 6, 1903, died Feb. 18, 1909; Rudolph, born
March 21, 1907, died Feb. 18, 1909.

Fred was born Feb. 22, 1909, just four days after the two brothers and one
sister passed away. Freida was born in 1912.

Johannes' wife, Karolina, passed away in 1916 after giving birth to twins. The
twins did not survive.

        Photo: Johannas and Christine Wagner in 1927.

Johannes and Christina (Schmidt) Seibold were married on Nov. 24, 1916. She was
born on Oct. 15, 1888. She came to Anamoose as a child and married Jacob Seibold
on Nov. 20, 1906. He died in 1912. Her children from her marriage to Seibold
were Robert, Roland, Minnie Spitzer and Lydia Braun.

Johannes passed away June 20, 1963, at the age of 87. Christina died in 1976.
They were members of the Mercer Baptist Church.

Son John married Emilia Neumiller in 1923 and they had three sons: Clifford,
Calvin and Marvin. They farmed most of their married life near Wing, N.D.

Fred married Louise Fischer of Hebron. They had four children: Arvid (deceased
in 1996) Arlis Lundgren, Donald (deceased in 1993) and Bonnie Volk.

Fred and Louise farmed the home place and later made their retirement home in
Turtle Lake.

Freida Brown has two daughters, Darlene and Donna (deceased). She still lives in
California.

Willa Juanita Lowe was born on Nov. 26, 1933, in Paris, Michigan, to Rev. M.L.

Jeff & Lori (Vossler) Walcker

Jeff and Lori Walcker were married on Oct. 22, 1982, in Turtle Lake, N.D. Jeff
was born on March 8, 1963, to Jack and Dolores Walcker. He was raised on a farm
northwest of Turtle Lake and graduated from Turtle Lake-Mercer High School.

Lori was born on June 24, 1963, to Arley and Aletha Vossler. She was raised on a
farm southwest of Mercer and also graduated from Turtle Lake-Mercer High School.

In their early years of marriage, they made their home in Turtle Lake where Jeff
was employed with Lindteigen Construction Co. and Lori worked at the Bank of
Turtle Lake. Their first child was a baby girl, Jill, born on Oct. 30, 1983.
Then came another baby girl, Lindsey, born on Feb. 24, 1985.

In November of 1985, Lori's father passed away so Jeff quit his construction job
and began farming her parents' land. On Aug. 6, 1987, a baby boy, Blake, was
born.

        Photo: The Walcker family: Lori and Jeff, Jill, Lindsey and Blake.

At this point Lori quit her job at the bank and the family moved from Turtle
Lake to the farm southwest of Mercer. The late 80s proved to be very dry and the
crops were poor, so the decision was made to start milking cows. They had a
grain and dairy operation until 1997 when the dairy cows were replaced with a
small beef herd. Jeff took an off the farm job for Garrison Diversion for two
years. In 1999 he took a full time job with Falkirk Mining Co. He and Lori
continue to farm and ranch on a smaller scale.

As of 2003, Jill attends college at Bismarck and Lindsey attends college at
Fargo. Blake is still in high school in Turtle Lake.

Norman & Vera (Sackman) Walcker

Norman Walcker was born in Turtle Lake on Oct. 4, 1921, to Fred and Ella Walcker
nee Heinle. He graduated from Turtle Lake High School in 1940. On Jan. 4, 1942,
he married Vera A. Sackman, daughter of Andrew and Regine Sackman nee Mayer.

Vera was born on April 27, 1922, and graduated from Mercer High School in 1940.
They were married at Our Savior's Lutheran Church in Mercer in a double wedding
ceremony with twin sister, Verna and her husband William Skorick.

The family moved to Washington State in 1942 and Norman worked in the Everett
shipyards from 1942 to 1945. He then went to work for Pacific Fruit and Produce
until 1950. Following this he went to work for Petrolane Gas Company until he
retired in 1975. After spending two winters in California, Norman passed away in
1977 while visiting in Turtle Lake. In 1985 Vera married Ken Zabel and lived in
Woodinville, Wash. until Ken died.

and Michael, born in 1954. The family unit also presently includes eight
grandchildren.

Vera Walcker Zabel spent her time caring for the family and operating a sewing
center in Sultan with twin sister Verna. The twins were also involved in the
making and selling of ceramics for many years. In 1985, Vera moved to Moses
Lake, Wash., where she presently resides.

Phillip Jr. & Katherine (Rueb) Wall

Phillip Wall Jr. was born April 23, 1883, in Russia (Kebulsky) to Phillip Wall
Sr. and Katherine (Scheuffele) Wall.

He came to the States with his parents in 1903 and settled in the Eureka, S.D.,
area for a short time, then moved to the Wishek, Ashley area. Phillip is one of
seven children, four brothers and two sisters.

Phillip married Katherine Rueb on Jan. 27, 1906. Katherine is the daughter of
Phillip and Caroline (Springer) Rueb and came from Kassel, South Russia, in the
early 1900s. She was born April 7, 1881. They also settled in the McIntosh Co.
area. Philip came to McLean County in 1905 with his parents to homestead eight
and one-half miles south of Mercer. After his marriage to Katherine, they lived
in Sheridan County for 10 years. Then they moved to his father's homestead where
they lived until retirement from farming.

They were blessed with three children. As Phillip's father had passed on,
Phillip Jr. named his first child, a son, Phillip Jr. and took for himself the
name Phillip Sr.

Phillip Jr. was born in 1906 and married Mary Geist. He died in 1934 leaving his
widow and four children. Mary passed away in 1939 or 40 leaving four orphans.
Phillip and Katherine then fostered these four grandchildren until they
graduated from high school.

Susana, born Oct. 21, 1907 married Edward C. Vossler in 1927. (See separate
history.)

Mary passed away as an infant.

They have 11 grandchildren, 32 great-grandchildren and four great great
grandchildren. They moved to Bismarck in the fall of 1943.

Phillip died in 1983 and Katherine in 1984.

By Mrs. Aletha Vossler, Taken from the McLean County Historical Book, 1978 and
updated..

William & Katherine (Hermann) Wall

William and Katherine Wall were both born in South Russia. Katherine was born
Oct. 11, 1882, and William was born Aug. 10, 1882. They were married on Feb. 28,
1901, South Russia.

They came to the United States in 1909. They stayed with a family south of
Mercer and a short time later they rented a farm south of Mercer. The house is
all that is left and that is ready to collapse. They got some land south of
Mercer west of the Zion Lutheran Church. They broke up some of the land, moved a
house on and added buildings as they could. Some of the land was fenced for
pasture.

        Photo: William and Katherine Wall and their children: (back, from left)
        Theophil, John, Lydia, Bill and Alvin. Not pictured: Rudolf and Mary.

They had seven children: Mary, Lydia, Bill, Rudolf, John, Alvin and Theophil.
Katherine and William moved into Mercer in November of 1944. Alvin and Ruth
(Gilbertson) took over the farm. William and Katherine Wall and their family are
all deceased.

Fred & Katherine (Sattler) Wanner

Fred Wanner, first child of Philip and Katherine (Leingert) Wanner was born on
May 7, 1883, in Kassel, South Russia, and came to the United States with his
parents as a small child in 1884. Fred was raised and received most of his
education in McIntosh County, North Dakota.

In 1903, the family moved to McLean County and in 1905, Fred struck out on his
own and homesteaded on a claim seven miles southeast of Mercer in Edgemont
Township in McLean County, now Sheridan. On Dec. 3, 1907, he married Katherine
Sattler in McLean County.

Katherine Sattler was born Oct. 13, 1884, the daughter of Heindrick and
Magdalena Hoffer Sattler. Fred farmed and ranched on a large scale for 43 years
before he retired and moved into McClusky, North Dakota, in 1948. In 1953 they
moved to Bismarck.

Fred and Katherine celebrated their 50th anniversary in 1957. They were faithful
and active members of the Evangelical Church for many years where Fred was a
trustee and a Sunday school teacher.

Fred died on May 11, 1962, at his home in Bismarck after a lingering illness.
Katherine died on Dec. 4, 1972, in the Bismarck Hospital in Bismarck.

They had nine children:

Emil Wanner (deceased), Robert Wanner, Martha Wanner Sifford (deceased), Ida
Wanner Wagner, Theodore Wanner (deceased), William Wanner (deceased), Phil
Wanner, Bertha Wanner, Charles Wanner (deceased).

Herb received his GED from the University of New Mexico in Grants, N.M., and
successfully completed his ministerial and Chaplaincy training. He is an

Dakota and Montana.

Minot Church of God.

Herb and Melvie reside in Minot.

Wanner Family History By Herbert (Herb) Wanner

The Wanner pioneers who settled in the Mercer, Turtle Lake and McClusky, N.D.
area at the turn of the 20th century and all who have lived in this area over
the past 100+ years are of the same family lineage. There are numerous Wanners
in the Dickinson and Hebron areas of North Dakota and in Estevan, Sask., Canada.
The relationship of the Mercer/Wishek Wanners with these and some large
settlements of Wanners in the State of Pennsylvania and New Hampshire has as yet
not been determined.

They are descendants traceable to Karl Wanner I. Karl was born approximately
1810 in Kassel, Province of Odessa, South Russia. This branch of the Wanner
family originated in Germany and are a part of the general German/Russian
families who migrated to the United States of America; and who settled in an
area then known as Dakota Territory. This migration took place over the period
of time from the early 1800s to the late 1800s. Coming to America and to Eureka
located in what is now South Dakota, was the farthest west the railroad went at
that time. Those that chose this southern route of the Dakota Territory
migration triangle ended settling in the general McIntosh County area.

The heritage of the Wanner family history begins with Friedrich Wanner who with
his wife Elizabeth (Bender) and other Wanner family members migrated to the
United States in October of 1884. Children who came with them were Karl Wanner
II, Phillip Wanner I, Caroline (Heuple), Elizabeth (Just), Christina (Knoll).

        Photo: Friedrich Wanner

While Friedrich didn't homestead immediately, his son Phillip homestead near
Zeeland, N.D. In 1901, Friedrich made the move north where he took a homestead
in Wells County (then part of McLean County) eight miles southwest of Harvey,
N.D. A few weeks later he transferred his homestead to son-in-law and daughter
Adam and Caroline Heuple. He then lived with them for a time, later staying with
son Philipp who had sold his homestead near Zeeland and moved north to purchase
what has become the Wanner family home place south of Mercer. Later this farm
was purchased by son Christ and is now owned by the Leland Vossler family.

Friedrich died in October of 1918 and is buried at the Bethel Evangelical Church
Cemetery near the Wanner home place south of Mercer. The location of the death
and burial of Elisabeth is at this time uncertain.

The family of son Phillip Wanner I greatly impacted the Mercer area with a large
family, most of who settled in the area. Phillip's first marriage to Kathrina
Liengart ended in Kathrina's death in 1897. Phillip was left with six children
under the age of 14: Fred, Philipp II, Caroline (Wolf), Katherina (Flemmer),
Madgelina (Bauer) and Christine (Wagner).

Fred married Katherine Sattler and established a sizable ranch located
approximately five miles southeast of Mercer. They had six sons and three
daughters: Robert, Emil, Theodore, William, Philipp and Karl. The daughters
were: Ida Wagner, Martha Sifford and Bertha Wanner. Robert, Emil and William
were well known local children. Robert was well known for breeding registered
Herefords, he is the oldest known living member of the Wanner family who settled
in the Mercer area. He was born on July 28, 1910. The Fred Wanner ranch was
later sold to the Warren Tewksbury family.

Philipp II married Susana Wall, they lived eight miles south of Mercer. Susana
died very young of cancer in 1917 leaving three sons, Alvin, Tobias and Arthur.
Alvin was taken in and raised by Philip Wall, Arthur was raised by his uncle
Christ Wanner and Tobias was adopted by Matt and Elizabeth Kiemele. Then another
tragedy stuck the family as Philip had now remarried Pauline Wagenman, when on
Nov. 20, 1918, he became the victim of the flu epidemic. They were parents of
Philip III who was born two months after the untimely death of his father.
Philip III later in life chose to spell his last name "Warner."

The other children of Phillip Wanner I were Carolina married to Christian Wolf.
Katherine married to Karl Flemmer, Magdalena married to William Bauer and
Christine married to Ludwig Wagner. All of these raised their families in the
Mercer area. Of these Christine (Wanner) Wagner also died during the flu
epidemic on Dec. 3, 1918, within a couple of weeks of Philipp II death. Phillip
I, following the death of Katherina (Liengart) Wanner, married Elisabeth Hotman,
the widow of Fred Gaub Sr. in 1899. She also had two small children: Fred Gaub
Jr. who established his family south of Mercer and Christina, who married John
Heim and lived north of Mercer.

        Photo: Phillip I and Elizabeth Wanner

Four children were born to the union of Phillip I and Elisabeth (Hotman) (Gaub).
These were: Christ, Jacob, John and Edward. Jacob, John and Edward (married Emma
Kurle of Mercer) made their homes in Lodi, Elk Grove and Sacramento areas of
California. Christ after a three-year stay in California established and raised
his family on the Phillip I home place south of Mercer.

Christ Wanner, the oldest son of Phillip I, was born at Wishek (McIntosh, Co.)
He married Christina Bonnet from the Mercer and McClusky area on March 20, 1918.
Christina had migrated with her parents Peter and Anna Marie (Kirschman) Bonnet
to the United States from South Russia in 1906. They first settled in Lincoln
Valley and later moved to the Prophet Mountain area northeast of Mercer. Christ
and Christina were parents of seven children.

John married Anna Marie Anderson, and they had two children, Judy and Gail. John
spent most of his life in Bismarck. During his lifetime he operated a
landscaping business, owned and operated a resort in Nevis, Minn., worked in
service stations in Bismarck and owned and operated real estate rental
properties until his death on April 11, 2000, in Bismarck.

Ruth married Anton Vogel and they had seven children. Anton serve in the Navy in
WWII. He and Ruth were in the real estate development business. They both died
in 2000 and they are buried in Bismarck.

        Photo: Christ and Christina and their son Ted and his wife, Laura.

        Photo: The Christ and Christina Wanner family: (front, from left) Helen,
        Christ, Christina, Marion; (back) John, Ruth, Lillian, and Herbert. Not
        pictured: Ted.

Theodore married Laura Settig on Oct. 11, 1952, in St. Paul, Minn. She died on
March 22, 1958. They had one son, Ronald, who died in October of 1974. Ted then
married Doris Mae Hohimer Herman. They have one son, Blair. Ted served in the
military, stationed in Okinawa during WWII and retired as a prison guard in
Bismarck where they reside.

Lillian married Reuben J. Bentz from McClusky. They farmed on Reuben's family
farm many years before retiring to make their home in Bismarck. Lillian is the
only one of Christ and Christina's children born outside of North Dakota being
born in California.

Herbert Harold Wanner was born Feb. 25, 1933, and married Melvie Ellen Lasher
from McClusky on July 20, 1956. They have three children and seven
grandchildren: Corinne Sayler, JoEllen Hallmark and Timothy. Herbert farmed with
his father Christ on the family farm and raised registered Hereford cattle as a
young man. He left the farm in 1957 to enter the ministry. For a time he and
Melvie owned the Mercer Café purchased from Doxie Norris. They retired from the
pastoral ministry after 35 years in 1993. Herb retired as Director of Red Cross
Disaster Service in April of 2001. Melvie has worked in sales and bookkeeping
retiring in 1999. They live in Minot. Corinne and Tim live in Colorado Springs,
Colo., where Corinne is an administrative assistant to Dr. James Dobson, head of
Focus on the Family. JoEllen lives in Indianapolis, Ind.

Helen Viola married Herbert Grosz from McClusky on Oct. 25, 1952. Herb and Helen
have one child, Vonnie Erdman. Herb operated the Mobil station in McClusky for
many years and later the Mobile Bulk Agency. Helen was an employee of Grenz
SuperValu and its successor for right at 40 years when she retired in 2002.

Marian Verlen married Otto Geigle on Sept. 4, 1958, at Mercer. They divorced in
1977. They had four children: Monica Schmidt, Lucille Klein, Sharlene Schuh and
Darin. Marian spent most of her life as a farm wife and housekeeper. She lives
in Anamoose, N.D.

Faith has been an important part of the life of the Wanner family over the
years. Many early records refer to the Wanner's religious affiliation as being
Evangelical Lutheran and in later years those in the Mercer area as being
faithful in the Evangelical Church. God, the Bible, the church and the family
are the only foundation upon which to build a life and future. The early
pioneers treasured these elements of truth and lived by them and today they are
still relevant.

Alexander (Alec) P. & Elizabeth (Jorgenson) Wardner

Alexander Wardner was born March 17, 1920, in Wilton. He was the son of Frank
and Anna (Kanski) Wardner. His dad came from the Ukraine lived in Canada for
awhile then settled in Wilton and worked in the coal mine. He died when Alec
was eight.

Alec worked for various farmers from Wilton to Mercer and in Sheridan County.
Alec helped his mother raise his brother and two sisters. His mother worked at
various Indian reservations. She died in 1970.

On Jan. 26, 1940, Alec married Elizabeth (Jack) Jorgenson. She was the daughter
of Louie and Dora (Davenport) Jorgenson. Alec and Elizabeth both worked for Doc
Ness in Pickard Township of Sheridan County. They lived in various places,
farming and ranching in Sheridan County. They bought the former Emil Wanner
ranch in 1959, which is five miles southeast of Mercer. They raised sheep,
cattle, horses and small grains.

Alec passed away in December of 1991 and Elizabeth (Jack) moved to the McClusky
retirement home in September of 2002.

        Photo: Alexander and Elizabeth Wardner

They are members of Our Savior's Lutheran Church, Mercer.

They had five children:

Richard was born in 1943 and he married Kayleen Mittlestedt at Killdeer. They
both retired from teaching school and reside in Dickinson. They have two sons:
Brandt and Julie have two sons and a daughter and live in Dickinson. Cory and
Mandie live in Bismarck.

Jerald (Frank) was born in 1945 and he married Marlene Monroe. They have two
children: Angela and Cody. (See separate history.)

Robert (Bob) was born in 1949 and married Karen Aune in Bismarck. They lived
south of Bismarck. Bob passed away in November of 1987. They have two children:
Jennifer and her daughter Shayla live south of Bismarck; John lives south of
Bismarck.

Ronald (Ron) was born in 1954. He married Sue Nathan. They live west of Turtle
Lake. They have three children who all attend Turtle Lake-Mercer school: Jay,
Sadie and Kyle.

Beverly (Bev) was born in 1956 and is married to Clark Jesz. They live in Turtle

School.

Jerald "Frank" & Marlene (Monroe) Wardner

Jerald (Frank) Wardner married Marlene Monroe in June of 1970, who was the
daughter of Wayne and Marion (Chase) Monroe from Baldwin. They purchased the
farm from Alec and Elizabeth and have continued with farming and ranching.

        Photo: The Frank Wardner family: (from left) Cody, Angela, Marlene and

James Roscoe & Margaret Jane (Jones) Washburn

James Roscoe Washburn and family were early residents of Mercer. J.R. was born
on May 25, 1853, in Jackson, Mich. He was the son of George and Lucy Young
Washburn. His mother died when he was six years old and he was raised by his
maternal grandparents. At age 13, he helped drive a large flock of sheep from
his home in Michigan to the Missouri Ozarks. He stayed there with the sheep
through the winter.

When he was 20 years old, he moved to Iowa and there he met and married Margaret
Jane (Maggie) Jones on Feb. 8, 1880, in Red Oak, Iowa. Three years later they
traveled by covered wagon to the virgin prairie of northwestern Nebraska in
Wayne County.

In 1902, J.R. and his son, Ira, took adjoining homesteads in Pickard Township,
McLean County (later Sheridan County). In 1906, the family left Nebraska to live
on their homestead. In 1913 the family moved into Mercer where they ran a dray
line, had a butcher shop, water delivery and cream station.

The family was active in the Lutheran Church. Mr. Washburn died in 1940 and Mrs.
Washburn died a year later. They had 10 children: twins sons who died at birth
and Ira, Mae, Ida (Martin Ness), Harvey, Adeline (C.B. Nielsen), Cora (E.M.
Shirts), Loren and Edwin who died in 1918.

Compiled from obituary.

Mae Washburn

Mae Washburn, the daughter of James R. and Margaret Jones Washburn, was born on
July 8, 1883, in Winside, Neb. She attended Wayne Teacher's College in Nebraska.
She came to rural Mercer in 1906 to join her parents and moved to Mercer with
them in 1913. She also attended Minot and Valley City State Teacher's Colleges.
She taught for many years in McClusky, Hurdsfield and the Mercer rural schools.

She served as clerk of the Mercer School Board and was the organizer and first
president of the Mercer Women's Study Club. She was an active member of Our
Savior's Lutheran Church.

She died on Oct. 24, 1949, in Washburn at the home of her sister, Ida (Martin
Ness), and is buried in the Mercer Cemetery.

This information is compiled from her obituary.

Martin & Ingeborg (Akre) Wassenberg

Martin George Wassenberg was born February 10, 1884, at Rushville near Chadron,
Sheridan County, Nebraska, to Lawrence "Frank" Wassenberg and Mary Jane
Heesacker. Martin filed on a claim in Prophet Township in Section 15 and 22 in
August of 1907. He proved it up by commutation in April of 1909 with Carl
Vandercook and John Thurlow as his witnesses before Judge Dunning in McClusky.
His homestead patent number is 465936.

In the spring of 1908, Martin broke up the block north of the Mercer railroad
depot to develop it into a town park. The Mercer Commercial Club planted the
trees there.

The April 9, 1909, Mercer Telegram reported, "J.M. Wassenberg was a passenger of
Rochester, Minnesota, Tuesday where Mrs. Wassenberg has been receiving medical
treatment. Mr. and Mrs. Wassenberg will return the latter part of the week."
Perhaps this was Martin's brother.

The May 21, 1909, Mercer Telegram reported, "The saw mill at the lumber yard (in
Mercer) has been going full blast. Martin Wassenberg and Ted Knutson are running
it."

Martin fractured three ribs and strained his back when he fell through a hay
rack at McHenry while helping his brother haul hay in June of 1909, according to
the Telegram. He spent two weeks recovering with relatives.

        Photo: Martin Wassenberg

        Photo: Belle (Akre) Wassenberg

In October of 1909, Martin left for Rushville, Nebraska, his hometown, to spend
the winter. "Dutch" (as he was called) said he intended to bring back a carload
of horses with him in the spring.

The following March he returned with the horses. That spring he accepted the
position as Foreman of the Olesen Well Digging Company and, with Harry Peterson,
they started digging wells, including one for Christ Lockrem.

On January 24, 1911, Martin married Ingeborg "Belle" Marie Akre at her sister's,
Hattie Ovre's home north of Mercer. Rev. Fladmark, a Lutheran minster from
Whiprud, North Dakota, officiated. Martin's neighbor, George Howell, was best
man, and Miss Alma Imdahl was the bridesmaid.

Belle was born at Highlandville, Iowa, on September 29, 1879, the daughter of
Johanes and Martha (Saervold) Johaneson Aakre. In October of 1908, Belle Akre of
Velva came to visit her sister, Hattie Ovre. When she visited in April of 1909,
Martin Wassenberg drove to Dogden (Butte) to meet her and gave her a ride to
Ovre's home. That summer on July 17, 1909, Belle filed on a homestead in Section
21 and 22 in Prophet's Township northeast of Mercer. Her land joined Martin's
homestead. Belle belonged to the Helping Hand Society in Mercer in 1910-1911.

Belle filed the final three year proof on her claim at McClusky on February 12,
1913. Her witnesses were Lawrence H. Harrum, Henry C. Westrook, Ols H. Kensmoe
and George Wiebe of McClusky. Her homestead patent number was 356306.

In the fall of 19ll, Martin was operated on for a rupture (hernia) by Dr.
Heinzeroth of Turtle Lake and Dr. Brown of McClusky. Apparently the operation
was a success, as he recovered. In 1916, Martin purchased the "Mercer Special",
a new manure spreader from James Rice, as did 18 other area farmers, according
to an advertisement in the Mercer Telegram.

Wassenbergs first child, Floyd Harold, was born April 17, 1913, and baptized
June 8, 1913. His sponsors were Krogh and Norman Ovre. He married Ada Mae Yeaman
on October 1, 1936, and they had one daughter, Sue Ann (Thompson). Floyd and Ada
celebrated their golden wedding anniversary in 1986. Ada died July 30, 1993, and
Floyd died June 26, 2003.

Jeanette "Arline" was born July 9, 1915. She married Francis E. Simpson, and
they had three children: James, Doreen, and Jerry Simpson. Arline died July 17,
1974.

Martin and Belle's twins, Thelma Harriet and Theodore Harry, were born May 5,
1917, and baptized May 11. Mrs. Krogh Ovre and Sevald Ovre were their sponsors.
Little Theodore Harry died May 14, 1917, and was buried the next day, May 15,
according to Mercer's Our Savior's Lutheran Church records.

Thelma married William Rogers on September 17, 1938, at Pocatello, Idaho, and
they had two children, Denny and Floyd William.

John Morris Wassenberg was delivered by Dr. Heinzeroth on May 16 (Sheridan Co.
records say May 29), 1919. He never married. He died June 1, 1946, at Big Piney,
Wyoming and was buried at Kemmerer, WY.

Milton Ervin (Sonny) was delivered by R.C. Rasmusson on January 22, 1923, when
Belle was 41, according to Prophet Township records. He married Louise
Charchalis, and they had one child, Pinky Sue. Milton died September 6, 1966, in
a car accident.

In an earlier interview with Joy Harrum Kline, she remembered Belle was red
headed and very pretty. She also said Belle was one of the nicest people she
knew. Both the Harrums and Wassengbergs moved into Mercer about 1923. Joy's
mother, Abby, was a midwife, and she delivered some of Belle's babies, including
the twins, Thelma and Theodore.

        Photo: (Front, from left) Donald 'Buzzy' Wassenberg, Martin Wassenberg,
        Patsy, a foster daughter of Arlene; (back) Ada Mae Yeaman Wassenberg,
        Thelma Rodgers, Milton 'Sonny' Wassenberg, Morris Wassenberg, Arlene
        'Pinky' Simpson, Floyd Wassenberg.

Times were hard and, in about 1923, Martin took a job in the oil fields of
Wyoming. Belle and the family remained in Mercer until about 1924, when they
joined him at Midwest, Wyoming.

Their youngest child, Donald (Buzz) Ray, was born May 11, 1927, at Midwest. He
married June Kothe December 23, 1954, and they had three children, Belle Lavon
(Stapleton), Jon Mori, and Donald Roy (Buzzy). Jon died in 1960, and Buzzy died
in 1986. Donald Sr. and June live at Big Piney, Wyoming.

Ingeborg "Belle" developed cancer and died February 19, 1932, at Calpet,
Wyoming, at the age of 52. She was buried at Kemmerer, Wyoming, in Lincoln
County.

Martin had a disability retirement from Texaco in 1939. He then moved to San
Francisco for his emphysema and worked there as a guard. He died December 17,
1959, and was buried at Kemmerer, Wyoming.
